title: @origingame/engine API v1
description:
The Origin Engine API. Game code declares components and systems, and reads the world through typed views over engine memory.
Every failure is a returned Result; desc objects may omit any field; nothing reads the wall clock inside a tick.

x-og-units.cssPx: CSS pixels of the play surface, origin at the top left
x-og-units.newton: newtons: the force that gives a kilogram one metre per second squared
x-og-units.newtonSecond: newton-seconds: an impulse, the momentum that changes a kilogram's velocity by one metre per second
x-og-units.perSecond: a rate per second: the fraction of a value that decays in one second
x-og-units.kgPerM3: kilograms per cubic metre (per square metre in the 2D profile)
x-og-units.evPerSecond: exposure stops (EV) per second of simulation time

x-og-modules.name: reflect
x-og-modules.doc:
Reflection: components and resources are declared once with their field layout and metadata, and registered by name.
The inspector, Tune, the probe, scene text and the wiki read this one schema. Each column factory below makes one field.
A field holds one value, or a list of at most a fixed number of one number type or handle: `list(u32(), 8)`, `list(Asset(), 4)` (the list factory below). A list is read as a frozen copy (`push` throws) and written whole (`chain.passes = [...chain.passes, h]`); one over its capacity is refused, never truncated. A few vectors are numbered fields (`p0` to `p7`, as og.CameraRail does); a list of things with fields of their own is an entity each, with its own component, looped over by a query (a ring of skid marks, the laps of a race); a long record (a lap's taped inputs) is text in `str` fields of at most 4,096 bytes each, chunked over entities. Keep none of it in module variables: they are not world state, so a snapshot, a replay and a hot reload lose them.
A handle (an og.load answer, a texture, a sound, a geometry, a material, an entity) is a 64-bit number: keep it in a field of its own kind (`Asset()`, `Texture()`, `Sound()`, `Font()`, `Style()`, `Geometry()`, `Material()`, `Entity()`: every handle type of the API has its factory, named as the type), never cast to another kind, in a component or a resource. A `u32` field refuses one (handles pass 2^32: `4294967298 is not a u32`); an `f64` holds the number but loses its type.

functions.name: defineComponent
functions.doc:
Declare a component: plain data stored per entity in engine memory, one column per field.
Registration is by name, so a hot reload re-registers the same component and migrates its fields by name.

params.name: name
params.doc: The component's unique name, PascalCase, as it appears in scenes and dumps.

params.name: fields
params.doc: The layout: field names to column factories, as `{ hp: f32(100) }`.

functions.returnsDoc: The token systems, queries and the world take.

functions.name: defineResource
functions.doc: Declare a resource: a reflected singleton, such as a tuning table. Its fields start at their defaults.
functions.returnsDoc: The token `world.resource` and system declarations take.

x-og-modules.name: world
x-og-modules.doc:
The world: an archetype ECS. Entities are generational handles; components are columns in engine memory.
Structural changes (spawn, despawn, insert, remove) invalidate typed views; the API refuses a stale view.

interfaces.name: World
interfaces.doc: The world a system, a command or a game callback is handed. Game code never holds a world beyond the call it was passed to.

members.name: tick
members.doc: Fixed steps taken since the world was created.

members.name: spawn
members.doc: Spawn an entity.
members.returnsDoc: The new entity, or why it was refused (a duplicate name, a dead parent).

members.name: despawn
members.doc: Despawn an entity and its descendants.
members.returnsDoc: Refused for a dead entity.

members.name: alive
members.doc: Whether an entity handle is live.

members.name: has
members.doc: Whether an entity has a component.

members.name: insert
members.doc: Add a component to an entity, or overwrite it when present. A structural change.

params.name: value
params.doc: Field values; omitted fields take their defaults.

members.returnsDoc: Refused for a dead entity or an unregistered component.

members.name: remove
members.doc: Remove a component from an entity. A structural change.
members.returnsDoc: Refused for a dead entity or a component it does not have.

members.name: get
members.doc: Copy one entity's component value. For bulk work use a system's typed views.

members.name: set
members.doc: Write some fields of one entity's component.
members.returnsDoc: Refused for a dead entity or a component it does not have.

members.name: resource
members.doc: A resource's live value: the same handle in a world every time, its fields typed reads and writes of the resource's packed record (no JSON, whatever its size). The record is fetched again only by the first read after another engine call or a system boundary, and writes reach the engine in one call before the next engine call and when the system or command returns, so two handles agree and a read after an engine call sees the engine's value (og-core §4). Inside a system, the resource must be among the system's reads or writes (writes to set a field): an undeclared one throws in a dev or release build, naming the system and the resource, and fails the tick; a publish build refuses it and logs it once per system in the engine log.
members.returnsDoc: Refused for an unregistered resource (or, in a publish build, one the running system did not declare).

members.name: find
members.doc: The entity with a name.
members.returnsDoc: Null when no live entity has the name.

members.name: nameOf
members.doc: An entity's name.
members.returnsDoc: Null for an unnamed or dead entity.

members.name: query
members.doc: A query over the current archetypes, for commands and callbacks (GameDesc.start, a command, a UI callback). Inside a system it is refused, by design: a system receives its one query (every component of its reads and writes) as its first argument; loop over another archetype in a system of its own.

members.name: events
members.doc: The events of one type emitted during the previous tick and this one, oldest first. Inside a system the event must be among its reads or writes (undeclared: thrown, or in a publish build refused and logged once).

members.name: emit
members.doc: Emit an event; readers see it this tick and the next. Inside a system the event must be among its writes (undeclared: thrown, or in a publish build refused and logged once).

members.name: instantiate
members.doc:
Spawn a loaded scene or glTF asset into the world: a root entity from the desc, then (for a scene) every scene entity under it with its components and names, or (for a glTF) a Model on the root.
Scene entity names must be free: a name already in use refuses the whole instantiation before anything spawns.

params.name: desc
params.doc: Name, parent and transform of the root entity.

members.returnsDoc: The root entity, or why it was refused (an asset still loading, a failed asset).

members.name: snapshot
members.doc: The whole world as text, to save a game's progress in the platform store: every entity with its components and names, every resource (og.Time's clock and the og.Rng streams too), the pending events and the modules' state (physics, animation, flipbooks, tweens, tilemap and terrain edits), each type with its schema hash, deflated and base64-encoded after `og-save:1:`. Every build has it, publish included, and the same world saves to the same text on both hosts. Save it with og.platform.saveSlot (`{ slot: "slot1", text, meta: { name, chimes } }`), which spreads it over as many store keys as it needs (a key holds 64 KiB) and writes the slot's manifest last, then og.platform.loadSlot and world.restore of the answer's `text` (examples/hollowbell, a 2D platformer of 189 entities on a 96 x 48 tile map, saves to about 25 KiB; examples/kestrel-stair, a 3D world of 93 entities with skinned characters, cloths and minds, to about 78 KB; a world of a few entities to about 11 KiB, most of it the table of every registered type). Inside a system it is the world in the middle of that tick, as that system sees it: what earlier systems wrote this tick is in it, a structural change the system queued (applied when it returns) is not, and it names the system, so a world restored from it completes that tick: its next step runs the systems after this one and the engine's (physics included) with the tick's own events, then ends the tick, and the world goes on tick for tick as the one that saved did (a replay from it matches; make the snapshot the system's last write of the tick, since what it does after the call is not in the save). Between ticks (GameDesc.start, a command, a UI callback) it is the world between two ticks. Physics carries its mesh, convex-hull and height-field colliders by their geometry's handle and scale, not their triangles (og.physics.setMesh). Asset and material handles in components are saved as their numbers: load what a saved entity uses in the same order on every launch (in GameDesc.start) before restoring.
members.returnsDoc: The save, or why not (the world could not be read).

members.name: restore
members.doc: Replace the world with a save that world.snapshot wrote: entities, components, names, resources, events and the modules' state, so the restored world hashes as the saved one did, on either host. The session stays: input (og.Input, og.Pointers, og.Gamepad), the player's bus volumes (og.Audio), the UI's focus and hover, and what lives outside the world (the platform's calls and clock, the language, the loaded assets, the command channel's scheduled steps, which keep their remaining delays though og.Time takes the saved tick, so an `og run --commands` script goes on to its last step or `quit` whether the save is of a later tick or an earlier one). Called in a system or a command it applies when the tick ends, after the last system; elsewhere (GameDesc.start, between ticks) at once. Either way the tick after it delivers og.WorldRestored, for the systems that reset what lives in the session. A save a system took mid-tick restores to that moment of its tick (og.Time reads its tick): the next step completes it (the systems after the saver, then the engine's), so the ticks after it are the saved run's. The meshes and height fields its colliders name must be loaded or registered first (a save naming one that is not is refused). A save holds only the world: progress kept in module variables is not in it, so keep it in components and resources.

params.name: desc
params.doc: Whether a type whose layout changed since the save is mapped field by field.

members.returnsDoc: Refused, with nothing changed, for text world.snapshot did not write, a save from a newer engine, or a type whose layout changed since the save (a field added, removed or retyped, an enum's variants): the reason names the type and the fields, and the fix (`{ migrate: true }`, or keeping a saved type's fields stable between releases).

interfaces.name: Query
interfaces.doc: A set of matched archetypes. Iterate archetypes, never entities one by one.

members.name: archetypes
members.doc: The matched archetypes this tick.

members.name: count
members.doc: The number of matched entities.

interfaces.name: ArchetypeView
interfaces.doc: One archetype's columns for this tick. Views are invalidated by structural changes; using a stale view throws with the tick and the system it belonged to.

members.name: count
members.doc: The number of entities in the archetype.

members.name: tick
members.doc: The tick this view belongs to.

members.name: entities
members.doc: The entities as (index, generation) pairs: entity i is at 2i and 2i + 1.

members.name: entity
members.doc: The handle of entity i.

members.name: has
members.doc: Whether the archetype carries a component.

members.name: column
members.doc:
The typed views of a component's fields: one typed array per field, `count * stride` long.
Writing requires the component among the system's writes; reading among its reads or writes.

x-og-modules.name: system
x-og-modules.doc:
Systems: functions the engine calls once per tick with their matched archetypes.
A system declares what it reads and writes; a write to an undeclared component is refused at registration with the field name.
Its query is every component of its reads and writes together: an entity matches only when it has all of them (and none of `without`). A component declared to read one entity with world.get (the player's car) therefore narrows the loop to entities that have it too, often to none, silently. world.query is refused inside a system, by design (a system reaches only what it declared, so its access is known before it runs): loop over each archetype in a system of its own, declaring only that archetype's components, and carry what crosses between systems in a resource.
Resources and events it reaches through the world must be declared too: in a dev or release build (og run, og test) an undeclared read or write throws with the system's name and the record and fails the tick; a publish build refuses it and logs it once per system in the engine log, and the game keeps running. og.Rng among the reads may fork (a fork reads the seed only and leaves the stream as it is); a draw moves the stream, so it needs og.Rng among the writes.

functions.name: defineSystem
functions.doc: Declare a system.

interfaces.name: System
interfaces.doc: A registered system.

members.name: name
members.doc: The system's unique name.

members.name: reads
members.doc: What it reads.

members.name: writes
members.doc: What it writes.

callbacks.name: SystemRun
callbacks.doc: A system's body. It is called once per tick; loop over `q.archetypes()`, then over rows.

params.name: q
params.doc: The archetypes matching the declared components.

params.name: time
params.doc: The Time resource for this tick.

params.name: world
params.doc: The world, for resources, events and structural changes.

x-og-modules.name: game
x-og-modules.doc: The game entry: what the bundle's default export declares.

functions.name: game
functions.doc: Declare the game. The bundle's default export is its result.

interfaces.name: Game
interfaces.doc: A declared game, the bundle's default export.

members.name: tick
members.doc: GameDesc.tick, or 60 when it is unset (the engine then runs at project.ogt's `tick` when the host passes the project, as og run and og build do).

members.name: systems
members.doc: The systems in declaration order.

callbacks.name: FactsFn
callbacks.doc: The game's own facts for the probe's state(): a small JSON object, computed from the world without changing it.

callbacks.name: StartFn
callbacks.doc: The game's setup: called once before the first tick, after GameDesc.scene has spawned. Spawn, insert, load and set resources here; systems then only read and write their views.

x-og-modules.name: transform
x-og-modules.doc: Transforms in the three.js vocabulary: position, quaternion and scale, composed into matrixWorld down the parent chain.

functions.name: compose
functions.doc: A matrix from position, rotation and scale, as three.js Matrix4.compose.

functions.name: decompose
functions.doc: Position, rotation and scale from a matrix, as three.js Matrix4.decompose.

functions.name: lookAt
functions.doc: The rotation that points -Z from an eye towards a target, as three.js Object3D.lookAt for cameras.

params.name: up
params.doc: The up direction; the zero vector means +Y.

functions.name: fromAxisAngle
functions.doc: A rotation about an axis, as three.js Quaternion.setFromAxisAngle.

x-og-modules.name: time
x-og-modules.doc: Simulation time. Game code never reads the wall clock; it reads Time.

functions.name: setScale
functions.doc: Set the global time scale (slow motion): physics, og.anim, flipbooks and tweens advance by dt * scale from the system after the call; systems may call it.
functions.returnsDoc: Refused outside 0..10.

functions.name: hitStop
functions.doc: Freeze scaled time for `ticks` ticks from now (this tick included): physics, og.anim, flipbooks and scaled tweens hold while input, the UI, unscaled tweens and camera shake keep moving. A longer hit stop in progress is never shortened. Typical values at 60 Hz: 2-3 ticks for a light hit, 4-6 medium, 8-12 heavy, 12-20 a finishing blow (paired with slow motion).

x-og-modules.name: rng
x-og-modules.doc:
Deterministic randomness. Every random draw comes from an Rng stream; the sequence for a seed is identical on every host and in the Web scaffold's rng.ts.
Inside a system: forking needs og.Rng among the reads (a fork is derived from the seed and the label, and leaves the main stream where it is); drawing from og.Rng itself (next, range, integer, chance) moves its state, so it needs og.Rng among the writes. A stream a fork returned is the system's own to draw from.

interfaces.name: RngStream
interfaces.doc: One generator stream, forked from the Rng resource for a subsystem that must not perturb the main sequence.

members.name: seed
members.doc: The stream's derived seed.

members.name: next
members.doc: Uniform in [0, 1).

members.name: range
members.doc: Uniform in [low, high).

members.name: integer
members.doc: A uniform integer in [low, high].

members.name: chance
members.doc: True with probability p.

members.name: fork
members.doc: A fresh stream on a seed derived from this stream's seed and a label.

params.name: label
params.doc: The subsystem's name; the same label always gives the same stream.

x-og-modules.name: input
x-og-modules.doc:
Input as the game sees it: the Input resource for polling, events for edges.
The shell collects pointer, keyboard and wheel input on the main thread; the probe and the command channel inject through the same path.
Several pointers at once (multi-touch) are og.Pointers; the first four gamepads, in the W3C standard mapping, are og.Gamepad. Both are world state, as og.Input is, so they replay.

consts.name: MAX_POINTERS
consts.doc: The most pointers og.Pointers tracks at once: ids 0 (the primary pointer) to 4.

consts.name: MAX_GAMEPADS
consts.doc: The most gamepads og.Gamepad reads: pads 0 to 3.

x-og-modules.name: camera
x-og-modules.doc:
The main camera, as a resource with three.js PerspectiveCamera and OrthographicCamera parameter names.
Camera controllers are components (OrbitCamera, FollowCamera, Follow2D) on the entity the camera orbits or follows; the systems that drive them ship in TypeScript as og.systems.cameras.

functions.name: shake
functions.doc: Add screen shake: trauma, clamped to 1, which og.Camera decays by traumaDecay. The shake grows with trauma squared, so 0.1-0.2 is a light hit, 0.25-0.4 a medium one, 0.5-0.8 an explosion or a boss slam; 1 is almost never right (nauseating). Visual only. Systems may call it; it takes effect at the engine's og.camera system this tick.

functions.name: punch
functions.doc: A zoom punch: the view narrows by `amount` (0.05 is a tap, 0.15 a slam) and springs back by Camera.punchDecay. Visual only.

params.name: amount
params.doc: The fraction to zoom in (negative zooms out), -0.9 to 4.

functions.name: kick
functions.doc: A directional nudge of the view (recoil, an impact from one side): offset by `distance` along `direction`, returning by Camera.kickDecay. Visual only.

params.name: direction
params.doc: The direction to push the view (normalised here; zero does nothing).

x-og-modules.name: render
x-og-modules.doc: What is drawn: meshes with materials. Draws are instanced by (geometry, material) automatically; there is no per-object draw call.

consts.name: PARTICLES_ARMED
consts.doc: ParticleSystem.startTick's default: never written. A looping emitter emits as if started at tick 0; a one-shot (`looping false`) emits nothing until its startTick is written, so a burst spawned in `start` waits for its first use. Write it back to re-arm a one-shot without firing it.

consts.name: MAX_LIGHTS
consts.doc: The most point and spot lights one frame draws, among those in view; past it the ones brightest at the camera are kept.

consts.name: MAX_CLUSTER_LIGHTS
consts.doc: The most point and spot lights that shade one screen cluster (a 1/16 by 1/9 tile of the view and one of 24 depth slices); past it the ones brightest at the camera are kept there.

consts.name: UI_LAYER
consts.doc: The UI's layer among screen sprites and screen text (SpriteDesc and TextDesc with screen): those at or below it draw under every og.ui element, those above it over every one, modals, toasts and the screen transition included (a HUD element made of sprites sitting on a UI panel: draw it only while its screen shows), in their layers' order either way.

consts.name: MAX_REFLECTION_PROBES
consts.doc: The most og.ReflectionProbe components one frame samples, nearest the camera first; the rest are skipped.

functions.name: ribbon
functions.doc: Draw a ribbon this frame. Systems and commands may call it; the list is cleared at every tick.

params.name: world
params.doc: The world whose renderer draws it.

functions.returnsDoc: Refused for a dead texture or fewer than two points.

functions.name: sprite
functions.doc: Draw a sprite this frame. Systems and commands may call it; the list is cleared at every tick, so submit it every tick the sprite should show.

params.name: world

params.name: desc
params.doc: The texture, placement, region and colour.

functions.returnsDoc: Refused for a dead texture.

functions.name: floatingText
functions.doc: Spawn a floating text (damage numbers, +coins, `blocked`). It lives `lifetime` seconds of scaled time on its own; systems and commands may call it.

params.name: world
params.doc: The world whose renderer draws it.

params.name: desc
params.doc: The text, the point and the style.

functions.returnsDoc: Refused for a dead font, or no font when the UI has none.

functions.name: measureText
functions.doc: The size text takes when og.render.text draws it, for centring, wrapping and layout.

params.name: world
params.doc: The world whose renderer owns the font.

functions.returnsDoc: Refused for a dead font.

functions.name: boxGeometry
functions.doc: Make a box geometry for og.Mesh. Physics can use it as a convex or triangle-mesh Collider.mesh too.

params.name: world
params.doc: The world whose renderer owns the geometry.

functions.name: planeGeometry
functions.doc: Make a plane geometry for og.Mesh. Physics can use it as a triangle-mesh Collider.mesh too.

params.name: world
params.doc: The world whose renderer owns the geometry.

functions.name: sphereGeometry
functions.doc: Make a sphere geometry for og.Mesh (give its body a sphere Collider, not this mesh).

params.name: world
params.doc: The world whose renderer owns the geometry.

params.name: desc
params.doc: Its radius, tessellation and texture repeat.

functions.name: standardMaterial
functions.doc: Create a standard material.

params.name: world
params.doc: The world whose renderer owns the material.

params.name: desc
params.doc: The parameters; omitted ones take three.js defaults.

functions.name: updateMaterial
functions.doc: Change some parameters of a standard material.

params.name: world
params.doc: The world whose renderer owns the material.

params.name: desc
params.doc: The parameters to change; omitted ones keep their values.

functions.returnsDoc: Refused for a dead material.

functions.name: shaderMaterial
functions.doc: Create a standard material that draws with a material shader's hooks (vertex_offset, surface_color, surface_normal, surface_emissive; the og-game skill's Material shaders section has their WGSL contract), its parameters at their defaults. The hooks apply to skinned meshes too, and shadows and the depth prepass (ambient occlusion, outlines, depth of field) see the mesh where vertex_offset moved it and cut where surface_color's alpha falls below alphaTest.

params.name: world
params.doc: The world whose renderer owns the material.

params.name: desc
params.doc: The base material; omitted parameters take three.js defaults. A dissolve sets alphaTest so that alpha below it is cut.

functions.returnsDoc: Refused for a shader not loaded in this world.

functions.name: setMaterialShader
functions.doc: Give an existing material a material shader, or take it away with null: a loaded model's material (GltfInfo.materials) draws its skinned or static meshes through the hooks, with the shader's parameters at their defaults. Every mesh drawn with that material changes.

params.name: world
params.doc: The world whose renderer owns the material.

params.name: material
params.doc: The material, from og.render.standardMaterial, og.render.shaderMaterial or a loaded glTF.

params.name: shader
params.doc: The shader, or null to draw the material plain again.

functions.returnsDoc: Refused for a dead material or a shader not loaded in this world.

functions.name: setShaderParam
functions.doc: Set a parameter of a shader material, by the name its shader declares: a number for float, two to four for vec2, vec3, vec4 and color.

params.name: world
params.doc: The world whose renderer owns the material.

params.name: material
params.doc: A material made by og.render.shaderMaterial or given a shader by og.render.setMaterialShader.

functions.returnsDoc: Refused for a material without a shader or a parameter its shader does not declare.

functions.name: applyLook
functions.doc: Apply a look, in GameDesc.start (or name it in GameDesc.look) or at any tick for a level's mood, a flashback or a photo mode: every resource the look names is replaced whole (the fields it sets take its values, the rest their defaults; PostEffects.flash and PostEffects.shakeTrauma, which game code animates, keep theirs), and the UI is configured with its style, keeping the rest of the last UiDesc. Resources it does not name are left as they are. Inside a system, the system must declare those resources among its writes. A look that switches the stylisation (a Stylise pass on or off, the pixel grid, retro 3D, the material style) starts TAA's history over, as a camera cut does, so its first frame holds no ghost of the old look.
functions.returnsDoc: Refused for a look not loaded in this world, one in a streaming group that is not resident (the reason names it), or a resource the system did not declare.

functions.name: applyQuality
functions.doc:
Apply a graphics preset: write its row of RenderSettings' quality fields (the rest of RenderSettings keeps its values) and record it in RenderSettings.quality. The renderer reads those fields and nothing else, so what the probe and dump_world show of RenderSettings is what the next frame draws. The settings screen calls it when the player picks a preset (SettingsDesc.world); a game applies a saved preset itself at start. Inside a system, the system must declare RenderSettings among its writes. The rows:
| Field | low | medium | high |
|---|---|---|---|
| rectShadows | false | true | true |
| shadowedLights | 2 | 8 | 8 |
| shadowMapScale | 0.5 | 1 | 2 |
| volumetricFog | false | true | true |
| softParticles | false | true | true |
| screenSpaceReflections | false | true | true |
| ambientOcclusion | false | true | true |
| msaaSamples | 1 | 4 | 4 |
Medium is every field's default, the frame drawn before any preset.
functions.returnsDoc: Refused for a world that is not alive, or inside a system that did not declare RenderSettings among its writes.

functions.name: look
functions.doc: The look last applied (by og.render.applyLook or GameDesc.look), as og.load.lookInfo describes it; null before any.

functions.name: capabilities
functions.doc: The renderer's tier and limits on this device.

params.name: world
params.doc: The world whose renderer is asked.

functions.name: text
functions.doc: Draw text this frame. Systems and commands may call it; the list is cleared at every tick, so submit it every tick the text should show. Multi-page fonts are drawn page by page with one layout.

params.name: world
params.doc: The world whose renderer draws it.

params.name: desc
params.doc: The font, text, placement and colour.

functions.returnsDoc: Refused for a dead font.

functions.name: bufferGeometry
functions.doc: Make a geometry from attribute arrays (three.js BufferGeometry): procedural levels, 2D polygons, meshes a tool made. It draws as any geometry (og.Mesh), its BVH is built for og.render.raycast, and (desc.physics) it is a Collider.mesh at once.

params.name: world
params.doc: The world whose renderer owns the geometry.

functions.returnsDoc: Refused for an attribute whose length does not fit the vertex count, an index past the vertices, or a number that is not finite (the reason names the attribute).

functions.name: updateGeometry
functions.doc: Rewrite a dynamic geometry's attributes in place (desc as og.render.bufferGeometry's, every attribute given again; `dynamic` and `physics` keep their values from when it was made). The same vertex and index counts rewrite its GPU buffers in place; other counts reallocate them, which costs more and is fine now and then. Its BVH is rebuilt, and its physics mesh re-registered (colliders made from it are rebuilt at the next step). Every og.Mesh, og.Lines and og.Points showing it changes.

params.name: world
params.doc: The world whose renderer owns the geometry.

params.name: geometry
params.doc: A geometry og.render.bufferGeometry made with dynamic true.

functions.returnsDoc: Refused for a dead or static geometry, or attributes og.render.bufferGeometry refuses.

functions.name: geometryInfo
functions.doc: A geometry's counts and bounds.

params.name: world
params.doc: The world whose renderer owns the geometry.

params.name: geometry
params.doc: Any geometry: made, a primitive or a loaded glTF's.

functions.returnsDoc: Refused for a dead geometry.

functions.name: cylinderGeometry
functions.doc: Make a cylinder geometry for og.Mesh (give its body a cylinder-like Collider: a capsule, a convex Collider.mesh of it, or the geometry itself).

params.name: world
params.doc: The world whose renderer owns the geometry.

functions.name: coneGeometry
functions.doc: Make a cone geometry for og.Mesh. Physics can use it as a convex Collider.mesh.

params.name: world
params.doc: The world whose renderer owns the geometry.

functions.name: capsuleGeometry
functions.doc: Make a capsule geometry for og.Mesh (its body's Collider is a capsule of the same radius and half the height).

params.name: world
params.doc: The world whose renderer owns the geometry.

functions.name: torusGeometry
functions.doc: Make a torus geometry for og.Mesh. Physics can use it as a triangle-mesh Collider.mesh.

params.name: world
params.doc: The world whose renderer owns the geometry.

functions.name: ringGeometry
functions.doc: Make a ring geometry for og.Mesh (one-sided: give it a double-sided material to see it from behind).

params.name: world
params.doc: The world whose renderer owns the geometry.

functions.name: circleGeometry
functions.doc: Make a circle geometry for og.Mesh (one-sided, as ringGeometry).

params.name: world
params.doc: The world whose renderer owns the geometry.

functions.name: tubeGeometry
functions.doc: Make a tube along a curve through points for og.Mesh: pipes, cables, rails, a path shown as a ribbon of geometry. Physics can use it as a triangle-mesh Collider.mesh.

params.name: world
params.doc: The world whose renderer owns the geometry.

functions.returnsDoc: Refused for fewer than two points or a point that is not finite (without a path), or a path that is not alive.

functions.name: shapeGeometry
functions.doc: Make a flat shape for og.Mesh (one-sided, as circleGeometry): an og.Shape with holes, or a points array. Physics can use it as a triangle-mesh Collider.mesh.

params.name: world

functions.name: extrudeGeometry
functions.doc: Make an extruded solid for og.Mesh: a three.js extrusion is a paste (`og.render.extrudeGeometry(world, { shapes: shape, depth: 0.2, bevelEnabled: true })`). Gears, signs, keys, logos, cookie cutters; along a path, a rail or a moulding.

params.name: world

params.name: desc

functions.name: latheGeometry

functions.name: polyhedronGeometry

params.doc: The world whose renderer owns the geometry.

functions.name: csgGeometry

params.name: world

functions.doc: Draw lines this frame. Systems and commands may call it; the list is cleared at every tick, so submit them every tick they should show (og.Lines keeps a static set).

params.name: world

functions.returnsDoc: Refused for fewer than two points or a colours list whose length is not the points'.

functions.name: raycast
functions.doc: Every drawn triangle a ray crosses, nearest first, as three.js Raycaster.intersectObjects: what is drawn, not the colliders (og.physics.raycast answers those). It tests og.Mesh and og.Model entities at their world transforms through a BVH per geometry (built when the geometry is made, loaded or updated), both faces of each triangle, skinned models in their bind pose. Read the world as of the call; inside a system, its transforms as earlier systems left them.

params.name: ray
params.doc: The ray; its direction need not be normalised and must not be zero.

functions.returnsDoc: Refused for a zero or non-finite direction.

functions.name: renderTarget
functions.doc: Make a render target: a texture an og.CameraView or og.Mirror draws into, its colour (RenderTargetInfo.texture) usable by any map, sprite or UI image, as three.js WebGLRenderTarget and its texture. Targets are drawn before the frame, so a material shows this frame's image; one a camera draws while it sees itself (a monitor in the room it films) shows the frame before.

params.name: world
params.doc: The world whose renderer owns it.

functions.returnsDoc: Refused for a side past RenderCapabilities.maxRenderTargetSize.

functions.name: setPostParam
functions.doc: Set a parameter of a custom post pass, by the name its asset declares: a number for float, two to four for vec2, vec3, vec4 and color. Every frame it runs in reads it.

params.name: world
params.doc: The world whose renderer owns the pass.

functions.returnsDoc: Refused for a pass not loaded in this world or a parameter it does not declare.

functions.name: postErrors
functions.doc: The custom post passes PostEffects.custom names that failed to compile on this device, each skipped (the frame draws as without it). The cook validates every pass for each back end, so this is a device's own refusal.

functions.name: bakedLighting
functions.doc: The baked lighting of every scene instantiated in the world, in instantiation order: whether it is drawn, and why not. A scene with no static model and no LightVolume is not listed.

x-og-modules.name: shapes
x-og-modules.doc:
Two-dimensional outlines in three.js's words: og.Shape and og.Path2 are three.js's Shape and Path, built by the same calls (moveTo, lineTo, quadraticCurveTo, bezierCurveTo, splineThru, arc, absarc, ellipse, absellipse, closePath) and flattened to points by getPoints, so a three.js outline is a paste. og.render.shapeGeometry, extrudeGeometry and sweepGeometry take them; only their points cross to the engine.
They are TypeScript values, not world state: make them in start or a command and let the geometry made from them be what the world keeps. Points come from basic arithmetic (no Math.sin), so they are the same on every host.
A prop of these parts belongs in an asset: an `.ogt` of `type model` names each part's geometry by its og.render call (`extrudeGeometry { shape { absarc 0 0 1 0 6.283185307179586 false } depth 0.2 }`), its shapes as og.Shape's calls one a line with `hole { }` blocks, places parts as mergeGeometries does (`position`, `quaternion`, `scale`, `mirror`, or several `at { }` blocks: one mesh drawn instanced), gives each a `material` and hangs it from a named `pivot` (a node). og cook builds it into the model blob a glTF cooks to (levels of detail, raycast BVH, nodes), refuses it past project.ogt's triangle and vertex budgets, and og dev re-cooks it on an edit; og.load.gltf and a scene's `model` line take it as any model. The og-game skill §18 has a whole example.

values.name: Path2
values.doc: three.js's Path (named Path2 beside og.path's 3D paths): `new og.Path2().moveTo(0, 0).lineTo(1, 0)`.

values.name: Shape
values.doc: three.js's Shape: `const s = new og.Shape(); s.moveTo(0, 0).lineTo(1, 0).lineTo(0, 1); s.holes.push(hole)`.

interfaces.name: PathList
interfaces.doc: A shape's holes, as three.js Shape.holes: an array; push a path to add a hole.

members.name: length
members.doc: How many holes.

members.name: push
members.doc: Add a hole (Array.push).

interfaces.name: Path2
interfaces.doc: An outline of curves, as three.js Path: each call adds a curve from the current point (moveTo only moves it). Every method but getPoints returns the path, so calls chain.

members.name: moveTo
members.doc: Move the current point without drawing, as three.js Path.moveTo.

members.name: lineTo
members.doc: A straight line to (x, y), as three.js Path.lineTo.

members.name: quadraticCurveTo
members.doc: A quadratic Bézier curve through one control point to (x, y), as three.js Path.quadraticCurveTo.

members.name: bezierCurveTo
members.doc: A cubic Bézier curve through two control points to (x, y), as three.js Path.bezierCurveTo.

members.name: splineThru
members.doc: A Catmull-Rom spline from the current point through the points, as three.js Path.splineThru (a SplineCurve).

params.name: points
params.doc: The points it passes through, in order.

members.name: arc
members.doc: A circular arc centred at (x, y) from the current point, as three.js Path.arc.

params.name: x
params.doc: The centre's x, from the current point.

params.name: y
params.doc: The centre's y, from the current point.

members.name: absarc
members.doc: A circular arc centred at (x, y), as three.js Path.absarc: a line joins it to the current point when they differ.

members.name: ellipse
members.doc: An elliptic arc centred at (x, y) from the current point, as three.js Path.ellipse.

params.name: x
params.doc: The centre's x, from the current point.

params.name: y
params.doc: The centre's y, from the current point.

params.name: rotation
params.doc: The ellipse's turn round its centre.

members.name: absellipse
members.doc: An elliptic arc centred at (x, y), as three.js Path.absellipse.

params.name: rotation
params.doc: The ellipse's turn round its centre.

members.name: setFromPoints
members.doc: Start at the first point and draw lines through the rest, as three.js Path.setFromPoints.

members.name: closePath
members.doc: A line back to the first point when the outline does not end there, as three.js CurvePath.closePath.

members.name: getPoints
members.doc: The outline as points, as three.js CurvePath.getPoints: each curve divided into `divisions` (an ellipse twice as many, a spline as many per point, a line one), repeated points dropped.

interfaces.name: Shape
interfaces.doc: An outline with holes, as three.js Shape.

members.name: holes
members.doc: The holes: `shape.holes.push(hole)`.

members.name: extractPoints
members.doc: The outline's and the holes' points, as three.js Shape.extractPoints.

interfaces.name: Path2Class
interfaces.doc: og.Path2: `new og.Path2(points?)`.

members.name: new
members.doc: A path, through the points when given (setFromPoints).

interfaces.name: ShapeClass
interfaces.doc: og.Shape: `new og.Shape(points?)`.

members.name: new
members.doc: A shape, through the points when given (setFromPoints).

x-og-modules.name: load
x-og-modules.doc:
Asset loading from cooked output: `og cook` turns assets/ into cooked/ (.ogb blobs and the manifest cooked/.cook.ogt), and the runtime reads only cooked/.
Paths are asset ids: the path under assets/ (`models/ship.glb`, `scenes/main.ogt`); an `assets/` prefix is accepted. Every blob is checked against the manifest's type, schema version and cook stamp.
The game's bundle (`cooked`) is opened before the first tick and GameDesc.scene is spawned then. Loads from an open bundle complete at once on both hosts (the web host fetches the bundle's files before the engine starts); only og.load.bundle of another bundle can be pending, and it completes at a tick boundary.

functions.name: bundle
functions.doc: Open another cooked bundle (the game's own `cooked` is open before the first tick). Its loads read through it once it is ready.

params.name: world
params.doc: The world that owns the asset.

params.name: path
params.doc: The cooked directory, relative to the project (or the page), such as `dlc/cooked`.

functions.returnsDoc: The bundle's handle: pending until its manifest is read, then ready or failed.

functions.name: bundleInfo
functions.doc: What an open bundle holds.

params.name: world
params.doc: The world that owns the asset.

params.name: asset
params.doc: A bundle handle; the game's own bundle is og.load.bundle's first answer, also given by `defaultBundle`.

functions.returnsDoc: Refused for a pending, failed or non-bundle asset.

functions.name: defaultBundle
functions.doc: The game's own bundle, opened before the first tick from `cooked/`.

params.name: world
params.doc: The world that owns the asset.

functions.returnsDoc: Refused when cooked/ was missing or unreadable (run og cook); the reason names the path.

functions.name: gltf
functions.doc:
Load a cooked glTF (.gltf or .glb), as three.js GLTFLoader.load: its meshes, materials and textures join the renderer once.
A MagicaVoxel `.vox` cooks to a glTF and loads here too: greedy-meshed, flat-shaded, its palette as vertex colours, z-up turned y-up, each model about its centre (MagicaVoxel's pivot, with a scene graph or without). Its import settings (`models/hut.vox.ogt`, `type import`) size and place it: `model { voxScale 0.1 voxOrigin bottom }` is 0.1 m a voxel (default 1) and the lowest voxel on y = 0 (default `center`, the editor's origin). A `.vox` with frames (MagicaVoxel's animation) cooks to clips that swap the frames' models, played by og.AnimationPlayer as any skinned clip: `voxFps 8` (default 10) and `voxClip walk 0 3` (frames 0 to 3; default one clip `frames` of the file's playback range, else of every frame); a node's `_loop` repeats its keys as the editor plays them.

params.name: world
params.doc: The world that owns the asset.

functions.returnsDoc: The handle, or why it was refused (an uncooked path, a cook stamp mismatch, no open bundle).

functions.name: scene
functions.doc: Load a cooked scene (.ogt). world.instantiate spawns its entities: depth first, parents before children, each component table matched to a registered component by its reflected name (`Transform` is og.Transform) and migrated field by field; a field the scene lacks keeps its default, one the component lacks is dropped with a warning.

params.name: world
params.doc: The world that owns the asset.

params.name: path
params.doc: The scene's asset id, such as `scenes/main.ogt`.

functions.name: font
functions.doc: Load a cooked MSDF font for og.render.text, or an icon set (an `.ogt` of `type icons`: SVG icons cooked into a distance-field atlas like a font) for UiDesc.icons.font.

params.name: world
params.doc: The world that owns the font.

params.name: path
params.doc: The font's asset id, such as `fonts/NotoSansSC-Regular-subset.ttf`.

functions.name: fontInfo
functions.doc: A loaded font's metrics.

params.name: world
params.doc: The world that owns the font.

functions.returnsDoc: Refused for a dead font.

functions.name: sound
functions.doc:
Load a cooked sound for the audio module.
A long sound (music, ambience) can be cooked in chunks of whole QOA frames: `sound { stream true chunk 4 }` in its `.wav.ogt` import settings (chunk in seconds, 1 to 60, default 4), and every sound whose QOA file would pass 1 MiB unless `stream false`. Its first chunk loads with it and the others follow the playheads (SoundInfo.chunks), so music is never resident whole; it plays sample for sample as the whole file would, loops and crossfades included. A sound cooked in chunks cannot join a streaming group.

params.name: world
params.doc: The world that owns the sound.

params.name: path
params.doc: The sound's asset id, such as `audio/blip.wav`.

functions.name: lut
functions.doc: A colour lookup table for PostEffects.lut, from a cooked `.cube` file (Adobe/Resolve 3D LUT; other sizes are resampled to 32). Loaded once per path. One in a streaming group's pack loads once its group is resident (refused before, naming the group); while the group is unloaded PostEffects.lut grades nothing with it, and it comes back under the same handle.

params.name: world
params.doc: The world whose renderer owns it.

functions.returnsDoc: Refused for a path not in the bundle (the reason says to run og cook).

functions.name: environment
functions.doc: A prefiltered environment map for Environment.map, from a cooked `.ogt` of `type environment`: `source` an equirectangular Radiance `.hdr` or OpenEXR `.exr` (the centre column faces +X, as three.js maps it) or a KTX2 cube map (six square faces +X -X +Y -Y +Z -Z with rows from the top; RGBA16F, RGB9E5, BC6H and the other HDR formats, decoded at cook time), or `faces` with six `.hdr`/`.exr` images in that order; `size` level 0's face size (a power of two, 16 to 2048, default 128), `intensity`, `rotation` (degrees about +Y) and `samples`. The cook prefilters it into a cube of five GGX levels (roughness 0 to 1) in RGB9E5 and the diffuse irradiance as nine harmonics, so loading only uploads it; `prefiltered true` takes a KTX2 cube's own mip chain as those levels instead (one already GGX-prefiltered by cmgen, IBLBaker or the glTF IBL sampler: level k of L at roughness k / (L - 1)), at the file's own size, without filtering it again. On the web it is fetched with the bundle like any blob; one in a streaming group's pack loads when its group is resident, and the sky lights the scene until then. Loaded once per path.

params.name: world
params.doc: The world whose renderer owns it.

functions.returnsDoc: Refused for a path not in the bundle (the reason says to run og cook) or not an environment map.

functions.name: emitter
functions.doc: A particle emitter asset for ParticleSystem.emitter, from a cooked `.ogt` of `type particles` (the og-game skill's Effects section gives every line with its default and an example; og-cook's fx module parses it): shape, rate and bursts, lifetime, speed, size and colour over life, gravity, drag, noise, a texture and sprite sheet, blending, collision, billboard or 2D sprite rendering. A sprite-mode emitter may draw from a texture array instead (`array "<id>" [<layers>] [off | life <cycles> | fps <n> | random]`: each particle shows a layer by its age, at a rate, or one at random for its life; one draw per array whatever the layers; `round true` fades each particle to the soft dot's round edge). The textures and the array it names are loaded with it; while the array's streaming group is not resident its systems draw nothing. Loaded once per path.

params.name: world
params.doc: The world whose renderer owns it.

functions.returnsDoc: Refused for a path not in the bundle, or a texture or texture array it cannot load.

functions.name: shader
functions.doc: A material shader for og.render.shaderMaterial, from a cooked `.ogt` of `type shader` (its WGSL compiled by the cook for every back end). `mode hooks` (the default) defines hooks of the lit shader; `mode full lit` or `mode full unlit` defines `fn vertex(v: VertexInput, model: mat4x4<f32>, p: Params) -> VertexOutput` and `fn fragment(f: FragmentInput, p: Params) -> SurfaceOutput` over the binding contract (camera(), the model with its skin, Params, tex0 to tex7 for the material's eight texture slots; the og-game skill's Full custom shaders section), lit by the frame's lights or drawn as returned, the prepass and every shadow pass drawn through the same entries. Loaded once per path.

params.name: world
params.doc: The world whose renderer owns it.

functions.returnsDoc: Refused for a path not in the bundle or not a shader.

functions.name: post
functions.doc: A custom post pass for PostEffects.custom, from a cooked `.ogt` of `type post`: `code` or `source` (a `.wgsl` beside it) defining `fn post(f: PostInput, p: Params) -> vec4<f32>` and `param <name> float|vec2|vec3|vec4|color <default...>` lines (at most eight). The function reads previous(uv), scene_color(uv), depth(uv), normal(uv) and f.uv, f.pixel, f.size, f.time, and returns linear HDR colour (the og-game skill's Custom post passes section has the contract). The cook compiles it for every back end. Loaded once per path.

params.name: world
params.doc: The world whose renderer owns it.

functions.returnsDoc: Refused for a path not in the bundle or not a post pass.

functions.name: texture
functions.doc:
Load a cooked texture for og.render.sprite and og.ui.image, as three.js TextureLoader.load.
Sources are PNG, JPEG or KTX2 files under assets/ (`texture { kind color|normal|linear|pixel }` in `<file>.ogt`). A KTX2's `KTXorientation` and `KTXswizzle` are honoured: one that is not `rd` and `rgba` is decoded, flipped to rows top to bottom and swizzled, and cooked again; one that is (Basis ETC1S or UASTC, or RGBA8, of a colour or linear kind) is taken as it is.

params.name: world
params.doc: The world whose renderer owns the texture.

params.name: path
params.doc: The texture's asset id, such as `textures/stone.png`.

functions.name: textureArray
functions.doc:
Load a cooked texture array (an `.ogt` of `type texture-array`: `kind color|normal|linear|pixel` and one `layer "<file>"` per layer, 1 to 256 images of one size, each path beside the file or under assets/) and upload it as one 2D-array texture, its layers in file order, each in the encoding the device takes for its kind. Each layer is also a texture of its own, `<path>#layer<n>`, for og.load.texture. Loading the same path again answers the same array.
SpriteDesc.array (world and screen sprites), og.Sprite.array and 2D particle emitters (an emitter's `array` line) draw from its layers, one draw per array whatever layer each shows, with glow and the additive blend; an `array true` flipbook sheet cooks its frames into one (materials and terrain layers do not sample arrays yet). TextureArrayInfo and the frame's texture bytes report it. One in a streaming group's pack loads once its group is resident (refused before, naming the group); when the group unloads the renderer lets it go, og.render.sprite of it is refused and og.Sprite and particles of it draw nothing until the group is resident again, when it comes back under the same handle.

params.name: world
params.doc: The world whose renderer owns the array.

params.name: path
params.doc: The array's asset id, such as `tiles/ground.ogt`.

functions.returnsDoc: Refused for a path not in the bundle (run og cook), not a texture array, or layers that do not agree.

functions.name: style
functions.doc: Load a cooked UI style (an `.ogt` of `type style`: every palette role, the radii, type ramp, durations, and its art: the atlas and its nine-slice frames, ornaments, fonts, icons, motion and sounds; the grammar is og-ui's `parse_style`) for UiDesc.style. Its atlas, fonts, icons and sounds are loaded with it. Loaded once per path. A built-in style a look names is in the bundle as `@styles/<name>/style.ogt`.

params.name: world
params.doc: The world whose UI uses it.

params.name: path
params.doc: The asset id, such as `styles/pixel/style.ogt` or `@styles/pixel/style.ogt`.

functions.returnsDoc: Refused for a path not in the bundle, a style that does not parse (the reason names the line) or an asset it names that cannot load.

functions.name: look
functions.doc: Load a look: an `.ogt` of `type look` binding a frame's art direction as data. Its top-level `name`, `extends` (a built-in preset's slug, such as `anime-cel-3d`, or another look's asset id: the game's own `assets/looks/<slug>.ogt` wins over the built-in preset of that slug), `ui` (a UI style: a built-in style's slug, such as `cartoon`, or the game's own style file's asset id) and `antialias`, then one block per resource it sets (RenderSettings, PostEffects, Stylise, MaterialStyle, Fog, Sky, Environment) with that resource's fields by name, an asset id where a field is a handle (`lut "luts/warm.cube"`, `palette "palettes/dusk.hex"`). The cook validates every field against the resources' reflected schema and flattens `extends`, so the blob is the whole look. The textures, LUTs, palettes, environment map and UI style it names are loaded with it. Loaded once per path.

params.name: world
params.doc: The world whose renderer owns it.

functions.returnsDoc: Refused for a path not in the bundle (the reason says to run og cook) or an asset it names that cannot load.

functions.name: lookInfo
functions.doc: What a loaded look holds and sets.

params.name: world
params.doc: The world that owns the look.

functions.returnsDoc: Refused for a look not loaded in this world.

functions.name: palette
functions.doc: A colour palette for Stylise.palette, from a cooked `.hex` (one RRGGBB per line, as palette sites publish them) or GIMP `.gpl` file: up to 256 sRGB colours, in file order. Loaded once per path. One in a streaming group's pack loads once its group is resident; while the group is unloaded Stylise.palette quantises to no palette, and the palette comes back under the same handle.

params.name: world
params.doc: The world whose renderer owns it.

functions.returnsDoc: Refused for a path not in the bundle (the reason says to run og cook).

functions.name: soundInfo
functions.doc: A loaded sound's format and length.

params.name: world
params.doc: The world that owns the sound.

functions.returnsDoc: Refused for a dead sound.

functions.name: status
functions.doc: Where a load is.

params.name: world
params.doc: The world that owns the asset.

functions.name: error
functions.doc: Why a load failed.

params.name: world
params.doc: The world that owns the asset.

functions.returnsDoc: The reason, naming the fix; null unless the load failed.

functions.name: gltfInfo
functions.doc: What a ready glTF holds.

params.name: world
params.doc: The world that owns the asset.

functions.returnsDoc: Refused for a pending, failed or non-glTF asset.

functions.name: animation
functions.doc:
Load a cooked glTF's animation (its `<model>#anim` blob: the rig, the clips, the skin and morph streams) and register its skeleton and clips with og.anim. Loading the same model again answers the same handles.
Clips are cooked as f32 samples, or with `animation { compress true tolerance 0.0001 }` in the model's import settings as quantised keys (rotations as 48-bit smallest-three, translations, scales and weights as 16 bits over each channel's range) with every frame dropped that interpolation rebuilds within the tolerance; either way every frame is rebuilt here and the clip plays as f32. Morph targets are cooked sparse (the vertices each moves).

params.name: world
params.doc: The world whose animation owns the assets.

params.name: path
params.doc: The model's asset id, such as `models/walker.glb` (a `#anim` suffix is accepted).

functions.returnsDoc: Refused for an uncooked path, a model the cook wrote no `#anim` blob for (no skins, clips or morph targets), a cook stamp mismatch or an invalid rig.

functions.name: rig
functions.doc: Load a cooked humanoid map (an `.ogt` of `type rig`: a naming scheme and bones named outright) for og.anim.retarget and og.anim.humanoid. Loading the same path again answers the same handle.

params.name: world
params.doc: The world whose animation uses it.

params.name: path
params.doc: The rig's asset id, such as `rigs/strider.ogt`.

functions.returnsDoc: Refused for a path not in the bundle (run og cook) or a cook stamp mismatch.

functions.name: flipbook
functions.doc: Load a cooked flipbook sheet (an `.ogt` of `type flipbook`, with its Aseprite or TexturePacker atlas resolved by the cook) and its texture, and register it with og.flipbook. A sheet with `array true` is cooked into a texture array instead (its frames, one size, cut out of the texture as layers): its sprites draw frame n as layer n, every sprite of the sheet one draw whichever frame each shows, and FlipbookInfo.array names the array. A sheet in a streaming group (its array and layers with it) loads once its group is resident (refused naming the group before), and its sprites draw nothing while the group is away. Loading the same path again answers the same handles.

params.name: world
params.doc: The world whose animation and renderer own it.

params.name: path
params.doc: The sheet's asset id, such as `sprites/hero.ogt`.

functions.returnsDoc: Refused for a path not in the bundle (run og cook) or a texture it cannot load.

functions.name: tilemap
functions.doc: Load a cooked map (a tilemap `.ogt`, a Tiled `.tmj` or an LDtk `.ldtk`), its tilesets and their textures. Loading the same path again answers the same handles.

params.name: world
params.doc: The world whose renderer and tilemaps own it.

params.name: path
params.doc: The map's asset id, such as `maps/room.tmj`.

functions.returnsDoc: Refused for a path not in the bundle, a missing tileset or texture, or a terrain its tileset lacks.

functions.name: video
functions.doc: Load cooked footage (an `.ogt` of `type video`: `source` an .mp4, .webm or .mov beside it or under assets/, `fps`, `maxSeconds`, `size W H`, `kind color|pixel`, `audio`), which og cook turns with ffmpeg into a texture array of its frames and its sound track. Uploads the frames as one 2D-array texture and makes the video's Texture (VideoInfo.texture), which shows the frame its og.VideoPlayer is at: a material map, an og.Sprite or a UI image draws it like any texture. Load it in GameDesc.start (every process of an og render --jobs run loads it the same way, so its handles agree). Loading the same path again answers the same handles.

params.name: world
params.doc: The world whose renderer and audio own it.

params.name: path
params.doc: The video's asset id: the `.ogt`, such as `clips/intro.ogt`.

functions.returnsDoc: Refused for a path not in the bundle (run og cook: a video needs ffmpeg there, og doctor) or not a video.

functions.name: videoInfo
functions.doc: A loaded video's size, frames, rate, length, texture and sound.
functions.returnsDoc: Refused for a handle og.load.video did not answer.

functions.name: timeline
functions.doc: Load a timeline: an `.ogt` of `type timeline` (the og.timeline module's file: duration, paths and tracks of keys), cooked with its caption files imported. Loaded once per path; play it with an og.Timeline whose asset is the handle, or `timeline:play:<name>` on the command channel.

params.name: path
params.doc: The timeline's asset id, such as `timelines/intro.ogt`.

functions.returnsDoc: Refused for a path not in the bundle (run og cook) or a file that is not a timeline.

functions.name: rig2d
functions.doc: Load a cooked 2D rig (an `.ogt` of `type rig2d`, written by hand or imported by the cook from DragonBones JSON) and its texture, and register it with og.skeleton2d. Loading the same path again answers the same handles.

params.name: world
params.doc: The world whose animation and renderer own it.

params.name: path
params.doc: The rig's asset id, such as `rigs/hero.ogt`.

functions.returnsDoc: Refused for a path not in the bundle (run og cook) or a texture it cannot load.

x-og-modules.name: physics
x-og-modules.doc:
Rigid bodies over rapier (rapier3d in the 3D profile, rapier2d in 2D, both with enhanced determinism): game code owns the components, the engine's og.physics system steps them after the game's systems and writes the dynamic bodies back.
The profile is the project's (`profile "2d"` or `"3d"` in project.ogt). In 2D, bodies move in the xy plane and rotate about z; a transform keeps its z. A collider without a RigidBody is static at its transform.
The rapier world persists between ticks and is world state: snapshots, restore and the world hash cover the whole simulation. Events sent in tick N are read in tick N + 1.

consts.name: BODY_DYNAMIC
consts.doc: RigidBody.kind: moved by the solver; its Transform and Velocity are written back every tick.

consts.name: BODY_STATIC
consts.doc: RigidBody.kind: never moves; collides with dynamic bodies.

consts.name: BODY_KINEMATIC
consts.doc: RigidBody.kind: not moved by the solver. With an og.Velocity the step moves it by it each tick and writes its Transform back (a lift, a conveyor, a turning gear); a Transform game code writes moves it there first (a teleport). Without one it stays where its Transform puts it. Either way it pushes dynamic bodies and carries the controllers standing on it.

consts.name: LOCK_TRANSLATION_X
consts.doc: RigidBody.lock bit: no translation along x.

consts.name: LOCK_TRANSLATION_Y
consts.doc: RigidBody.lock bit: no translation along y.

consts.name: LOCK_TRANSLATION_Z
consts.doc: RigidBody.lock bit: no translation along z.

consts.name: LOCK_ROTATION_X
consts.doc: RigidBody.lock bit: no rotation about x.

consts.name: LOCK_ROTATION_Y
consts.doc: RigidBody.lock bit: no rotation about y.

consts.name: LOCK_ROTATION_Z
consts.doc: RigidBody.lock bit: no rotation about z (the 2D profile's only rotation).

consts.name: SHAPE_BOX
consts.doc: Collider.shape: a box of `size` (both profiles).

consts.name: SHAPE_SPHERE
consts.doc: Collider.shape: a sphere of `radius` (a circle in 2D).

consts.name: SHAPE_CAPSULE
consts.doc: Collider.shape: a capsule along y of `radius`, with `height` between the cap centres (both profiles).

consts.name: SHAPE_CYLINDER
consts.doc: Collider.shape: a cylinder along y of `radius` and `height` (3D only).

consts.name: SHAPE_CONVEX
consts.doc: Collider.shape: the convex hull of the vertices of `mesh` (3D), or of their xy (a convex polygon, 2D).

consts.name: SHAPE_TRIMESH
consts.doc: Collider.shape: the triangles of `mesh` (3D only; for static and kinematic bodies).

consts.name: SHAPE_HEIGHTFIELD
consts.doc: Collider.shape: the height field registered as `mesh`, centred on the entity (3D only; a terrain: og.terrain.load's TerrainInfo.geometry).

consts.name: PROFILE_2D
consts.doc: Physics.profile: rapier2d, bodies in the xy plane rotating about z.

consts.name: PROFILE_3D
consts.doc: Physics.profile: rapier3d.

consts.name: JOINT_FIXED
consts.doc: `Joint.kind`: the two bodies move as one.

consts.name: JOINT_REVOLUTE
consts.doc: `Joint.kind`: a hinge about `axis` (2D: about z), with optional limits and a motor.

consts.name: JOINT_PRISMATIC
consts.doc: `Joint.kind`: a slider along `axis`, with optional limits and a motor.

consts.name: JOINT_SPRING
consts.doc: `Joint.kind`: a damped spring pulling the anchors to `restLength` apart.

consts.name: JOINT_ROPE
consts.doc: `Joint.kind`: a rope: the anchors stay at most `length` apart, free inside it.

consts.name: JOINT_BALL
consts.doc: `Joint.kind`: a ball and socket (3D; the 2D profile treats it as a hinge).

consts.name: MOTOR_NONE
consts.doc: `Joint.motor`: no motor.

consts.name: MOTOR_VELOCITY
consts.doc: `Joint.motor`: drive towards `motorTarget` speed (rad/s or m/s).

consts.name: MOTOR_POSITION
consts.doc: `Joint.motor`: spring towards `motorTarget` angle or position (a servo).

consts.name: CHARACTER_JUMPED
consts.doc: `CharacterEvent.kind`: a jump from the ground (or in coyote time).

consts.name: CHARACTER_LANDED
consts.doc: `CharacterEvent.kind`: touched the ground after being in the air.

consts.name: CHARACTER_WALL_JUMPED
consts.doc: `CharacterEvent.kind`: a jump off a wall.

consts.name: CHARACTER_AIR_JUMPED
consts.doc: `CharacterEvent.kind`: a jump in the air (PlatformerController.airJumps).

consts.name: CHARACTER_LEFT_GROUND
consts.doc: `CharacterEvent.kind`: left the ground without jumping (ran off an edge).

consts.name: CHARACTER_BUMPED
consts.doc: `CharacterEvent.kind`: hit a ceiling while rising.

consts.name: DRIVE_REAR
consts.doc: `Vehicle.drive`: the rear wheels drive.

consts.name: DRIVE_FRONT
consts.doc: `Vehicle.drive`: the front wheels drive.

consts.name: DRIVE_ALL
consts.doc: `Vehicle.drive`: every wheel drives.

consts.name: PIN_TOP
consts.doc: `Cloth.pins` bit: the whole top row is pinned.

consts.name: PIN_TOP_CORNERS
consts.doc: `Cloth.pins` bit: the top-left and top-right corners are pinned.

consts.name: PIN_LEFT
consts.doc: `Cloth.pins` bit: the whole left column is pinned (a flag on a pole).

consts.name: PIN_TOP_RINGS
consts.doc: `Cloth.pins` bit: every fourth point of the top row (curtain rings).

functions.name: raycast
functions.doc: The nearest collider along a ray. Inside a system it sees the colliders as they were at the start of the tick (og.physics.queries records them before the game's systems); between ticks, as the world holds them.
functions.returnsDoc: The hit, or null when nothing is hit; refused for a zero direction.

functions.name: shapeCast
functions.doc: The first collider a shape meets when swept along a direction; the same view of the colliders as raycast.

params.name: desc
params.doc: The shape, its sweep and the filter.

functions.returnsDoc: The hit, or null; refused for a zero direction or an unknown mesh.

functions.name: overlap
functions.doc: Every collider overlapping a shape, sorted by entity id; the same view of the colliders as raycast.

params.name: desc
params.doc: The shape, its placement and the filter.

functions.name: applyForce
functions.doc: Push a dynamic body with a force (N, world axes) over the next physics step, at a world point or its centre of mass: call it every tick for a steady force (thrust, wind, a car's downforce or an anti-roll assist). Applied by the og.physics step after the systems, in the order given, then gone; a hit stop drops it. Kinematic and static bodies ignore it. Pushes not yet applied are world state (in snapshots and the hash).

params.name: force
params.doc: The force in newtons (2D uses x and y).

params.name: point
params.doc: Where it acts, in world space; omitted is the centre of mass (no spin).

functions.returnsDoc: Refused for an entity without an og.RigidBody, or a force or point that is not finite.

functions.name: applyImpulse
functions.doc: Give a dynamic body an impulse (N·s, world axes) at a world point or its centre of mass: a sudden change of momentum (a kick, a hit, a jump: its velocity changes by impulse / mass), applied by the next physics step (after a hit stop ends). As applyForce otherwise.

params.name: impulse
params.doc: The impulse in newton-seconds (2D uses x and y).

params.name: point
params.doc: Where it acts, in world space; omitted is the centre of mass.

functions.returnsDoc: Refused for an entity without an og.RigidBody, or an impulse or point that is not finite.

functions.name: applyTorque
functions.doc: Turn a dynamic body with a torque (N·m about each world axis; 2D uses z) over the next physics step, as applyForce: call it every tick for a steady twist.
functions.returnsDoc: Refused for an entity without an og.RigidBody, or a torque that is not finite.

functions.name: applyTorqueImpulse
functions.doc: Give a dynamic body an angular impulse (N·m·s about each world axis; 2D uses z): its spin changes at once, as applyImpulse.
functions.returnsDoc: Refused for an entity without an og.RigidBody, or a value that is not finite.

functions.name: setMesh
functions.doc: Register (or replace) the geometry a convex or triangle-mesh Collider names by its mesh handle. Loaded glTF geometries are registered under their own handles already; meshes are assets, not world state: world.snapshot carries a mesh, convex-hull or height-field collider by its handle and scale, not its triangles, and world.restore rebuilds the collider from the geometry registered then (so load or register it before restoring; a save naming one that is not is refused).

params.name: mesh
params.doc: The handle colliders name in Collider.mesh.

functions.returnsDoc: Refused for an empty, non-finite or out-of-range mesh.

functions.name: ropePoints
functions.doc: An og.Rope's points after the last step, from its entity to its end (empty before its first step). The engine draws visible ropes itself; this is for game logic and custom drawing.
functions.returnsDoc: Refused for an entity without an og.Rope.

functions.name: clothPoints
functions.doc: An og.Cloth's points after the last step, row by row (`columns` per row, rows downwards from the top edge).
functions.returnsDoc: Refused for an entity without an og.Cloth.

functions.name: fluidParticles
functions.doc: An og.Fluid2D's particle positions after the last step, in world space.
functions.returnsDoc: Refused for an entity without an og.Fluid2D.

functions.name: fluid3dParticles
functions.doc: An og.Fluid3D's particle positions after the last step, in world space (emitted particles last, in the order they appeared).
functions.returnsDoc: Refused for an entity without an og.Fluid3D.

functions.name: waterHeight
functions.doc: The surface height of an og.WaterSurface (world y) or an og.WaterLine (world y at `x`; `z` ignored) at a point, as the last step left it: for boats that bob and spray that starts on the surface.
functions.returnsDoc: Refused for an entity without water; outside the water, its rest level.

functions.name: vehicleWheels
functions.doc: An og.Vehicle's wheels after the last step (front left, front right, rear left, rear right), for drawing wheel models.
functions.returnsDoc: Refused for an entity without a vehicle.

functions.name: ragdollRigFromSkeleton
functions.doc: A ragdoll rig from a loaded skeleton (og.load.animation's `skeleton`): a bone per joint of its first skin, parents first, each from its joint's rest pose to its first child joint, every bone naming its joint and the rig naming the skeleton. Pass it to og.physics.setRagdollRig, edited or not.
functions.returnsDoc: Refused for a skeleton that is not loaded or has no skin.

functions.name: setRagdollRig
functions.doc: Give an entity with an og.Ragdoll its bones (and, from og.physics.ragdollRigFromSkeleton, the skeleton they stand for: its og.Model is then drawn blended from the animation towards the bones by og.Ragdoll.blend). While weight is 0 the bones follow the rig's rest pose at the entity. Rigs are assets, not world state: kept by the engine and given again to a reloaded world.
functions.returnsDoc: Refused for an empty rig or a parent that does not come before its child.

functions.name: ragdollPose
functions.doc: An og.Ragdoll's bones after the last step, in rig order (empty before its first step).
functions.returnsDoc: Refused for an entity without a ragdoll.

functions.name: stats
functions.doc: What the last physics step cost: each phase's time and whether it ran on the lanes pool. All zero before the first step.
functions.returnsDoc: Refused for an engine without physics.

x-og-modules.name: atmosphere
x-og-modules.doc:
Fog, a procedural sky, the day-night cycle, weather and water, declared as resources and components (the E5 round). Everything is off by default: a world that sets none of them draws exactly as before.
The day-night clock is a function of the tick (DayNight.start plus the simulated time times speed), so it is the same on every run and after a restore; rendering reads the world and never writes it.

consts.name: WEATHER_NONE
consts.doc: Weather.kind: clear.

consts.name: WEATHER_RAIN
consts.doc: Weather.kind: rain streaks falling with the wind, the light dimmed and a grey distance fog.

consts.name: WEATHER_SNOW
consts.doc: Weather.kind: flakes drifting down on gusts, a pale fog.

consts.name: WEATHER_DUST
consts.doc: Weather.kind: dust blowing along the wind near the ground, a warm thick fog.

consts.name: WEATHER_MIST
consts.doc: Weather.kind: no particles, a dense low height fog.

functions.name: timeOfDay
functions.doc: The DayNight clock at the current tick, in hours from 0 to 24 (its start when the cycle is off): for lamps that light at dusk and shops that close at night. Inside a system, declare og.DayNight among its reads.

x-og-modules.name: anim
x-og-modules.doc:
Skeletal animation over og-anim: glTF skins and clips (cooked into the `<model>#anim` blob, loaded with og.load.animation), blend-tree graphs with layered state machines, root motion, two-bone and FABRIK IK and blendshapes, evaluated by the engine's og.anim system after the game's systems and before physics.
Game code owns the components and sets players, graph parameters and IK targets; og.anim writes the pose (kept as world state in the `og.anim` state block, so snapshots, restore and the world hash cover it), the joint palette, root motion into og.Transform and the fields marked written. Asset handles are what og.load.animation and og.anim.graph answer; 0 is none.
Clips bind to a skeleton's nodes by name, so a clip of one rig plays on another with the same node names; a rig with other names or proportions plays it retargeted (og.anim.retarget at run time, or a model's `animation { library }` import setting at cook time). Assets are not world state: a hot reload registers them again.

functions.name: graph
functions.doc: Register a blend-tree graph for AnimationGraph.asset. Its `clip` lines are resolved by name against `clips`.

params.name: world
params.doc: The world whose animation owns the graph.

params.name: desc
params.doc: The text and the clips it may name.

functions.returnsDoc: Refused for a parse error (the reason names the line), a clip name `clips` lacks, or an invalid graph.

functions.name: humanoid
functions.doc: The standard humanoid bones of a skeleton, as retargeting sees them: to check a rig before retargeting onto it.

params.name: world
params.doc: The world whose animation owns the skeleton.

functions.returnsDoc: Refused for an unregistered skeleton or rig, or a rig naming a node the skeleton lacks.

functions.name: retarget
functions.doc: A new clip for `target` from a clip of `source`: each animated humanoid bone turns as the source's does from its rest pose (after a rest correction, so a T-pose drives an A-pose and other bone frames agree; fingers turn from their hand, so a hand pose holds whatever the arm does), the target keeps its bone lengths, the hips travel the source's distance scaled by the leg ratio (root motion kept, hip height scaled), and with footIk the feet land where the source's do, scaled, on the ground each rig's `footHeight` names (else its rest pose's foot heights). The target's twist bones (unmapped nodes named `twist`, or Rigify's `DEF-….001`, on an upper or lower arm or leg) take a share of their segment's twist by how far along it they sit. Same name, duration and markers. The cook does the same for a model's `animation { library }` import setting; this is for clips chosen at run time.

params.name: world
params.doc: The world whose animation owns the skeletons and the clip.

params.name: desc
params.doc: The clip, the two skeletons and their rigs.

functions.returnsDoc: The new clip (what AnimationPlayer.clip takes). Refused for an unregistered clip, skeleton or rig, a skeleton without recognisable hips (name them in a `type rig` file), or a rig naming a missing node.

functions.name: mirror
functions.doc: A new clip that plays `clip` on the other side: every frame reflected in the skeleton's x = 0 plane, each node taking its counterpart's motion (a left swing becomes the right's), rotations moved in model space so left and right bone frames need not mirror each other, root motion's sideways travel and turns flipped. Assumes a symmetric rest pose; a sided node without a counterpart keeps its rest pose. Same name, duration and markers (markers keep their names). Mirroring twice gives the clip back.

params.name: world
params.doc: The world whose animation owns the skeleton and the clip.

functions.returnsDoc: The new clip (what AnimationPlayer.clip takes). Refused for an unregistered clip or skeleton.

functions.name: clip
functions.doc: The index of a flipbook clip by name, for Flipbook.clip: `og.anim.clip(hero, "walk_down")`. -1 when the sheet has no such clip.

functions.name: clip
functions.doc: A loaded model's clip by name, for AnimationPlayer.clip: `og.anim.clip(og.load.animation(world, "models/slime.glb").value, "chase")`, the same lookup as a flipbook's (Animation.clips by ClipInfo.name). A skinned glTF's clips are its animations' names; an animated `.vox`'s are `frames` or its `voxClip` names. 0 (plays nothing) when the model has no such clip.

functions.name: clip
functions.doc: The index of a 2D rig's clip by name, for Skeleton2D.clip: `og.anim.clip(og.load.rig2d(world, "rigs/hero.ogt").value, "walk")`. -1 when the rig has no such clip.

functions.name: rig2dInfo
functions.doc: What a loaded 2D rig holds: its bones, slots, IK constraints and clips, by the handle Skeleton2D.rig keeps (og.load.rig2d answers the same on load).

params.name: world
params.doc: The world whose animation owns the rig.

functions.returnsDoc: Refused for a handle og.load.rig2d did not answer.

functions.name: skeleton2dBoxes
functions.doc: The bounding boxes an og.Skeleton2D's pose showed when og.skeleton2d last ran (after the game's systems, so a system reads the previous tick's): hurt and hit boxes a clip switches on and off with its slots' attachments, to test against points or other shapes. Empty for a rig without boxes or when no slot shows one. They are part of the og.skeleton2d state block, so a restored snapshot answers what it saved.

params.name: world
params.doc: The world whose animation poses the skeleton.

functions.returnsDoc: Refused for an entity og.skeleton2d has not posed: no og.Skeleton2D with a loaded rig, or before its first tick.

x-og-modules.name: tween
x-og-modules.doc:
Tweens: animate any numeric field of a component (og.Transform.position, og.Sprite.color, og.Sprite.opacity, a game's own f32) from its value to a target over time with an easing curve, a delay, loops and yoyo; chain them in sequences or run them in parallel. Advanced by the engine's og.tween system after the game's systems and before og.anim and physics, by scaled time (slow motion, hit stop) unless unscaled.
Running tweens are world state (the og.tween state block): snapshots, restore and the world hash cover them. og.TweenCompleted reports a tween or group that ends on its own; a cancelled one, or one whose entity or component went away, ends silently.
Feel presets are tweens too: og.tween.squash (squash and stretch that recovers) and og.tween.flash (a hit flash that fades).

functions.name: to
functions.doc: Start a tween. Systems may call it; it first moves in this tick's og.tween run.

params.name: desc
params.doc: The field, the values and the timing.

functions.returnsDoc: Refused for a dead entity, a component it lacks, a field that is not numeric, or values of the wrong length.

functions.name: sequence
functions.doc: Start tweens one after another (each with its own delay, duration and loops); the time one leaves over goes to the next.

functions.name: parallel
functions.doc: Start tweens together; the group ends with the last one.

functions.name: cancel
functions.doc: Stop a tween where it is (no event).
functions.returnsDoc: False when it was not running.

functions.name: cancelEntity
functions.doc: Stop every tween of an entity (no events), say before starting a new reaction.
functions.returnsDoc: How many stopped.

functions.name: active
functions.doc: Whether a tween is still running.

functions.name: squash
functions.doc: Squash and stretch the entity's og.Transform.scale (cancels its earlier squash).
functions.returnsDoc: Refused for an entity without og.Transform.

functions.name: flash
