functions.doc: The world's shared hash now, hex: the hash lockstep compares, which leaves this peer's session out (og.Input, og.Lockstep, input and room events, the UI's focus; module docs). Two peers at the same tick agree on it exactly when their simulations agree; the world dump's `hash` covers everything and differs between peers.

Vector3.description: A 3D vector, as three.js Vector3. The engine is right-handed with +Y up, as three.js.

Quaternion.description: A unit quaternion rotation, as three.js Quaternion. The zero value is the identity.

Matrix4.description: A 4x4 matrix, as three.js Matrix4: sixteen elements in column-major order. The zero value is the identity.

elements.description: The elements, column-major, as three.js Matrix4.elements.

Color.description: A linear RGB colour, as three.js Color with colour management on. Components are usually between 0 and 1; above 1 is HDR.

direction.description: The unit direction the ray points in.

Box3.description: An axis-aligned box, as three.js Box3. A box whose min exceeds its max on an axis is empty (box3.empty() makes one: min +Infinity, max -Infinity).

Sphere.description: A sphere, as three.js Sphere. A negative radius is empty.

radius.description: The radius.

Plane.description: A plane, as three.js Plane: the points p with dot(normal, p) + constant = 0; normal is unit length, and the positive side is where it points.

constant.description: The signed distance from the origin to the plane, negated along the normal (three.js Plane.constant).

Frustum.description: A view volume, as three.js Frustum: six planes whose normals point inwards (right, left, bottom, top, far, near, three.js's order). frustum.fromCamera and frustum.fromProjectionMatrix make one.

FieldOptions.description: Metadata of one field. Ranges and units are what Tune and the probe's bounds show. Nothing clamps writes: game code's writes (world.set, a resource field, a column) are stored as given, and writes from outside the game (the probe's `set`, `patch` and sweeps, Tune, a look's fields at cook) are refused outside min..max with the range named.

unit.description: A unit name from the API's unit table, or empty.

label.description: The person-facing name; empty uses the field name.

doc.description: One sentence on what the field means.

tunable.description: Publish the field to Tune and to the probe's bounds and patch.

Entity.description:
An entity: an index and a generation. The value is index + generation * 2^32, with the generation below 2^21, so it stays an exact JavaScript number.
Generations start at 1, so 0 is never a live entity.

SpawnDesc.description: How to spawn an entity. `{}` spawns an unnamed entity at the origin with a Transform.

name.description: A unique name; the probe and the command channel address the entity by it. Empty leaves it unnamed.

parent.description: The parent entity; the new entity's Transform is then relative to it.

bare.description: Spawn without a Transform: a pure data entity.

migrate.description: Map a type whose layout changed since the save field by field, by name, as a hot reload does: a field added since takes its default, a removed one is dropped, an enum value is mapped by its variant's name, a field of another type starts at its default, and a type this build no longer registers is dropped. Off, such a save is refused naming the type and its fields.

WorldRestored.description: A world.restore applied: the tick after it (the first whole tick after a save taken mid-tick, whose next step completes the saved tick) delivers this, read through world.events like any event. Everything in the world came back as saved, request numbers and resources the session filled included; the session did not (og-game §17), so a system that reads this resets what belongs to the session: it forgets requests answered long ago, asks the store again for the settings and progress, and closes a menu the player had open. Sent as that tick starts, not when the restore applies, so the world between the two hashes as the save did.

from.description: The tick the world was at when the restore applied.

tick.description: The saved tick: og.Time's tick right after the restore.

without.description: Components an entity must not have.

SystemDesc.description: A system's declared access and order.

reads.description: Components, resources and events the system reads (world.events). Every component here is also required by its query: a matched entity has all of the reads' and writes' components.

writes.description: Components, resources and events the system writes (world.emit). Every component here is also required by its query, with the reads'.

without.description: Components a matched entity must not have.

after.description: Names of systems that must run before this one.

before.description: Names of systems that must run after this one.

GameDesc.description: A game: its tick, scenes, systems and commands.

tick.description: The fixed tick rate. Left unset, project.ogt's `tick` applies (else 60); tick, seed, scenes and scene set both here and in project.ogt to different values refuse the engine, naming both.

seed.description: The project seed every Rng stream derives from; left unset, project.ogt's `seed` (else 0). A replay overrides it.

scenes.description: Scene names to `.ogt` paths, as `{ main: "scenes/main.ogt" }`; left unset, project.ogt's `scenes` block.

scene.description: The scene loaded first; left unset, project.ogt's `scene` (else main).

systems.description: The systems, in declaration order before `after`/`before` constraints apply.

resources.description: The game's own resources, created at their defaults.

commands.description: Game actions registered into the command channel, by action name.

commandHelp.description: Each game action's argument form and one sentence, by its name in commands, for `help`: `{ place: { usage: "<x>:<y>", doc: "Move the hero there." } }`. An action without an entry is listed by name alone.

maxCatchUp.description: The most ticks one frame may run to catch up with the clock; the accumulator drops the rest.

facts.description: The game's own facts for the probe's state().

start.description: Called once before the first tick, after the first scene spawned. A throw fails the run: no tick runs on the half-built world, `og run`, `og test` and `og dev` exit non-zero naming the error with its stack, and the web shell shows it.

render.description: How the renderer is created: antialiasing and shadow map size. Read once, when the host attaches the renderer.

look.description: A look (`looks/<name>.ogt`, og.load.look) applied after the first scene spawned and before start runs, so start may still change any of it; its antialias is the renderer's when render leaves antialias out. Empty applies none.

Transform.description: Where an entity is, relative to its parent (or the world).

Parent.description: The entity this one's Transform is relative to. Set by SpawnDesc.parent.

MatrixWorld.description: The world matrix the engine composes after the systems run, as three.js Object3D.matrixWorld.

Time.description: The fixed tick's clock. Every value is a function of the tick count, so a replay sees the same numbers. The world keeps the time scale in a second resource, og.TimeScale (`scale`, `hitStop`, and `elapsed`, which is scaledElapsed), set through og.time.setScale and og.time.hitStop; read og.Time, which carries all of it. The probe's `get:og.Time` answers every field here, as a system's `time` does; `set:og.TimeScale.scale=0.5` slows time from a script.

tick.description: Fixed steps taken since load.

dt.description: The length of one tick: 1 / rate.

elapsed.description: Simulation time since load: tick * dt.

scale.description: Global slow motion, set with og.time.setScale: 1 is normal, 0.5 half speed, 0 stopped. Physics, animation, flipbooks and tweens advance by scaledDt; the tick itself, the UI, input and the probe keep their pace.

hitStop.description: Ticks of hit stop left (og.time.hitStop): while above 0, scaledDt is 0.

scaledDt.description: This tick's scaled length: 0 during a hit stop, else dt * scale. Move gameplay by it so slow motion and hit stop reach game code too.

scaledElapsed.description: Scaled seconds since load: the sum of every finished tick's scaledDt.

Rng.description: The world's main random stream, seeded from GameDesc.seed (or the replay seed). Its state is part of every snapshot.

seed.description: The seed the stream started from.

state.description: The generator state; snapshot and restore carry it.

GamepadButton.description: A gamepad button in the W3C standard mapping, in its index order (a is button 0).

x-og-variants.leftTrigger: The left trigger, as a button (its analog value is the leftTrigger axis).
x-og-variants.rightTrigger: The right trigger, as a button.

GamepadAxis.description: An analog input of a gamepad.

x-og-variants.leftY: The left stick's y, -1 (up) to 1 (down), as the Gamepad API reports it.
x-og-variants.rightY: The right stick's y, down positive.

KeyAction.description: What an injected key event does.

x-og-variants.press: Down, then up on the next tick.

PointerAction.description: What an injected pointer event does.

x-og-variants.click: Down, then up on the next tick, at the point.

PointerButton.description: A physical pointer button; `none` is a hover move.

x-og-variants.left: The primary button, or a touch.

Modifiers.description: Modifier keys held during a key event.

platform.description: Command on macOS, the Windows key on Windows.

KeyInput.description: A key event. `key` names the physical key as KeyboardEvent.code does: ArrowRight, Space, KeyA.

at.description: When it happened, in ticks from the start of the tick that reads it (-1 to 1; omitted is 0): the KeyDown, KeyUp, PointerDown or PointerUp it raises carry it. An engine extension of protocol 5.

PointerInput.description: A pointer event at a point in CSS pixels of the play surface.

button.description: The button; `none` for a hover move.

id.description: Which pointer: 0 the primary one (the mouse, the first touch; what protocol 5 means), 1 to 4 further touches held at the same time (an engine extension). Omitted is 0.

at.description: When it happened, in ticks from the start of the tick that reads it (-1 to 1; omitted is 0): the KeyDown, KeyUp, PointerDown or PointerUp it raises carry it. An engine extension of protocol 5.

GamepadInput.description: A gamepad's whole state (an engine extension of protocol 5): the shell sends one whenever a pad changes, and a playtest can send its own.

connected.description: Whether the pad is connected (omitted is true); a disconnected pad holds nothing.

axes.description: Left stick x, y, right stick x, y; each -1 to 1, y down. Missing values are 0.

triggers.description: The left and right analog triggers, 0 to 1. Missing values are 0.

WheelInput.description: A wheel or trackpad scroll at a point.

TextEntry.description: Typed or composed text (an engine extension of protocol 5): what the page's `beforeinput` inserted (a key's character, a paste, an input method's commit), or with `composing` an input method's composition so far. Raises TextInput events; the UI's focused text field takes them.

composing.description: An input method's composition, not yet committed: it replaces the composition before it, and empty ends it. Omitted is false: committed text.

A11yActionKind.description: What an assistive technology asks of a UI control.

x-og-variants.focus: Move the UI's focus to it (with the focus ring).
x-og-variants.activate: Press it, as Enter on it would (a text control takes the focus).
x-og-variants.increment: Step an adjustable control (a slider, a stepper) up.

A11yRequest.description: A screen reader's request on a UI control (an engine extension of protocol 5): the web shell's mirror of og.ui.a11y() sends it when a reader focuses, activates or adjusts a mirrored node. Raises an A11yAction event; the UI acts on it at the start of the next frame, against the last frame's controls (a path naming no focusable control of the topmost dialog is ignored; increment and decrement also take a stepper's spinbutton, whose buttons are the focusable controls).

path.description: The control's path, as og.ui.a11y() names it.

InjectedInput.description: One input event in the game's own vocabulary, as the probe's input() and playtest scripts carry it.

at.description: When it happened, in ticks from the start of the tick that reads it (-1 to 1; omitted is 0): the KeyDown, KeyUp, PointerDown or PointerUp it raises carry it. An engine extension of protocol 5.

button.description: The button; `none` for a hover move.

id.description: Which pointer: 0 the primary one (the mouse, the first touch; what protocol 5 means), 1 to 4 further touches held at the same time (an engine extension). Omitted is 0.

at.description: When it happened, in ticks from the start of the tick that reads it (-1 to 1; omitted is 0): the KeyDown, KeyUp, PointerDown or PointerUp it raises carry it. An engine extension of protocol 5.

connected.description: Whether the pad is connected (omitted is true); a disconnected pad holds nothing.

axes.description: Left stick x, y, right stick x, y; each -1 to 1, y down. Missing values are 0.

triggers.description: The left and right analog triggers, 0 to 1. Missing values are 0.

composing.description: An input method's composition, not yet committed: it replaces the composition before it, and empty ends it. Omitted is false: committed text.

oneOf.description: A screen reader's request on a UI control.

path.description: The control's path, as og.ui.a11y() names it.

Input.description:
The input state at the start of this tick (og-input's og.Input, version 2). Edges (pressed, released) last exactly one tick; read the state through the methods.
Key sets are 128 bits over og-input's KEY_CODES (KeyboardEvent.code names): code i is bit i % 32 of word i / 32. Button masks: left 1, middle 2, right 4.

pointerInside.description: Whether a pointer event has placed the pointer over the play surface.

buttons.description: Held pointer buttons, as a mask.

buttonsPressed.description: Buttons that went down this tick.

buttonsReleased.description: Buttons that went up this tick.

buttonsReleaseNext.description: Buttons a click releases at the end of the next tick.

keys0.description: Held keys, word 0: codes 0 to 31 of KEY_CODES.

keys1.description: Held keys, word 1: codes 32 to 63 of KEY_CODES.

keys2.description: Held keys, word 2: codes 64 to 95 of KEY_CODES.

keys3.description: Held keys, word 3: codes 96 to 127 of KEY_CODES.

pressed0.description: Keys that went down this tick, word 0: codes 0 to 31 of KEY_CODES.

pressed1.description: Keys that went down this tick, word 1: codes 32 to 63 of KEY_CODES.

pressed2.description: Keys that went down this tick, word 2: codes 64 to 95 of KEY_CODES.

pressed3.description: Keys that went down this tick, word 3: codes 96 to 127 of KEY_CODES.

released0.description: Keys that went up this tick, word 0: codes 0 to 31 of KEY_CODES.

released1.description: Keys that went up this tick, word 1: codes 32 to 63 of KEY_CODES.

released2.description: Keys that went up this tick, word 2: codes 64 to 95 of KEY_CODES.

released3.description: Keys that went up this tick, word 3: codes 96 to 127 of KEY_CODES.

releaseNext0.description: Keys a press releases at the end of the next tick, word 0: codes 0 to 31 of KEY_CODES.

releaseNext1.description: Keys a press releases at the end of the next tick, word 1: codes 32 to 63 of KEY_CODES.

releaseNext2.description: Keys a press releases at the end of the next tick, word 2: codes 64 to 95 of KEY_CODES.

releaseNext3.description: Keys a press releases at the end of the next tick, word 3: codes 96 to 127 of KEY_CODES.

Pointers.description:
Every pointer on the play surface at once, at the start of this tick (og-input's og.Pointers): a touch stick and a touch button can be held together. Pointer 0 is og.Input's pointer; ids 1 to 4 are further touches, in the order they landed (the lowest free id).
Edges last exactly one tick, as og.Input's do. Masks are bit `id`; read them through the methods.

heldMask.description: Pointers held down, as a mask.

pressedMask.description: Pointers that went down this tick.

releasedMask.description: Pointers that went up this tick.

releaseNextMask.description: Pointers a click releases at the end of the next tick.

Gamepad.description:
The first four gamepads in the W3C standard mapping, at the start of this tick (og-input's og.Gamepad). On the web the shell polls the pads each display frame and sends their state through the input ring, so a pad is world state and replays; it also maps pads to keys for games that only read keys.
Button masks are bit `GamepadButton` index per pad; edges last exactly one tick, and a press and a release between two ticks leave both edges set. Read them through the methods.

pressed0.description: Buttons of pad 0 that went down this tick.

pressed1.description: Buttons of pad 1 that went down this tick.

pressed2.description: Buttons of pad 2 that went down this tick.

pressed3.description: Buttons of pad 3 that went down this tick.

released0.description: Buttons of pad 0 that went up this tick.

released1.description: Buttons of pad 1 that went up this tick.

released2.description: Buttons of pad 2 that went up this tick.

released3.description: Buttons of pad 3 that went up this tick.

leftStick0.description: The left stick of pad 0, -1 to 1, y down.

leftStick1.description: The left stick of pad 1, -1 to 1, y down.

leftStick2.description: The left stick of pad 2, -1 to 1, y down.

leftStick3.description: The left stick of pad 3, -1 to 1, y down.

rightStick0.description: The right stick of pad 0, -1 to 1, y down.

rightStick1.description: The right stick of pad 1, -1 to 1, y down.

rightStick2.description: The right stick of pad 2, -1 to 1, y down.

rightStick3.description: The right stick of pad 3, -1 to 1, y down.

triggers0.description: The left (x) and right (y) triggers of pad 0, 0 to 1.

triggers1.description: The left (x) and right (y) triggers of pad 1, 0 to 1.

triggers2.description: The left (x) and right (y) triggers of pad 2, 0 to 1.

triggers3.description: The left (x) and right (y) triggers of pad 3, 0 to 1.

KeyDown.description: A key went down (a down for a held key is a repeat and sets no edge). Input events are sent between ticks and read by the next tick's systems.

at.description: When it happened, in ticks from the start of the tick that reads it, -1 to 1 (0 when the host gave no time): its world time is `time.elapsed + at * time.dt`. The shell stamps it from the browser event's timeStamp, the command channel from the step's time; it is part of the event, so a replay carries it.

TextInput.description: Text typed or composed (an engine extension): the shell sends it from the page's `beforeinput` and composition events, the probe's `type:`, `compose:` and `commit:` from scripts. A text longer than 255 bytes arrives as several events in order. Key events still arrive for the keys; a text field types from these once a world has had one.

composing.description: An input method's composition so far, not committed: it replaces the composition before it (empty ends it). False: committed text to insert.

more.description: Continues the composition of the event before it (a composition longer than one event).

at.description: When it happened, in ticks from the start of the tick that reads it, -1 to 1 (0 when the host gave no time): its world time is `time.elapsed + at * time.dt`. The shell stamps it from the browser event's timeStamp, the command channel from the step's time; it is part of the event, so a replay carries it.

PointerDown.description: A pointer button went down (or a touch landed).

id.description: Which pointer: 0 the primary one, 1 to 4 further touches (og.Pointers).

at.description: When it happened, in ticks from the start of the tick that reads it, -1 to 1 (0 when the host gave no time): its world time is `time.elapsed + at * time.dt`. The shell stamps it from the browser event's timeStamp, the command channel from the step's time; it is part of the event, so a replay carries it.

PointerUp.description: A pointer button went up (or a touch lifted).

id.description: Which pointer: 0 the primary one, 1 to 4 further touches.

at.description: When it happened, in ticks from the start of the tick that reads it, -1 to 1 (0 when the host gave no time): its world time is `time.elapsed + at * time.dt`. The shell stamps it from the browser event's timeStamp, the command channel from the step's time; it is part of the event, so a replay carries it.

id.description: Which pointer: 0 the primary one, 1 to 4 further touches.

A11yAction.description: A screen reader's request on a UI control (an engine extension): the web shell sends it from its mirror of og.ui.a11y(); the UI takes it at the start of the next frame. A path longer than 255 bytes is refused.

path.description: The control's path, as og.ui.a11y() names it.

Camera.description: The camera the frame is rendered from. Rendering reads it after the tick; it never feeds back into the simulation.

quaternion.description: Its rotation; the camera looks down its local -Z.

fov.description: The vertical field of view of the perspective projection.

zoom.description: The zoom factor, as three.js Camera.zoom.

orthographic.description: Use an orthographic projection (the 2D profile) instead of a perspective one.

height.description: The visible world height of the orthographic projection.

background.description: The clear colour, as three.js Scene.background. The default is the brand ink #14161b in linear RGB.

exposure.description: Exposure before tone mapping, as three.js toneMappingExposure.

trauma.description: Screen shake, 0 to 1, added by og.camera.shake and decayed by traumaDecay every tick (unscaled, so a hit stop still shakes). The offset and roll grow with trauma squared and follow smooth noise of the tick: visual only, a replay shakes the same.

traumaDecay.description: How much trauma drains per second.

shakeOffset.description: The largest offset at trauma 1, as a fraction of the view height.

punch.description: A zoom punch in progress (og.camera.punch): the view is narrowed by this fraction, decaying by punchDecay. Visual only.

punchDecay.description: How fast a punch springs back (exponential, per second).

kick.description: A kick in progress (og.camera.kick): the view is offset by this, decaying by kickDecay. Visual only.

kickDecay.description: How fast a kick returns (exponential, per second).

zoneActive.description: The followed entity is in an og.CameraZone: the view keeps inside zoneMin to zoneMax. Written by the og.camera system.

zoneMin.description: The zone the view keeps inside: its bottom-left corner.

zoneFromActive.description: A room transition is in progress from the zone zoneFromMin to zoneFromMax: the view scrolls from where that zone kept it to where the new one does.

zoneFromMin.description: The zone being left: its bottom-left corner.

zoneScroll.description: How far the transition has come, 0 to 1 (eased; 1 is settled).

zoneScrollTime.description: How long the transition takes: the entered zone's scrollTime.

layers.description: Three.js layers, as Camera.layers.mask: the frame draws the meshes, models, world sprites, particle systems, lines and points whose layers share a bit with it. 1 (layer 0) by default, as every object's.

OrbitCamera.description:
Orbits og.Camera around the entity carrying it, as three.js OrbitControls: a left-button drag on the play surface turns it, the wheel zooms, autoRotate turns it on its own.
Camera controllers are game-level systems the engine ships in TypeScript (og.systems.cameras); list them in GameDesc.systems: `systems: [...og.systems.cameras, ...yours]`. The first entity carrying one, in query order, drives the camera.
The camera sits `distance` from the orbited point (the entity's position plus `target`) in the direction given by `azimuth` about +Y and `polar` from +Y, and looks at the point. Every angle is computed with deterministic arithmetic, so a replay moves the camera identically on every host.

target.description: The orbited point, relative to the entity's position.

distance.description: How far the camera is from the orbited point, as three.js OrbitControls' distance.

minDistance.description: The closest the wheel zooms in, as three.js OrbitControls.minDistance.

maxDistance.description: The farthest the wheel zooms out, as three.js OrbitControls.maxDistance.

azimuth.description: The horizontal angle about +Y; 0 puts the camera on the +Z side of the point.

polar.description: The angle from +Y: near 0 looks straight down, half pi is level with the point.

minPolarAngle.description: The smallest polar angle a drag reaches, as three.js OrbitControls.minPolarAngle.

maxPolarAngle.description: The largest polar angle a drag reaches, as three.js OrbitControls.maxPolarAngle.

rotateSpeed.description: Drag sensitivity, as three.js OrbitControls.rotateSpeed: at 1, dragging the play surface's height turns a full circle.

zoomSpeed.description: Wheel sensitivity, as three.js OrbitControls.zoomSpeed: at 1, 100 CSS pixels of wheel change the distance by a tenth.

autoRotate.description: Turn about the point on its own while not dragged, as three.js OrbitControls.autoRotate.

enabled.description: Read the pointer and the wheel; false keeps only autoRotate and the fields' own values.

dragging.description: Controller state: a left-button drag that started on the play surface is in progress.

pointer.description: Controller state: where the pointer was on the previous tick of a drag.

FollowCamera.description: Chases the entity carrying it with og.Camera: a third-person 3D view that eases towards a point offset from the entity and looks at it. Driven by og.systems.cameras; the first entity carrying one, in query order, drives the camera.

offset.description: Where the camera sits relative to the entity: in the entity's own axes with followRotation, else in world axes.

lookOffset.description: The point the camera looks at, relative to the entity's position.

followRotation.description: Turn the offset with the entity's rotation, so the camera stays behind it.

smoothTime.description: Roughly how long the camera takes to catch up with a moved entity; 0 snaps it there every tick.

Follow2D.description: Keeps og.Camera on the entity carrying it in the xy plane, for 2D games: the camera moves only when the entity leaves the dead zone, eases by smoothTime (smoothTimeY for y when set) and, with clamp, stays inside the bounds; lookAhead leads it in the direction the entity moves. The camera keeps its z, rotation and projection. Driven by og.systems.cameras; og.CameraZone entities then keep the view inside the zone the entity is in.

offset.description: Where the camera centre sits relative to the entity.

deadZone.description: Half the width and height of the box around the camera centre inside which the entity moves without moving the camera.

smoothTime.description: Roughly how long the camera takes to catch up; 0 snaps it every tick.

smoothTimeY.description: The same for y alone (a platformer follows jumps more lazily than runs); below 0 uses smoothTime.

lookAhead.description: Lead the entity by its velocity times this many seconds (0: no look-ahead).

lookAheadMax.description: The largest lead along x and y.

lookAheadSmoothing.description: Roughly how long the lead takes to turn when the entity does.

last.description: Controller state: the entity's position on the previous tick.

clamp.description: Keep the camera centre between boundsMin and boundsMax.

boundsMin.description: The smallest x and y the camera centre takes with clamp.

boundsMax.description: The largest x and y the camera centre takes with clamp.

CameraZone.description: A rectangle of the xy plane (min to max, world units, not moved by the entity's Transform) that keeps a 2D view inside it while the entity followed by og.Follow2D is in it: rooms, arenas, a level's bounds. Of overlapping zones the highest priority wins, then the first in query order. The engine's og.camera system picks the zone after the game's systems (into og.Camera's zone fields); entering another zone scrolls the view across over the new zone's scrollTime, or jumps when it is 0. A zone smaller than the view centres it.

scrollTime.description: Seconds the view takes to scroll from the zone the entity left into this one (a room transition, eased in and out); 0 jumps at once. Visual only: the camera resource records the transition, so replays scroll the same.

CameraRail.description: Moves og.Camera along a spline through p0 to p(points - 1) (Catmull-Rom, through every point) to the point nearest the entity carrying it, easing by smoothTime: a corridor, a side-scroller's track, a 3D chase on rails. A perspective camera looks at the entity; an orthographic one keeps its z and rotation. Applied by the engine's og.camera system after the game's systems.

points.description: How many of p0...p7 the rail uses (2 to 8).

smoothTime.description: Roughly how long the camera takes to catch up along the rail; 0 snaps.

path.description: A path (og.path.create, or a scene's `path` by og.path.find) the rail follows instead of p0 to p(points - 1): any number of points, catmullRom, bezier or linear, closed or not. 0 uses the points.

Geometry.description: Vertex and index data, as three.js BufferGeometry. Comes from a loaded glTF.

Side.description: Which faces are drawn, as three.js FrontSide, BackSide and DoubleSide.

RenderTier.description: The backend the renderer runs on; the probe's hello reports it.

x-og-variants.webgpu: WebGPU in a browser: the full feature set.
x-og-variants.webgl2: The WebGL2 fallback: no compute, CPU culling and particles, tiled lights.
x-og-variants.vulkan-cpu: Native Vulkan on a CPU rasterizer (Mesa lavapipe or llvmpipe, SwiftShader): the executors' sandboxes. Frame times there say nothing about a player's GPU.
x-og-variants.none: No renderer (a sandbox without a GPU; natively also OG_RENDERER=none): the simulation, the dumps and the world hash are the same as with one, a screenshot step writes no PNG and reports its frame unchecked, and capture answers null.

Antialias.description: Antialiasing, as og-render's Antialias. RenderCapabilities.antialias reports what the device resolved.

x-og-variants.tier: The tier's method: TAA on the full tier (WebGPU, Metal, Vulkan), 4x MSAA on WebGL2, FXAA where the HDR format cannot be multisampled.
x-og-variants.msaa4: 4x MSAA on any tier: sharp sprites and text, no temporal blur; FXAA where the HDR format cannot be multisampled.
x-og-variants.taa: Temporal antialiasing on any tier: a sub-pixel jitter per frame and a reprojected history; converges over about eight frames. RenderOptions.taaHistory and taaSharpen refine it.
x-og-variants.fxaa: FXAA on any tier: one full-screen pass over the tonemapped image (the overlay stays sharp), no extra samples and nothing to converge; softer than MSAA on fine texture.

PointShadows.description: How a point light's shadow map is stored, as og-render's PointShadows. RenderCapabilities.pointShadows reports what the device resolved.

x-og-variants.auto: Cube faces on the full tier, paraboloids on WebGL2.
x-og-variants.cube: Six 90 degree faces: six shadow passes per light.
x-og-variants.paraboloid: Two paraboloid hemispheres (below and above the light): two passes per light instead of six, coarser, and large casters' silhouettes approximate (their edges stay straight in the curved projection).

TaaHistory.description: How TAA resamples its history each frame, as og-render's TaaHistory.

x-og-variants.bilinear: One bilinear tap: cheap, slightly soft while the camera moves.
x-og-variants.catmullRom: A Catmull-Rom filter over 4x4 texels (9 taps): the history stays sharp under camera motion.

DebugView.description: What the debug overlay shows besides og.debug's draws (og.debug.setView, RenderOptions.debugView, `debug:<view>`), drawn over the finished frame. Streams add views as they add what to show.

x-og-variants.physics: The colliders' shapes, joints and contacts as the last physics step left them.
x-og-variants.nav: The navigation grids (blocked cells) and navmeshes (polygon edges), and every og.NavAgent's path.
x-og-variants.bounds: Every drawn mesh's bounds (its geometry's box at its transform).
x-og-variants.lod: Every og.Model tinted by the level of detail it draws (green the full mesh, yellow level 1, orange level 2, red level 3 and beyond), so the levels' distances read in one frame.

RenderOptions.description: How the renderer is created for a game (GameDesc.render). The host reads it once, when it attaches the renderer.

shadowMapSize.description: The side of each of the directional light's three cascade maps, in texels; smaller saves memory on phones (three 2048 maps are 64 MB).

pointShadows.description: How point lights' shadows are stored: cube faces, or two paraboloid hemispheres (fewer passes, coarser).

taaHistory.description: With TAA: how the history is resampled.

taaSharpen.description: With TAA: a sharpening pass after it, 0 (none) to 1; it never pushes a pixel past its neighbours' range.

debugView.description: A debug overlay from the first frame (og.debug.setView, the command channel's `debug:<view>`): none in a game, a view while building one. Not in publish builds.

StandardMaterialDesc.description:
A physically based metallic-roughness material with three.js MeshStandardMaterial parameter names.
It is og-render's reflected StandardMaterial field for field: metalnessMap and roughnessMap read a glTF metallic-roughness texture (blue metal, green rough), so give both the same texture; alphaTest above 0 discards below that alpha; transparent blends, sorted back to front.
The stylised fields: unlit (three.js MeshBasicMaterial), toon with its gradientMap ramp, a rim (fresnel) light, a hit flash, dissolve with a glowing edge, and a per-material outline. All are off at their defaults. og.MaterialStyle fills the ones a material leaves at their defaults unless the material sets styled false.
The MeshPhysicalMaterial fields, under three.js's names and glTF's KHR_materials_* meanings, all off at their defaults: clearcoat with clearcoatMap, clearcoatRoughnessMap and clearcoatNormalMap; sheen (velvet, cloth) with sheenColor, sheenRoughness and their maps; transmission (glass, water) refracting the opaque scene behind through thickness, attenuationColor and ior; iridescence (soap film, oil) with its film's iridescenceIOR and iridescenceThicknessRange; anisotropy (brushed metal) along anisotropyRotation or anisotropyMap. They draw on every tier, WebGL2 included; unlit and toon materials ignore them.
A transmissive material is drawn after the opaque scene, back to front with the transparent ones, and refracts what was drawn before it (not other transmissive or transparent objects); thickness is in the mesh's own units, scaled with it.
normalMap is read in glTF's tangent frame: red tilts towards +u, green up the image. The tangents come from the model (the cook generates MikkTSpace ones where a glTF has none) or are generated when the geometry is made; normals follow a non-uniform scale correctly.

metalnessMap.description: Metalness from the texture's blue channel.

roughnessMap.description: Roughness from the texture's green channel.

aoMap.description: Ambient occlusion from the texture's red channel.

emissiveIntensity.description: A multiplier on the emitted colour.

opacity.description: The opacity; below 1 only with transparent.

transparent.description: Blend instead of writing opaque pixels.

alphaTest.description: Discard pixels whose alpha is below this.

normalScale.description: How strongly the normal map bends the normal, per tangent axis.

aoMapIntensity.description: How strongly aoMap darkens the ambient light.

unlit.description: No lighting at all, as three.js MeshBasicMaterial: the colour (times map) plus emissive.

toon.description: Cel shading, as three.js MeshToonMaterial: light is quantized by gradientMap (three built-in bands without one), highlights are hard.

gradientMap.description: The toon ramp: a texture whose first row maps the light's angle (left dark, right lit) to the light received, read without filtering.

rimColor.description: Rim (fresnel) light added at grazing angles, unshadowed (linear).

rimIntensity.description: The rim light's strength; 0 is none.

rimPower.description: How tight the rim is (higher: thinner).

flashColor.description: The colour a hit flash mixes towards (linear, may exceed 1).

flash.description: How far the final colour is mixed towards flashColor (0 none, 1 flat): animate it per tick for a hit flash.

dissolve.description: The dissolved fraction: 0 whole, 1 gone. Pixels whose noise is below it are discarded (shadows too); the band just above glows with dissolveEdgeColor.

dissolveMap.description: The dissolve noise from the texture's red channel; without one, value noise over the object-space position.

dissolveEdgeColor.description: The glowing edge (linear, usually above 1 so it blooms).

dissolveEdgeWidth.description: The width of the glowing band in noise units.

dissolveScale.description: The frequency of the built-in noise (cells per object-space unit).

outlineWidth.description: This material's outline width in pixels; 0 is none (PostEffects.outline outlines everything). A hull outline, as toon shading draws one: the object's silhouette, where one part of it passes in front of another, and its creases against other objects (where it meets the ground or a wall), never the edges between its own faces, so a .vox model or any flat-shaded, hard-edged mesh keeps clean faces inside its silhouette; a face seen at a grazing angle (a box's side nearly edge-on, a large ground plane) is not lined across, only where it ends. Creases inside an object are Stylise.inkDepth's.

styled.description: Whether og.MaterialStyle (a look's scene-wide toon, rim, outline, flat facets, shadow tint and outline distance) reaches this material. false keeps it exactly as declared under any look: a lantern's lacquer, a UI-like prop, a hero kept photographic in a toon scene. A material with a MeshPhysicalMaterial lobe (clearcoat, sheen, transmission, iridescence, anisotropy, an ior other than 1.5) keeps its physical shading under the style's toon even when styled (toon would drop those lobes) and takes the rest of the style; its own toon true still makes it toon.

clearcoat.description: A clear lacquer over the surface, as three.js MeshPhysicalMaterial.clearcoat: a second, 4 % reflective specular layer on the surface's normal before normalMap (car paint, varnished wood, wet plastic); 0 is none.

clearcoatRoughness.description: How rough the clear coat is, as three.js MeshPhysicalMaterial.clearcoatRoughness.

clearcoatMap.description: The coat's strength from the texture's red channel, times clearcoat (MeshPhysicalMaterial.clearcoatMap).

clearcoatRoughnessMap.description: The coat's roughness from the texture's green channel, times clearcoatRoughness.

clearcoatNormalMap.description: A tangent-space normal map of the coat alone; the base keeps normalMap (MeshPhysicalMaterial.clearcoatNormalMap).

clearcoatNormalScale.description: How strongly clearcoatNormalMap bends the coat's normal, per tangent axis.

sheen.description: A velvet-like layer that brightens grazing angles (cloth, fuzz, peach skin), as MeshPhysicalMaterial.sheen: its strength, times sheenColor; 0 is none.

sheenColor.description: The sheen's colour (linear), times sheenColorMap; black is none.

sheenRoughness.description: How rough the sheen is: low keeps it to a thin rim, high spreads it over the surface.

sheenColorMap.description: The sheen's colour from the texture's RGB (sRGB).

sheenRoughnessMap.description: The sheen's roughness from the texture's alpha channel.

transmission.description: How much light passes through, as MeshPhysicalMaterial.transmission (glass, water, thin plastic): the opaque scene behind is refracted and blurred by roughness; 0 is none. Unlike opacity, the surface keeps its reflections.

transmissionMap.description: Transmission from the texture's red channel.

thickness.description: The volume's thickness under the surface in the mesh's own units (glTF KHR_materials_volume): how far refraction bends the view and how much attenuationColor absorbs; 0 is a thin wall.

thicknessMap.description: Thickness from the texture's green channel.

attenuationDistance.description: The distance light travels in the volume before it is tinted to attenuationColor (world units); 0 is no absorption, three.js's Infinity.

attenuationColor.description: The colour white light becomes after attenuationDistance in the volume (linear).

ior.description: The index of refraction (glTF KHR_materials_ior): the reflectance of a dielectric, ((ior - 1) / (ior + 1))^2 (4 % at 1.5), and how far transmission refracts.

iridescence.description: A thin-film interference layer, as MeshPhysicalMaterial.iridescence (soap bubbles, oil, beetle shells); 0 is none.

iridescenceThicknessRange.description: The film's thickness in nanometres: x where iridescenceThicknessMap is black, y where it is white and everywhere without the map (three.js's [100, 400]).

iridescenceMap.description: Iridescence from the texture's red channel.

iridescenceThicknessMap.description: The film's thickness between iridescenceThicknessRange's ends from the texture's green channel.

anisotropy.description: Stretches the specular highlight along a direction of the surface, as MeshPhysicalMaterial.anisotropy (brushed metal, hair, satin); 0 is none, 1 fully stretched. Needs the geometry's tangents (generated when it has none).

anisotropyRotation.description: The stretch's direction in radians from the tangent (+u) towards the bitangent.

anisotropyMap.description: The stretch's direction in red and green (-1 to 1 in the tangent frame, turned by anisotropyRotation) and its strength in blue, times anisotropy.

mapArray.description: The base colour from layer mapLayer of a texture array (og.load.textureArray) instead of map: variants of one look (tiles, skins, damage states) are one material, each Mesh picking its layer with Mesh.materialLayer, and every mesh of the material is one draw whichever layer it shows. A material with mapArray or normalMapArray reads its base colour and normal map from arrays only (map and normalMap are not read); it draws on every tier, WebGL2 included. Physical materials (the MeshPhysicalMaterial fields) and shader materials do not take arrays.

mapLayer.description: The layer of mapArray drawn where the Mesh does not pick one (past the array's last layer: the last).

normalMapArray.description: A tangent-space normal map from layer normalMapLayer of a texture array (linear: cook it with `kind normal`), the counterpart of mapArray.

normalMapLayer.description: The layer of normalMapArray read where the Mesh does not pick one.

wireframe.description: Draw the edges of the mesh's triangles instead of its faces, as three.js Material.wireframe: one CSS pixel wide, in color plus the emissive light, unlit, depth tested; on every tier (lines, not a polygon mode WebGL2 lacks). Its meshes cast no shadow.

Mesh.description:
Draws a geometry with a material at the entity's MatrixWorld, as a three.js Mesh.
The material is a handle from og.render.standardMaterial or from a loaded glTF (GltfInfo.materials); its StandardMaterialDesc maps to the renderer as that struct's docs say.

castShadow.description: Cast shadows, as three.js Object3D.castShadow: drawn into the sun's cascades and the shadowed lights' maps. Off by default: a lamp's own glass around its light, a glow card or a decal-like slab casts none.

receiveShadow.description: Receive shadows, as three.js Object3D.receiveShadow: darkened where the sun's cascades and the shadowed lights' maps say something stands between it and the light. On by default (three.js's is off): every mesh received shadows before the flag was applied. false lights it as if unshadowed by every light, while it still casts as castShadow says: a glowing sign, a hero kept readable in a dark alley.

flash.description: A hit flash on this mesh only: the lit colour mixed towards flashColor by this much (og.tween.flash fades it out). Carried with its transform to the lit shaders, as og.Model's, so a flashing mesh is one draw with the other meshes of its geometry and material, and the amount is continuous.

flashColor.description: The flash's linear colour, 0 to 1 a channel (8 bits a channel).

materialLayer.description: The texture-array layer this mesh's material reads (StandardMaterialDesc.mapArray and normalMapArray), in place of the material's mapLayer and normalMapLayer: one material, one draw, a layer per mesh (a tile set, a crowd's skins). -1 keeps the material's layers; a material without arrays ignores it.

layers.description: Three.js layers, as Object3D.layers.mask: bit n set puts it on layer n. A camera (og.Camera, og.CameraView, og.Mirror) draws it when their masks share a bit, and og.render.raycast tests it when its own `layers` does. Shadow maps take every caster whatever its layers, so a body hidden from a first-person camera still casts.

DirectionalLight.description:
The sun, as three.js DirectionalLight: parallel light along the entity's local -Z (aim it with transform.lookAt, as a camera). The first one found is drawn, with three shadow cascades.
Without one, the renderer's default sun (from above and to the side, intensity 3) lights the scene.

intensity.description: The radiance multiplier, as three.js DirectionalLight.intensity.

castShadow.description: Cast shadows through three cascades, as three.js Light.castShadow.

shadowDistance.description: How far from the camera shadows reach; they fade over the last tenth. Smaller is sharper.

shadowSoftness.description: Soft shadows (PCSS): the penumbra's width per metre between caster and receiver, the tangent of the sun's apparent radius (the real sun's is 0.005). 0 keeps the hard one-texel edge; 0.01 to 0.05 is a soft sun, sharp at contact and blurring with distance. Costs a blocker search and a 16-tap filter per shadowed pixel.

cascadeBlend.description: The fraction of each shadow cascade's depth over which it fades into the next, hiding the seam where the shadow's resolution changes. 0 is none; 0.1 to 0.2 is typical (those pixels read two cascades).

PointLight.description:
A light shining in every direction from the entity's position, as three.js PointLight. Its radiance at distance d is color * intensity / d^2, faded smoothly to zero at distance.
Lights are clustered (Forward+): each pixel shades only the lights whose distance reaches it, so hundreds are cheap. Lights out of view are skipped; up to MAX_LIGHTS in view are drawn, and past that (or past what one screen cluster holds, MAX_CLUSTER_LIGHTS) the ones brightest at the camera are kept. Of those in view with castShadow, RenderCapabilities.maxShadowedLights (8 on the full tier, 4 on WebGL2) get shadows, the brightest at the camera first.

distance.description: Where the light reaches zero, as three.js PointLight.distance (never infinite here).

castShadow.description: Cast shadows: six cube faces or two paraboloid hemispheres (RenderOptions.pointShadows).

cookie.description: A light cookie projected all around the light: a cube of six square faces in one texture, stacked top to bottom as +X, -X, +Y, -Y, +Z, -Z (a KTX2 cube's face order and a cube map's orientation, world axes; the texture is six times as tall as it is wide). The light's colour is multiplied by the texel its direction meets, so a lamp behind a pierced shade throws its pattern on the walls. 0 is none.

SpotLight.description: A cone of light along the entity's local -Z, as three.js SpotLight.

intensity.description: The radiance at one metre on the axis.

angle.description: The half-angle of the outer cone, as three.js SpotLight.angle.

penumbra.description: The fraction of the cone over which the light fades out, as three.js SpotLight.penumbra.

cookie.description: A light cookie, as three.js SpotLight.map: the texture projected along the cone (its centre on the axis, its edges at the outer angle, its top towards world up), multiplying the light's colour, so a spot throws a window's bars or a stained-glass pattern. 0 is none. A shadowed spot keeps its shadow over the pattern.

ToneMapping.description: The curve from the lit HDR image to the display, as three.js toneMapping. RenderSettings.toneMapped false clamps instead, whichever is chosen.

x-og-variants.aces: ACES (the fitted filmic curve), as three.js ACESFilmicToneMapping: the default.
x-og-variants.agx: AgX (Blender 4's and three.js AgXToneMapping's fit, base look): bright saturated lights go to white instead of skewing hue, and keep their hue further up than under ACES.
x-og-variants.none: No curve: the exposed linear colour is clamped to 0..1, so 2D colours come out exactly as authored at exposure 1 (the same as toneMapped false).

GraphicsQuality.description: A graphics preset: a row of RenderSettings' quality fields that og.render.applyQuality writes (its doc has the table). The settings screen (og.ui.settingsScreen) offers the three.

x-og-variants.medium: The full frame: every quality field at its default.
x-og-variants.low: The cheapest frame: no rect-light shadows, two shadowed lights, half-size shadow maps, plain fog, hard particles, no screen-space reflections or ambient occlusion, FXAA for MSAA.
x-og-variants.high: The full frame with the shadow maps at twice their side.

QualityPreset.description: The preset RenderSettings' quality fields were last written with (RenderSettings.quality).

x-og-variants.none: No preset applied: the fields are their defaults or the game's own.

RenderSettings.description: The frame's look after lighting: environment light, sky, bloom, exposure metering and tone mapping, and what the frame may cost: the quality fields (rectShadows to msaaSamples) that og.render.applyQuality sets from a graphics preset. Read after each tick; it never feeds back into the simulation. Camera.exposure is the manual exposure.

environmentIntensity.description: The strength of the image-based ambient light from the sky; og.Environment.intensity takes its place while an environment map is set.

sky.description: Draw the procedural sky behind the scene instead of Camera.background (with an og.Environment map set, the map).

bloom.description: Light above the threshold bleeds into its surroundings.

bloomThreshold.description: Brightness after exposure where bloom starts; 1 is display white.

bloomKnee.description: Softens the threshold over threshold plus or minus knee; 0 is a hard cut.

bloomIntensity.description: How much of the blurred light is added back.

autoExposure.description: Meter every frame to middle grey, then apply Camera.exposure as compensation. With both adapt speeds 0 the exposure is the current frame's alone; otherwise it adapts over time like an eye, starting at the metered exposure of the first frame drawn after the first tick (a frame drawn before it, such as the web shell's first frame behind the play gate, meters at once and is never adapted from), so every host draws the same exposures for the same ticks.

adaptSpeedUp.description: How fast auto exposure rises when the view gets darker, in EV per second of game time: each drawn frame moves it by at most the speed times the ticks since the last drawn frame (never the wall clock, so a replay and every host adapt the same, however many frames each drew); 0 is instant. Snapshots and probe sweeps carry the adapted exposure.

adaptSpeedDown.description: How fast auto exposure falls when the view gets brighter, in EV per second of game time; 0 is instant. Eyes adapt to brightness faster than to the dark: 3 down and 1 up is a natural pair.

toneMapped.description: Tone mapping by toneMapping; false clamps, so 2D colours come out exactly as authored at exposure 1.

toneMapping.description: Which curve tone maps the frame while toneMapped is true: aces (the default), agx or none.

exposure.description: A multiplier on every camera's Camera.exposure, as three.js renderer.toneMappingExposure is one for the whole frame: a look's brightness without touching the cameras; 1 leaves them as they are.

decalAtlas.description: The texture Decal components take their uvMin to uvMax region from; 0 draws decals as solid colour.

lodBias.description: A multiplier on every model's projected level-of-detail error when its level is picked (og.Model.lodBias multiplies it again): a level is drawn while its error, measured by the cook against the full mesh, covers less than a pixel on the screen. 1 is the engine's choice, 2 keeps full meshes twice as far, 0.5 simplifies sooner; 0 draws every model at its full mesh.

bakedLighting.description: Draw the baked lighting of the scenes that have it (og bake lightmaps): static models with their lightmaps, everything else inside a LightVolume with its probes. False draws every scene as if unbaked, its ambient light from the sky or the environment map: to compare, or to see the realtime lights alone.

quality.description: The graphics preset og.render.applyQuality last wrote into the quality fields below (rectShadows to msaaSamples), or none. A record for the settings screen and the probe: the renderer reads the fields, never this, so a field the game sets after the preset is drawn as set.

rectShadows.description: Rect lights whose castShadow is on cast their soft shadows; false draws every rect light unshadowed, each keeping its castShadow for when this is on again. The low preset turns it off: a rect light's shadow is the costliest light in the frame.

shadowedLights.description: At most this many point, spot and rect lights cast shadows in a frame, the brightest at the camera kept (RenderCapabilities.shadowedLights caps it); 0 casts none. The directional light's cascades are not counted.

shadowMapScale.description: The shadow maps at this fraction of their full side: the directional light's cascades (2048 texels by default) and the local lights' layers (512), each kept within 64 texels and the device's limit (4096 for the cascades). Changing it makes the maps again at the next frame; RenderCapabilities.shadowMapSize is the cascades' side drawn.

volumetricFog.description: An og.VolumetricFog is drawn lit, with its light shafts; false draws the same medium as plain distance and height fog.

softParticles.description: Particles with a softDistance fade against the scene behind them; false draws them hard-edged and asks no depth prepass for them.

screenSpaceReflections.description: PostEffects.ssr draws (on the full tier); false leaves smooth surfaces the reflection probes' and the environment's reflection. PostEffects keeps its settings either way.

ambientOcclusion.description: PostEffects.ao darkens creases; false draws none. PostEffects keeps its settings either way.

msaaSamples.description: Samples per pixel where the antialiasing multisamples (msaa, the WebGL2 tier's choice; RenderCapabilities.antialias): 4, or 1, which draws FXAA instead. TAA, FXAA and no antialiasing take one sample whatever it says. Changing it makes the multisampled targets and pipelines again at the next frame.

Lut.description: A colour lookup table for PostEffects.lut, from og.load.lut (a `.cube` file).

EnvironmentMap.description: A prefiltered HDR environment map for Environment.map, from og.load.environment (an `.ogt` of `type environment` naming an equirectangular `.hdr` or `.exr`, a KTX2 cube map, or six face images).

ParticleEmitter.description: A particle emitter asset for ParticleSystem.emitter, from og.load.emitter (an `.ogt` of `type particles`).

Environment.description: Image-based light from a cooked HDR environment map instead of the sky, as three.js scene.environment, and the map behind the scene, as scene.background = the environment. Load the map with og.load.environment: the cook has already prefiltered it (GGX levels for reflections from mirror to rough, harmonics for the diffuse light), so setting it costs a few copy passes on any tier, WebGL2 included. Without a map the sky lights the scene as before (og.Sky, a DayNight, or the built-in one). Read after each tick; it never feeds back into the simulation.

map.description: The map from og.load.environment; 0 lights by the sky.

intensity.description: The strength of the map's light on every surface, as three.js scene.environmentIntensity; while a map is set it replaces RenderSettings.environmentIntensity.

rotation.description: Turns the map about +Y, as three.js scene.environmentRotation.y: positive turns what was at +X towards -Z. The light and the background turn together.

background.description: Draw the map behind the scene, as three.js scene.background = the environment (Camera.background, og.Sky and RenderSettings.sky give way); false leaves the background as they set it.

backgroundIntensity.description: Multiplies the map where it is drawn behind the scene, as three.js scene.backgroundIntensity; the light is not changed.

x-og-variants.auto: GTAO on the full tier, SSAO on WebGL2.
x-og-variants.gtao: Ground-truth ambient occlusion (3 slices): the better looking one.
x-og-variants.ssao: Hemisphere SSAO with 8 samples: the cheaper one.

DofQuality.description: How many taps depth of field gathers per pixel.

x-og-variants.high: 48 taps at half resolution: rounder, smoother bokeh.

SpriteBlend.description: How a sprite is blended over what is below it.

x-og-variants.additive: Added (light, fire, magic): order-independent within a layer.

StripBlend.description: How a trail, ribbon or beam is blended.

x-og-variants.alpha: Alpha blended: smoke trails, tyre marks.

PostEffects.description:
The post stack beyond RenderSettings' bloom, exposure and tone mapping, and camera shake. Every effect is off by default (its switch false or its amount 0) and then costs nothing: no pass is recorded. Read after each tick; it never feeds back into the simulation.
Screen-space ambient occlusion, outlines, depth of field, motion blur and god rays run a depth-normal prepass, turned on with them. Grading, vignette, aberration, grain and the flash apply to the display colour after tone mapping; the UI and screen-space sprites (the overlay) come after all of it.

ao.description: Screen-space ambient occlusion: darkens the ambient light in creases and contact areas.

aoRadius.description: The world-space radius searched for occluders.

outline.description: Outlines every opaque surface from depth and normal edges, creases between the faces of one object included (materials with outlineWidth get their own hull outline instead).

outlineWidth.description: Line width in pixels, drawn inside the silhouette.

outlineDepthThreshold.description: The relative depth step that counts as a silhouette (0.04 is 4 %).

outlineNormalThreshold.description: The normal change that counts as a crease (1 - cos of the angle; 0.4 is about 53 degrees).

depthOfField.description: Bokeh depth of field: pixels away from the focus distance blur into discs.

dofFocusDistance.description: The distance from the camera that is sharp.

dofFocusRange.description: The half-width of the sharp band around it.

dofMaxBlur.description: The largest blur radius, as a fraction of the image height (0.012 is about 9 px at 720p).

dofFalloff.description: How quickly blur grows outside the band: full blur focusRange times (1 + falloff) away.

motionBlur.description: Per-object and camera motion blur along the screen-space velocity.

motionBlurShutter.description: The shutter as a fraction of the frame (0.5 is a 180 degree shutter).

godRays.description: Screen-space light shafts from the DirectionalLight (the sun must be in front of the camera).

godRaysDecay.description: How fast the rays fade along their length.

godRaysDensity.description: How far towards the sun each ray samples (a fraction of the distance).

godRaysTint.description: A linear tint on the light the rays carry.

godRaysThreshold.description: Sky brightness (linear, before exposure) below which the sky carries no rays.

glow.description: Order-independent 2D glow: sprites with SpriteDesc.glow (and 2D particles with a glow) are blurred and added back, with or without bloom.

glowIntensity.description: How much of the blurred glow is added back.

lut.description: Colour grading by a lookup table from og.load.lut; 0 is none (and so is a LUT whose streaming group is not resident).

lutIntensity.description: 0 leaves the image as tone mapped, 1 applies the table fully.

vignette.description: Darkened (or tinted) edges of the frame.

vignetteRadius.description: Where darkening starts, as a fraction of the half-diagonal.

vignetteColor.description: The linear colour the edges move towards.

chromaticAberration.description: Red and blue split towards the edges, in pixels at the corners at 720p; 0 is off.

filmGrain.description: Luminance-weighted noise amplitude in display units, a new pattern every tick (0.04 is subtle); 0 is off.

flash.description: A full-screen flash: the display colour mixed towards flashColor by this much (animate it per tick); 0 is off.

shakeTrauma.description: Camera shake held at a fixed level (decay it yourself): 0 none, 1 the most (the amplitude is trauma squared). Prefer og.camera.shake, which decays by itself; the frame shakes by the larger of the two. Smooth value noise by the tick, so a replay shakes the same. Visual only.

shakeMaxOffset.description: The largest offset at trauma 1, as a fraction of the view height.

ssr.description: Screen-space reflections on the full tier: smooth surfaces reflect what the frame already drew by marching the depth-normal prepass along the reflected ray, faded by roughness and at the screen's edges, over the reflection probes and the environment where the ray misses. WebGL2 draws none (RenderCapabilities.ssr is false) and smooth surfaces keep the probes' reflection.

ssrMaxDistance.description: How far a reflected ray marches, in world units.

ssrThickness.description: How far behind the depth buffer a surface is taken to extend: a ray passing behind a surface by less than this hits it.

ssrSteps.description: Steps along each ray (a binary refinement follows the hit).

ssrFade.description: The fraction of the screen's edge, and of the march's end, over which a reflection fades into the probes'.

ssrIntensity.description: How much of the reflection is laid over the frame; 1 is physically weighted by the surface's Fresnel.

custom.description: The custom post passes, in order (og.load.post, `type post` assets): at most RenderCapabilities.maxCustomPosts (8, og-render's MAX_CUSTOM_POSTS). Each runs over the one before it (the lit image for the first), after depth of field and motion blur and before exposure, bloom and the tone curve, and reads the lit image, depth and normals too (any pass turns the prepass on). Write the whole list: `post.custom = [grade, crt]`, `post.custom = []`; a look gives it on one line (`custom "post/tint.ogt" "post/crt.ogt"`). A 0 in it is skipped. Its parameters are set with og.render.setPostParam. A pass the device fails to compile is reported (og.render.postErrors) and skipped.

Palette.description: A colour palette for Stylise.palette, from og.load.palette (a `.hex` or GIMP `.gpl` file of up to 256 colours).

Look.description: A look from og.load.look (an `.ogt` of `type look`): the frame's whole art direction as data, applied with og.render.applyLook.

DitherPattern.description: The threshold pattern Stylise.dither spreads the steps of posterize and palette with.

x-og-variants.none: No dither: every pixel rounds to its nearest step or colour, in flat bands.
x-og-variants.bayer2: Ordered dither by a 2 by 2 Bayer matrix: the coarsest checker, as on early handhelds.
x-og-variants.bayer4: Ordered dither by a 4 by 4 Bayer matrix: the cross-hatched ramps of 8- and 16-bit art.
x-og-variants.bayer8: Ordered dither by an 8 by 8 Bayer matrix: finer ramps with 64 levels between two colours.
x-og-variants.blueNoise: Blue noise: an even grain without a visible grid (a 64 by 64 void-and-cluster tile the engine ships, repeated), fixed per pixel so a still frame does not crawl.
x-og-variants.interleavedGradient: Interleaved gradient noise: computed per pixel without a texture; a finer diagonal structure than blueNoise up close.

StyliseSpace.description: Where Stylise lays a pattern (the paint canvas, the hatching, the halftone).

x-og-variants.screen: Over the frame in logical pixels, as a print or a sheet of paper over the screen: the pattern stays put while the camera moves and the scene slides under it.
x-og-variants.surface: On the surfaces, through the depth-normal prepass's position and normal (three world planes blended by the normal): the pattern sticks to the scene as the camera moves and wraps round forms, a tonal art map's strokes on the objects. Hatching and halftone keep about their pixel spacing by fading between whole octaves of world spacing; the sky keeps the screen pattern. The frame runs the prepass PostEffects.outline uses.
x-og-variants.object: On the surfaces as surface, but in each mesh instance's own space (three planes of the instance blended by its normal, in metres along its axes): a moving, turning or skinned object carries its strokes, dots and grain instead of sliding through them, and keeps them however it is scaled. Terrain, scattered copies and the vertices a material shader moves keep the world pattern, the sky the screen pattern. The frame runs the prepass and an object pass that draws the opaque instances again.

Stylise.description:
Stylisation primitives that move the frame away from the photographic: a low-resolution pixel grid scaled up by whole numbers, fewer tones or a fixed palette through an ordered or blue-noise dither, halftone dots, cross-hatching, painterly smoothing over a canvas, ink lines on tonal edges, flat colour bands by depth, and the vertex snapping, affine textures and coarse depth of early 3D hardware. They compose: a look (og.load.look) sets this with PostEffects and RenderSettings, and the game's art direction is in that data, not in the engine. Every primitive is off at its zero value (0, false, none) and then costs nothing: no pass is recorded and no pipeline is built. RenderCapabilities.stylise names the primitives this renderer draws; a field it does not name is carried and read back but not drawn. Read after each tick; it never feeds back into the simulation.
Order in the frame: depth bands colour the lit scene with the fog, before tone mapping; after tone mapping and PostEffects' grading come paint, hatching, halftone and ink, then posterize and palette quantise through the dither, all at the logical resolution, and the pixel grid is scaled up last. The UI and screen-space sprites are drawn over the scaled frame at the output's resolution, unstylised.

pixelHeight.description: The logical resolution: the scene is rendered this many pixels tall and scaled up to the output by a whole number with nearest filtering, as a low-resolution three.js render target drawn with NearestFilter; 0 renders at the output's resolution. The height sets the scale (pixelUpscale); the width is the output's aspect times the height, rounded, but at most the output's width over the scale, so the last column gives way rather than the scale: 240 rows at 1280x720 are 426.67 columns, rounded to 427, and 427 x 3 = 1281 does not fit, so the grid is 426 x 240 at 3x (1278 x 720, a 1-pixel border each side). Heights that divide the output's evenly fill it: 180 (4x), 240 (3x) and 360 (2x) at 720p, 270 (4x) and 360 (3x) at 1080p.

pixelUpscale.description: The whole-number scale from the logical to the output resolution, a hard request: honoured whenever pixelHeight times it fits the output's height (a smaller scale than the largest leaves the border it implies: 240 lines at 2x in 1280x720 draw 854 x 480 in a 213 x 120 border), else the largest that fits; 0 takes the largest that fits (720 / 240 = 3, 1080 / 240 = 4, rounded down). A frame that does not fill the output is centred with Camera.background round it.

pixelSnap.description: Snap the camera and world sprites to the logical pixel grid, so a moving orthographic camera scrolls by whole pixels and sprites in a 3D world keep their edges (pixel sprites in 3D sets).

posterize.description: Tones per colour channel after tone mapping (2 to 64): smooth gradients become flat steps; 0 is off.

palette.description: Quantise every pixel to the nearest colour of this palette (og.load.palette), measured in a perceptual space after posterize; 0 is none.

dither.description: How the steps of posterize and palette are mixed: none rounds every pixel, an ordered or blue-noise pattern alternates the two nearest steps in proportion.

ditherStrength.description: The dither's amplitude in steps: 1 spreads exactly one step, less keeps flatter bands.

ditherScale.description: The size of one dither cell in logical pixels.

halftone.description: Halftone print: tones become dots on a rotated grid, larger where the image is darker; 0 is off, 1 dots only.

halftoneSize.description: The dot grid's pitch in logical pixels.

halftoneSpace.description: Where the dots lie: screen, a grid over the frame; surface, grids on the surfaces that stay on them as the camera moves and wrap round forms (halftoneSize is then about the pitch in pixels where they lie); object, the same grids in each instance's own space, so a moving object carries its dots.

hatching.description: Pencil or ink cross-hatching from a tonal art map: darker tones add strokes in more directions over a paper-light ground; 0 is off, 1 strokes only.

hatchingScale.description: The spacing of hatch lines in logical pixels.

hatchingLevels.description: How many tones the hatching distinguishes, each adding one stroke direction or density (1 to 6).

hatchingAngle.description: The direction of the first stroke set.

hatchingColor.description: The stroke colour (linear): graphite, sepia or ink.

hatchingSpace.description: Where the strokes lie: screen, stripes over the frame that follow the tone alone; surface, strokes laid on the surfaces that follow the tone and the form, wrapping round curved objects and staying on them as the camera moves (hatchingScale is then about the spacing in pixels where they lie); object, the same strokes in each instance's own space, so a moving or turning object carries its strokes.

hatchingDepth.description: Hatching from luminance and depth: the depth-normal prepass's silhouettes and creases darken the tone the strokes follow, at this strength, so strokes gather along contours and folds as inkDepth inks them (the edges are inkDepthThreshold's and inkNormalThreshold's, found within one stroke spacing). 0 is the tone alone; above 0 the frame runs the prepass PostEffects.outline uses.

paintRadius.description: Painterly smoothing (a Kuwahara filter): flat regions become strokes of one colour this many logical pixels across while edges stay sharp; 0 is off.

paintAnisotropy.description: How far the strokes follow the image's edges: 0 square brush cells, 1 strokes stretched along every contour (an anisotropic Kuwahara).

paintEdgeDarkening.description: Pigment pooling at the edges of colour regions, as wet watercolour dries darker at its rim; 0 is none.

paintBleed.description: Colour bleeding across edges into its neighbours, wet in wet; 0 is none.

paintCanvas.description: A tileable paper or canvas texture (og.load.texture) laid over the frame by paintCanvasStrength; 0 is none.

paintCanvasStrength.description: How much the canvas texture modulates the frame: 0 none, 1 its full grain.

paintCanvasScale.description: Canvas texels per logical pixel, with paintCanvasSpace screen (and on the sky).

paintCanvasSpace.description: Where the canvas lies: screen, over the frame (the scene slides under the paper as the camera moves); surface, on the surfaces, so the grain sticks to the scene, foreshortened with the floor and walls; object, in each instance's own space, so a moving object carries its grain.

paintCanvasWorldScale.description: Canvas texels per metre with paintCanvasSpace surface: 128 repeats a 256-texel canvas every two metres.

ink.description: Ink lines where the tone changes sharply (luminance edges), over every surface, sprite and texture alike: comic and storybook contours without PostEffects.outline's depth prepass. inkDepth adds the prepass's silhouettes and creases.

inkThreshold.description: The luminance step that counts as an edge (0 to 1 in display units): lower draws more lines.

inkWidth.description: The line width in logical pixels.

inkDepth.description: With ink: lines also where the depth-normal prepass breaks (silhouettes against what is behind, creases between faces), at this strength: comic contours round flat colours that luminance alone misses. 0 is luminance only; above 0 the frame runs the prepass PostEffects.outline uses.

inkDepthThreshold.description: With inkDepth: the relative depth step to a farther neighbour that counts as a silhouette (0.04 is 4 %), as PostEffects.outlineDepthThreshold: lower inks smaller steps.

inkNormalThreshold.description: With inkDepth: the normal change between neighbours of about the same depth that counts as a crease (1 - cos of the angle; 0.4 is about 53 degrees), as PostEffects.outlineNormalThreshold: lower inks gentler folds.

depthBands.description: Colour bands by depth (2 to 8): the scene from depthBandsNear to depthBandsFar is cut into this many equal layers, the first in depthBandsNearColor, the last in depthBandsFarColor, those between stepping evenly from one to the other in lightness, chroma and hue (never through grey), for layered-silhouette and stage looks; 0 is off. For side and three-quarter views, where the depth runs across the frame: seen from above the play area lies at one depth and falls in one band.

depthBandsFar.description: Where the last band ends; the last band (the far colour) starts one band's depth before it, and everything beyond it is the far colour too.

depthBandsNearColor.description: The nearest band's colour (linear, before exposure).

depthBandsFarColor.description: The farthest band's colour (linear, before exposure).

depthBandsFlatten.description: How far a band replaces the surfaces' own shading: 1 flat silhouettes in the band's colour; 0 a tint over the lit scene, its colours times the band's at unit luminance (a coloured filter: the shading, the value and the surfaces' own hues show through); between, a mix of the two.

vertexSnap.description: Snap every vertex of the 3D scene to a screen grid this many logical pixels wide, as fixed-point hardware did: geometry jitters by whole steps as it moves; 0 is off.

affineTexturing.description: How far texture coordinates are interpolated without perspective correction: 1 fully affine, so textures warp and swim across large polygons as on early consoles; 0 is off.

depthBits.description: Quantise depth to this many bits, for the coarse depth buffers of early 3D (12 to 16 are period-like: distant surfaces fight); 0 keeps full precision.

MaterialStyle.description: Stylised defaults for every lit material, so a whole scene takes one treatment without editing each material: toon shading and its ramp, a coloured shadow side, rim light, outlines whose width falls off with distance, and flat facets. Each applies to a material (og.render.standardMaterial or a loaded glTF's) that leaves that field at its own default; unlit and shader materials, materials with StandardMaterialDesc.styled false, sprites and the UI are untouched, and toon passes by a material with a MeshPhysicalMaterial lobe (clearcoat, sheen, transmission, iridescence, anisotropy, ior), which keeps its physical shading. All off (false, 0) is no change. A look sets it; RenderCapabilities.stylise names what this renderer draws. Read after each tick; it never feeds back into the simulation.

toon.description: Cel shading for every lit material, as StandardMaterialDesc.toon: light quantised by the ramp, hard highlights. A material with a physical lobe (clearcoat, transmission and the rest) keeps its physical shading; set its own toon to make it toon anyway.

gradientMap.description: The toon ramp for materials without their own (StandardMaterialDesc.gradientMap, og.load.texture): its first row maps the light's angle to the light received, read without filtering; 0 is three built-in bands.

shadowTint.description: The colour the shadowed side of a toon or lit surface moves towards instead of black (linear): the cool or warm shadow of illustration.

shadowTintAmount.description: How far shadowed light moves towards shadowTint; 0 is off.

rimColor.description: Rim (fresnel) light for materials without their own (linear).

rimIntensity.description: The rim light's strength; 0 is none.

rimPower.description: How tight the rim is (higher: thinner).

outlineColor.description: The outline colour for materials without their own (linear).

outlineWidth.description: The outline width in pixels at outlineDistance for materials without their own; 0 is none. A hull outline (StandardMaterialDesc.outlineWidth): silhouettes and creases against other objects, never the faces of one, so voxel and flat-shaded models stay clean. A surface seen at a grazing angle is lined only where it ends: a 1,600 m ground under a chase camera keeps its far edge and nothing else (no band along the horizon).

outlineDistance.description: The distance at which outlines are outlineWidth wide: nearer they grow, up to four times outlineWidth, farther they thin in proportion (an inked look keeps line weight by depth); 0 keeps every outline outlineWidth wide.

flatShading.description: Shade every lit material with face normals, as StandardMaterialDesc.flatShading: visible facets for low-poly, paper-craft and voxel looks.

LookInfo.description: A loaded look: where it came from and what applying it sets.

name.description: Its name (the file's `name`, else its file name without `.ogt`).

extends.description: The looks it builds on, nearest first: asset ids under assets/ and built-in preset slugs.

resources.description: The resources it sets, by IDL name (RenderSettings, PostEffects, Stylise, MaterialStyle, Fog, Sky, Environment). Applying it replaces each of them whole: the fields the look names take its values, the rest their defaults.

style.description: The UI style its `ui` line names (a game's own or a built-in by slug), loaded with it; applying the look configures the UI with it.

antialias.description: The antialiasing it asks for. GameDesc.look's is the renderer's when GameDesc.render leaves antialias out; a running renderer keeps its method.

Lighting2D.description: 2D lighting of the sprite layers minLayer to maxLayer (sprites, 2D particles and og.Tilemap layers there, a map layer unless its `lit` property is false): their colour is multiplied by ambient plus every Light2D reaching the pixel, shadowed by Occluder2Ds and sprites with castShadow. Other layers (and the overlay) are drawn as authored. Off by default.

ambient.description: Light everywhere (0 is darkness outside the lights).

maxLayer.description: The highest lit sprite layer (above it: UI and HUD layers stay unlit).

resolution.description: The light map's resolution as a fraction of the target.
