Light2D.description: A light in the 2D plane at the entity's position (z ignored): color times intensity at its centre, falling to zero at radius with (1 - d/r)^falloff, shadowed by occluders when castShadows. Lighting2D.enabled turns 2D lighting on; at most 64 are drawn.

radius.description: Where the light reaches zero, in world units.

sourceRadius.description: The light's own size: larger gives softer shadows.

castShadows.description: Occluders between the light and a pixel shade it.

Occluder2D.description: A rectangle that blocks 2D light (walls, crates, characters), centred on the entity's position and turned with it about z. Pixels inside it are not shadowed by it. At most 128 are drawn.

Decal.description: A projected decal (scorch marks, blood, posters, bullet holes): the entity's unit box (-0.5 to 0.5 on each axis, scaled by its Transform) projected along its local -Z onto every lit opaque surface inside it, shaded with the surface. Its image is the uvMin to uvMax region of RenderSettings.decalAtlas (a solid colour without one). At most 32 are drawn.

color.description: A linear colour multiplied with the atlas.

uvMin.description: The atlas region's top-left corner, v down.

uvMax.description: The atlas region's bottom-right corner, v down.

emissive.description: Linear light added where the decal covers (glowing runes, lava).

roughness.description: The surface roughness under the decal; -1 keeps the surface's.

angleFade.description: Surfaces turned further than this from the projection direction are not covered (the last 15 degrees fade).

ParticleSystem.description: Emits particles from an og.load.emitter asset at the entity's MatrixWorld. Particles are simulated by the renderer from (seed, startTick, the tick), so they are deterministic and replay, and never feed back into the simulation: compute on the full tier, the CPU on WebGL2, identical either way.

seed.description: The random seed: systems with different seeds differ.

startTick.description: The tick emission started: write the tick (`time.tick`, `world.tick`) to fire a one-shot burst, or to restart one. Its default, PARTICLES_ARMED, is never written: a looping emitter emits as if started at tick 0, while a one-shot (`looping false`) stays armed and emits nothing until a tick is written, so effects spawned ahead of their first use wait.

stopTick.description: The tick emission stops (the particles live out); 0 keeps emitting while the emitter loops.

visible.description: Whether it is drawn (a hidden system loses its particles).

layers.description: Three.js layers, as Mesh.layers: its particles (billboards and 2D sprite particles alike) are drawn by the cameras whose masks share a bit with it (og.Camera, og.CameraView, og.Mirror).

Trail.description: A streak behind the entity: its world positions over the last `lifetime` seconds as a camera-facing strip, from widthStart and color at the head to widthEnd and colorEnd at the tail.

lifetime.description: How long a position stays in the trail.

minDistance.description: A new point is kept when the head has moved this far.

color.description: The linear colour at the head; above 1 blooms.

colorEnd.description: The linear colour at the tail.

texture.description: A texture along the strip; 0 is solid.

uvTile.description: The texture repeats every this many world units; 0 stretches it once over the length.

layered.description: Draw it in the 2D sprite order at `layer` (a sprite's trail over a tile background) instead of with the 3D scene.

layer.description: With layered: the sprite layer it is drawn in, before that layer's sprites.

Beam.description: A strip from the entity's position to `end` whose texture scrolls with the tick: lasers, tethers, lightning (jitter).

end.description: The far end, in world space.

texture.description: A texture along the beam; 0 is solid.

tile.description: Texture repeats per world unit along the beam.

scroll.description: Texture scroll in repeats per second.

segments.description: Segments: 1 is straight, more let jitter bend it.

jitter.description: Sideways jitter in world units, new every tick (lightning).

RibbonDesc.description: An explicit camera-facing strip through points, drawn this frame only (immediate mode, as og.render.sprite): submit it every tick it should show.

points.description: The points, in order (at least two).

texture.description: A texture along the strip; null is solid.

uvTile.description: The texture repeats every this many world units; 0 stretches it once.

TextDesc.description: A line or block of MSDF text in the world's xy plane facing +z, drawn this frame only (immediate mode: submit it every tick it should show).

font.description: The font from og.load.font; null draws nothing.

text.description: The text; `\n` starts a new line.

position.description: The baseline origin of the first line.

size.description: The em size in world units.

layer.description: Draw order among sprites and text; higher draws on top.

align.description: How each line sits on `position`: start puts its left end there, center its middle, end its right end.

outline.description: World text: an outline around the glyphs, as a fraction (0 to 1) of the widest the font's distance range allows (a font cooked with a larger px_range takes thicker outlines).

screen.description: Draw in screen space over the finished frame: position is the first baseline's origin in CSS pixels from the top left, y down, size in CSS pixels, rotation clockwise. With og.ui: under every UI element at a layer up to UI_LAYER (1000), over every one above it.

clip.description: Screen text: cut to [x, y, width, height] in CSS pixels, per pixel; null draws it whole.

TextMeasureDesc.description: Text to measure with og.render.measureText, laid out as og.render.text lays it out.

text.description: The text; `\n` starts a new line.

size.description: The em size in world units.

TextMetrics.description: The extent of a laid-out text, in world units.

height.description: Lines times the font's line height.

SpriteDesc.description: A textured or solid quad in the world's xy plane facing +z, drawn this frame only (immediate mode, as og.render.text): submit it every tick it should show. Sprites and text are sorted by layer and drawn over the 3D scene.

texture.description: The texture from og.load.texture; null draws a solid quad of the colour.

array.description: Draw from a layer of this texture array (og.load.textureArray) instead of `texture`: every sprite of one array is one draw whichever layer each shows, so a flipbook's frames packed as layers batch across frames. World and screen sprites alike, with flash, glow, blend and 2D lighting as a textured sprite. null uses `texture`.

arrayLayer.description: With `array`: the layer drawn, 0 to the array's layers minus 1 (refused past it). `uv` is the region within the layer.

anchor.description: The point of the quad at `position`, as a fraction of its size from the bottom-left corner: (0.5, 0.5) is the centre.

color.description: A linear colour multiplied with the texture.

uv.description: The texture region drawn, [u0, v0, u1, v1] with v down; null is the whole texture (a sheet's frame for animation).

layer.description: Draw order among sprites and text; higher draws on top.

flash.description: A hit flash: the colour mixed towards flashColor by this much, keeping the alpha.

glow.description: Strength in the 2D glow buffer (PostEffects.glow); 0 none.

castShadow.description: Block 2D light (Lighting2D) with the sprite's rectangle.

dropShadow.description: A drop shadow this dark (0 none, 0.5 typical): the sprite's shape in black, flattened along the sun (the first og.DirectionalLight) onto the ground under it (dropShadowHeight, or the og.Terrain there), drawn before every sprite of its layer: pixel sprites standing in a 3D set cast shadows that agree with it. Where the ground already lies in the sun's cascaded shadow the drop shadow fades, so a shadow inside a shadow is no darker. None with the sun below the horizon; at most five times the sprite's height long under a low one. World sprites with a perspective camera over the xz ground; a 2D camera sees the ground edge on.

dropShadowHeight.description: The height of the level ground the drop shadow lies on (a floor, a deck, a step). Where an og.Terrain under the sprite's anchor is higher, the shadow lies on the terrain instead, on the plane fitted to its slope under the shadow, or bent over a hollow or a ridge narrower than the shadow (the terrain's heights under a 4 x 2 grid of the shadow's cells). 0 with no terrain is the ground plane y = 0.

toneMapped.description: As three.js Material.toneMapped: true draws the sprite into the lit scene, carried by exposure (auto exposure included), bloom and the tone curve like any surface. false keeps its colours as given: still placed in the world, depth tested and sorted with the other sprites, but shown unexposed and uncurved (clamped to 0 to 1), outside bloom and fog; the grade, vignette, grain and screen flash still apply. For world UI that must read the same at noon and at dusk: speech bubbles, name tags, markers. Alpha blending only: an additive sprite adds light and is always tone mapped.

flipX.description: Mirror the region left to right.

flipY.description: Mirror the region top to bottom.

sortY.description: Within its layer, draw by y: lower on the screen draws in front (top-down games).

slice.description: Nine-slice: [left, top, right, bottom] insets in texture pixels of the region; the corners keep their size (sliceScale world units per pixel), edges and centre stretch. null draws it whole.

sliceScale.description: Nine-slice: world units (CSS pixels on screen) per texture pixel of the insets.

screen.description: Draw in screen space over the finished frame instead of the world: position x, y in CSS pixels from the top left with y down, width and height in CSS pixels, anchor from the top left, rotation clockwise; never tone mapped, blurred or depth tested (a HUD). flash, glow, blend and castShadow apply to world sprites only. With og.ui: under every UI element at a layer up to UI_LAYER (1000), over every one above it.

clip.description: Screen sprites: cut to [x, y, width, height] in CSS pixels; null draws it whole.

Sprite.description:
A sprite drawn every frame at the entity's MatrixWorld (its xy and z, its rotation about z; its scale multiplies width and height, so squash and stretch is a tween of og.Transform.scale). With an og.Flipbook on the entity, the texture (or an `array true` sheet's texture array layer), region and anchor come from the flipbook's current frame.
Sorted with the immediate sprites and text by layer, then (sortY) by y, then texture: one draw per run of one texture. Tile layers draw before the sprites of their layer.

texture.description: The texture (og.load.texture); 0 draws a solid quad of the colour.

array.description: Draw from a layer of this texture array (og.load.textureArray) instead of `texture`; 0 uses `texture`. Every sprite of one array is one draw whichever layer each shows. While the array's streaming group is not resident the sprite draws nothing.

arrayLayer.description: With `array`: the layer drawn (past the last layer, the last). uvMin and uvMax are the region within the layer; a nine-slice measures the layer.

width.description: Its width in world units (times Transform.scale.x).

height.description: Its height in world units (times Transform.scale.y).

anchor.description: The point of the quad at the entity's position, as a fraction from the bottom-left corner: (0.5, 0) stands it on its feet. A flipbook frame's pivot replaces it.

color.description: A linear colour multiplied with the texture.

uvMin.description: The texture region's top-left corner, v down.

uvMax.description: The texture region's bottom-right corner, v down.

layer.description: Draw order among sprites, tiles and text; higher draws on top.

sortY.description: Within its layer, lower y draws in front: top-down characters, props and trees overlap by their feet.

flipX.description: Mirror left to right (a character facing left).

flash.description: A hit flash: the colour mixed towards flashColor by this much (og.tween.flash fades it out).

glow.description: Strength in the 2D glow buffer (PostEffects.glow); 0 none.

castShadow.description: Block 2D light (Lighting2D) with the sprite's rectangle.

sliceX.description: Nine-slice: the left and right insets in texture pixels of the region (0 0 with sliceY 0 0 draws it whole). World panels, health bars, speech bubbles.

sliceY.description: Nine-slice: the top and bottom insets in texture pixels.

sliceScale.description: Nine-slice: world units per texture pixel of the insets.

shadow.description: A soft blob shadow on the ground under the sprite's anchor, this dark (0 none, 0.4 typical), drawn under every sprite of its layer.

shadowSize.description: The blob's width and height; 0 0 is 0.8 by 0.3 of the sprite's width.

shadowOffset.description: The blob's centre relative to the anchor.

dropShadow.description: A drop shadow this dark (0 none, 0.5 typical): the sprite's shape flattened along the sun onto the ground under it (dropShadowHeight, or the og.Terrain there), faded where that ground already lies in the sun's shadow, drawn before every sprite of its layer (SpriteDesc.dropShadow): pixel sprites standing in a 3D set.

dropShadowHeight.description: The height of the level ground the drop shadow lies on; where an og.Terrain under the anchor is higher, the terrain (SpriteDesc.dropShadowHeight).

toneMapped.description: As three.js Material.toneMapped: false keeps the sprite's colours as given, outside exposure, bloom, fog and the tone curve, still placed and depth tested in the world (SpriteDesc.toneMapped): speech bubbles and markers that must not blow out at dusk. Alpha blending only.

layers.description: Three.js layers, as Mesh.layers: a world sprite is drawn by the cameras whose masks share a bit with it (a screen sprite draws on every camera's frame).

Afterimage.description: Ghosts of the entity's og.Sprite: every `interval` ticks its pose (position, rotation, scale, frame, flips) is kept, and the last `count` are drawn behind it, fading from `opacity` to 0, tinted by color. A dash, a speed-up, a teleport. The history is world state (the og.sprite state block).

color.description: A linear tint (above 1 with additive, a glow).

additive.description: Add the ghosts instead of blending them.

active.description: Record new ghosts; false lets the existing ones fade out.

FloatingTextDesc.description: A damage number or pickup text that pops at a point, rises, spreads and fades by itself (no per-tick submission). Deterministic: its drift comes from the tick and its order, and it is world state (the og.sprite state block).

text.description: The text, such as `-12` or `+1 key`.

position.description: Where it appears (above a hit, usually).

font.description: The font; null uses the UI's body font.

size.description: The em size in world units.

outline.description: The outline's width as a fraction of the font's distance range (0 none).

rise.description: How far it climbs over its life.

spread.description: The largest sideways drift, left or right.

fade.description: The last part of its life it fades over.

pop.description: How much bigger it starts, settling to its size in the first fifth of its life.

crit.description: A critical hit: critScale times bigger, a stronger pop.

BoxGeometryDesc.description: A box centred at the origin, as three.js BoxGeometry(width, height, depth).

uvRepeat.description: How many times a texture repeats across it, along u and v: its UVs run 0 to uvRepeat instead of 0 to 1 (three.js texture.repeat, here on the geometry; material textures sample with repeat wrapping). A ground grid every 10 m on a 1,600 m plane is uvRepeat 160 160.

PlaneGeometryDesc.description: A rectangle in the xy plane facing +z, centred at the origin, as three.js PlaneGeometry(width, height); turn it -pi/2 about x for a floor.

uvRepeat.description: How many times a texture repeats across it, along u and v: its UVs run 0 to uvRepeat instead of 0 to 1 (three.js texture.repeat, here on the geometry; material textures sample with repeat wrapping). A ground grid every 10 m on a 1,600 m plane is uvRepeat 160 160.

SphereGeometryDesc.description: A UV sphere centred at the origin, as three.js SphereGeometry(radius, widthSegments, heightSegments).

radius.description: Its radius.

uvRepeat.description: How many times a texture repeats across it, along u and v: its UVs run 0 to uvRepeat instead of 0 to 1 (three.js texture.repeat, here on the geometry; material textures sample with repeat wrapping). A ground grid every 10 m on a 1,600 m plane is uvRepeat 160 160.

RenderCapabilities.description: What the renderer can do on this device. Backend limits are reported here, never by missing members.

compute.description: Whether compute passes run (GPU culling, GPU particles).

antialias.description: The antialiasing the device resolved RenderOptions.antialias to.

maxLights.description: How many point and spot lights one frame draws (MAX_LIGHTS on every tier).

maxShadowedLights.description: How many point and spot lights cast shadows in one frame (8 on the full tier, 4 on WebGL2); past it, the shadowed lights brightest at the camera keep theirs.

pointShadows.description: How point lights' shadows are stored on this device: cube or paraboloid (what RenderOptions.pointShadows resolved to).

width.description: The render target width in device pixels.

height.description: The render target height in device pixels.

stylise.description: The Stylise and MaterialStyle primitives this renderer draws, by group: pixel, posterize, palette, dither, halftone, hatching, paint, ink, inkDepth, depthBands, retro3d, surfaceSpace (paintCanvasSpace, hatchingSpace and halftoneSpace surface) and objectSpace (the same object) of Stylise; toon, shadowTint, rim, outline, outlineDistance and flatShading of MaterialStyle. A look that uses one this list lacks still applies; that primitive is not drawn.

ssr.description: Whether PostEffects.ssr draws: true on the full tier, false on WebGL2, where smooth surfaces reflect the reflection probes and the environment instead.

reflectionProbes.description: How many og.ReflectionProbe components one frame samples (MAX_REFLECTION_PROBES on every tier).

renderTargetDepth.description: Whether a render target made with `depth` gets its view's depth drawn: true on every tier with a renderer (WebGPU, Vulkan, Metal and WebGL2 alike), false without one. The depth comes from the view's own depth prepass of its opaque meshes into a linear-depth colour target, never from its depth buffer, which WebGL2 cannot read in a shader.

maxRenderTargetSize.description: The largest side of a render target (the device's largest 2D texture).

maxCustomPosts.description: The most custom post passes a frame runs: 8 on every tier, PostEffects.custom's capacity.

volumetricFog.description: How Fog.volumetric is drawn on this device: a froxel grid (the full tier) or a raymarch along each pixel's view ray (WebGL2), each lit by the sun through its shadows and by the point, spot and rect lights around each sample (up to volumetricLights of them) through their shadows and cookies.

volumetricLights.description: The most point, spot and rect lights that light one sample of Fog.volumetric: those of its screen cluster, MAX_CLUSTER_LIGHTS (64) in the froxel grid, 8 in WebGL2's raymarch, the brightest at the camera first.

maxLightCookies.description: The most light cookie layers one frame draws (24 on every tier): a SpotLight.cookie takes one, a PointLight.cookie six (its cube's faces), and a texture several lights of one kind share takes its layers once. Cookies past it, in the order of their lights' entities, are not drawn: those lights shine without them, and the log names them in a warning.

gpuTimestamps.description: Whether the device times each render pass on the GPU (timestamp queries: Vulkan, Metal and D3D12 adapters that have them, WebGPU with `timestamp-query`; never WebGL2, and never in a publish build, which leaves the queries out): ProbeTimings.gpuPasses and the trace's gpu thread are filled only where it is true.

spriteAnisotropy.description: The anisotropic filtering of sprites and og.ui's images (text is not filtered anisotropically: its distance field would lose its edge): 16 where the device filters anisotropically (WebGPU, Vulkan, Metal, WebGL2 with EXT_texture_filter_anisotropic), 1 where it has none and on a software rasterizer (the vulkan-cpu tier: lavapipe's anisotropic filter softens even an image drawn 1:1), 0 without a renderer. Above 1, an image squeezed along one axis keeps the other axis's detail: a style's nine-slice middle squeezed into a short button keeps its outline as crisp as the corners. At 1 the squeezed piece reads a smaller mip level and blurs; og.ui bounds a middle's squeeze at twice its art, so the outline there is one mip level softer than the corners.

world3d.description: Whether the renderer draws the 3D world subsystems: terrain, planar water (og.Water), the 3D fluids, scattered copies and volumetric fog. False in the 2D profile's publish and lanes modules, which leave them out (a scene's are not drawn, og.terrain's calls and a SHAPE_HEIGHTFIELD collider answer a refusal naming this field, and `og build --publish` refuses a 2D project whose scenes hold og.Terrain, og.TerrainScatter, og.Water, og.WaterSurface or og.Fluid3D, by scene file and line); true in the 3D modules, the dev module and the native host.

ReflectionProbeMode.description: When a reflection probe's cube is rendered.

x-og-variants.baked: Once: read from the project's cook cache when `og bake probes` wrote it there, otherwise rendered on its first frame and kept. Static rooms.
x-og-variants.realtime: Again every `interval` ticks, so moving things show in it (a cost per update of six faces).

ReflectionProbe.description: A local reflection: a cube of what is around the entity's position, sampled by every lit surface inside its box with box projection (the reflected ray meets the box, so a room's walls reflect where they are, not at infinity) and blended with the environment map over blendDistance at the box's faces. Interiors that the sky must not light: a chrome sphere in a room shows the room. Overlapping probes: the smallest wins. The cube is rendered from the probe's position without it (nothing is drawn twice) and without the probes' own reflections.

size.description: The box's full extents in world units, centred on the entity (its rotation is ignored: the box is axis-aligned).

resolution.description: The side of each cube face in texels; it is rounded to a power of two.

mode.description: baked (rendered once, or loaded from `og bake probes`) or realtime (every interval ticks).

interval.description: With realtime: ticks between updates (1 is every frame).

intensity.description: A multiplier on the probe's light.

blendDistance.description: The distance inside the box's faces over which the probe fades into the environment map.

Shader.description: A material shader from og.load.shader (an `.ogt` of `type shader`): WGSL hooks of the lit shader, or with `mode full` its own vertex and fragment entries, and the parameters they read.

BufferGeometryDesc.description:
Geometry from attribute arrays, as three.js BufferGeometry with its attributes set: one item per vertex in each array, triangles three indices each (or, with no indices, every three vertices).
Missing normals are computed, as three.js computeVertexNormals (each vertex the area-weighted sum of its triangles' normals: shared vertices shade smooth, an unindexed geometry flat); missing tangents are generated when a normal map needs them. An unindexed geometry whose vertex count is not a multiple of three has no triangles: it draws nothing as an og.Mesh and is a vertex set for og.Lines and og.Points.

positions.description: The vertex positions, x y z per vertex (three.js `position`); at least one vertex.

normals.description: Unit normals, x y z per vertex; null computes them.

uvs.description: Texture coordinates, u v per vertex, v down the image (glTF's, as og-render's); null is 0 0.

colors.description: Linear vertex colours, r g b or r g b a per vertex, multiplied into the material's colour (three.js `color` with vertexColors); null is white.

tangents.description: Tangents, x y z w per vertex (glTF's: w the bitangent's sign); null generates them.

indices.description: Triangles, three vertex indices each, counter-clockwise seen from the front; null takes every three vertices as one.

dynamic.description: Whether og.render.updateGeometry may rewrite it (a mesh made each tick: water, a deforming terrain, a trail of geometry). A static geometry is refused there.

physics.description: Register it as a physics mesh too, so an og.Collider with it as `mesh` (SHAPE_MESH or SHAPE_CONVEX) collides with what is drawn; equivalent to og.physics.setMesh with its positions and indices. An update re-registers it.

min.description: The bounds' least corner in the geometry's own space, as three.js boundingBox.min.

CylinderGeometryDesc.description: A cylinder (or a truncated cone) along +Y centred at the origin, as three.js CylinderGeometry(radiusTop, radiusBottom, height, radialSegments, heightSegments, openEnded, thetaStart, thetaLength).

thetaStart.description: Where the side starts around y, from +Z towards +X.

thetaLength.description: How far around the side goes; 2 pi is whole.

ConeGeometryDesc.description: A cone along +Y centred at the origin, its tip up, as three.js ConeGeometry(radius, height, radialSegments, heightSegments, openEnded).

radius.description: The base's radius.

CapsuleGeometryDesc.description: A capsule along +Y centred at the origin, as three.js CapsuleGeometry(radius, height, capSegments, radialSegments, heightSegments): a cylinder of `height` between two hemispheres, `height + 2 radius` long in all (an og.Collider capsule of halfHeight height / 2 and that radius matches it).

radius.description: The radius.

TorusGeometryDesc.description: A torus in the xy plane around +Z, as three.js TorusGeometry(radius, tube, radialSegments, tubularSegments, arc).

radius.description: From the centre to the tube's centre.

arc.description: How far around the ring goes.

RingGeometryDesc.description: A flat ring in the xy plane facing +Z, as three.js RingGeometry(innerRadius, outerRadius, thetaSegments, phiSegments, thetaStart, thetaLength).

CircleGeometryDesc.description: A disc (or a sector) in the xy plane facing +Z, as three.js CircleGeometry(radius, segments, thetaStart, thetaLength): a 2D polygon's simplest shape.

radius.description: The radius.

TubeGeometryDesc.description: A tube along a curve, as three.js TubeGeometry(curve, tubularSegments, radius, radialSegments, closed): its rings are evenly spaced along the curve's length (three.js getPointAt), u runs along it, v around. The curve is `path` when set (an og.path, whatever its kind, followed exactly: a scene's or a timeline's path becomes a tube), otherwise new CatmullRomCurve3(points, closed, 'centripetal') through `points`, which may come from anywhere: a rope's points, a spline a tool made.

points.description: The points the curve passes through, in order (at least two), when `path` is 0.

path.description: A path (og.path.create, or a scene's `path` by og.path.find) the tube follows instead of the points: its own curve, kind and closed flag (`closed` is the path's then). 0 uses the points.

radius.description: The tube's radius.

closed.description: Join the last point back to the first.

ShapePoints.description: A shape as points, what og.Shape.extractPoints returns and what shapeGeometry, extrudeGeometry and sweepGeometry read: the outline, then each hole. A repeated closing point is dropped, as three.js drops it.

ShapeGeometryDesc.description: A flat shape with holes in the xy plane facing +Z, as three.js ShapeGeometry(shapes, curveSegments): triangulated by earcut (three.js's own port), the outline made clockwise and the holes counter-clockwise first, so its vertices and triangles are three.js's for the same shape. uvs are world x and y (v flipped to run down the image).

shapes.description: One og.Shape (an og.Path2 is a shape without holes), a list of them, or the outline's points. Without it, three.js's default triangle (0, 0.5), (-0.5, -0.5), (0.5, -0.5).

curveSegments.description: Points per curve when an og.Shape's curves are flattened (three.js extractPoints(curveSegments); an ellipse takes twice as many, a spline as many per point).

uvRepeat.description: How many times a texture repeats across it, along u and v: its UVs scaled by uvRepeat (three.js texture.repeat, here on the geometry; material textures sample with repeat wrapping).

physics.description: Register it as a physics mesh too (BufferGeometryDesc.physics).

dynamic.description: Whether og.render.updateGeometry may rewrite it later (BufferGeometryDesc.dynamic).

ExtrudeGeometryDesc.description: Shapes pushed along +Z, or along a path, as three.js ExtrudeGeometry(shapes, options) with its option names and defaults: a closed solid, its lids from earcut and its walls ring by ring, rounded by a bevel of bevelSegments rings at each face. Unindexed as three.js's (every triangle its own vertices, flat normals), three.js's vertex order and counts; uvs from three.js's WorldUVGenerator (v flipped to run down the image).

shapes.description: One og.Shape, a list of them, or the outline's points. Without it, three.js's default square of side 1.

depth.description: How far the shape is pushed along +Z (without extrudePath).

steps.description: Rings along the depth or the path.

bevelEnabled.description: Round the edges of both faces.

bevelThickness.description: How far the bevel reaches beyond each face, along z.

bevelSize.description: How far the bevel reaches out from the outline. Null or unset, bevelThickness - 0.1, as three.js derives it (0.1 at the default thickness, 0 at a thickness of 0.1).

bevelOffset.description: How far the bevel starts out from the outline.

curveSegments.description: Points per curve when an og.Shape's curves are flattened.

extrudePath.description: A path (og.path.create or og.path.find) to extrude along instead of +Z: the shape's x along the path's normal and y along its binormal (three.js's Frenet frames), steps rings evenly spaced along it. A path turns the bevel off, as three.js. 0 extrudes along +Z.

uvRepeat.description: How many times a texture repeats across it, along u and v: its UVs scaled by uvRepeat (three.js texture.repeat, here on the geometry; material textures sample with repeat wrapping).

physics.description: Register it as a physics mesh too.

dynamic.description: Whether og.render.updateGeometry may rewrite it later.

LatheGeometryDesc.description: A profile turned round +Y, as three.js LatheGeometry(points, segments, phiStart, phiLength): vases, bottles, columns, wheels. three.js's vertices, indices and smooth normals; u round the axis, v along the profile (flipped to run down the image). A whole turn's seam meets exactly.

points.description: The profile, x the distance from the axis and y the height, in order (at least two). Without it, three.js's default (0, -0.5), (0.5, 0), (0, 0.5).

phiStart.description: Where the turn starts, from +Z towards +X.

phiLength.description: How far it turns; 2 pi is whole (clamped to it).

uvRepeat.description: How many times a texture repeats across it, along u and v: its UVs scaled by uvRepeat (three.js texture.repeat, here on the geometry; material textures sample with repeat wrapping).

physics.description: Register it as a physics mesh too.

dynamic.description: Whether og.render.updateGeometry may rewrite it later.

PolyhedronGeometryDesc.description: A polyhedron from vertices and faces, every face subdivided `detail` times and every vertex pushed onto the sphere of `radius`, as three.js PolyhedronGeometry(vertices, indices, radius, detail): unindexed, flat normals at detail 0 and the sphere's above, three.js's spherical uvs.

vertices.description: The corners, x y z each (three.js's flat array).

indices.description: The faces, three corner indices each, counter-clockwise seen from outside.

radius.description: The sphere the vertices are pushed onto.

detail.description: Subdivisions of each face: (detail + 1)² triangles a face.

uvRepeat.description: How many times a texture repeats across it, along u and v: its UVs scaled by uvRepeat (three.js texture.repeat, here on the geometry; material textures sample with repeat wrapping).

physics.description: Register it as a physics mesh too.

dynamic.description: Whether og.render.updateGeometry may rewrite it later.

SolidGeometryDesc.description: A regular solid, as three.js IcosahedronGeometry, DodecahedronGeometry, OctahedronGeometry and TetrahedronGeometry(radius, detail): PolyhedronGeometryDesc with the solid's own vertices and faces. An icosahedron at detail 2 or more is a sphere with even triangles.

radius.description: The radius.

uvRepeat.description: How many times a texture repeats across it, along u and v: its UVs scaled by uvRepeat (three.js texture.repeat, here on the geometry; material textures sample with repeat wrapping).

physics.description: Register it as a physics mesh too.

dynamic.description: Whether og.render.updateGeometry may rewrite it later.

SweepKey.description: A value at a fraction of a sweep's path: linear between keys, held before the first and past the last.

t.description: The fraction of the path's length, 0 to 1.

SweepGeometryDesc.description: A section swept along a path, scaled and twisted over it: horns, tusks, handles, blades, tapered pipes, twisted columns (img2threejs's tapered sweep; three.js has no class for it). The section's x lies along the path's normal and y along its binormal (three.js's Frenet frames), rings evenly spaced along the path's length; u runs along the path, v round the section (flipped to run down the image), the sides smooth. An open path's ends are capped.

section.description: The section's outline: an og.Shape or og.Path2 (flattened by curveSegments; holes are not swept) or its points, at least three, either winding.

steps.description: Rings along the path, less one.

scale.description: The section's scale over the path (none: 1 throughout). A horn: [{ t: 0, value: 1 }, { t: 1, value: 0.05 }].

twist.description: The section's turn round the path over its length, in radians (none: 0).

caps.description: Close the ends of an open path.

curveSegments.description: Points per curve when an og.Shape section is flattened.

uvRepeat.description: How many times a texture repeats across it, along u and v: its UVs scaled by uvRepeat (three.js texture.repeat, here on the geometry; material textures sample with repeat wrapping).

physics.description: Register it as a physics mesh too.

dynamic.description: Whether og.render.updateGeometry may rewrite it later.

MirrorAxis.description: The world axis a part is mirrored along, after its placement.

x-og-variants.x: x negated: the mirror image across the yz plane.
x-og-variants.y: y negated: across the xz plane.
x-og-variants.z: z negated: across the xy plane.

GeometryPart.description: A geometry placed as an Object3D is (scale, then rotate, then move), then mirrored: one part of og.render.mergeGeometries or an operand of og.render.csgGeometry.

geometry.description: Any geometry: made, a primitive or a loaded glTF's.

scale.description: Its scale (a negative component mirrors it as `mirror` does).

mirror.description: Mirror it along a world axis after placing it: a symmetric prop is one half twice, the second mirrored.

CsgOp.description: A boolean operation on two solids.

x-og-variants.subtract: What of a is not in b: a - b (holes, notches, a dice's pips).

CsgGeometryDesc.description: Two closed geometries combined by a boolean operation, each placed first: a box with a hole bored through it, a dice, a window cut in a wall. The result is closed when both are (every edge shared by two triangles, wound opposite), every piece keeps its source's normals, uvs and colours (b's turned inside out where it is subtracted). Where a plane side or an edge crossing is decided, the decision is exact (Shewchuk's predicates), so every host makes the same cuts; faces that coincide keep one copy or none, as the operation says.

uvRepeat.description: How many times a texture repeats across it, along u and v: its UVs scaled by uvRepeat (three.js texture.repeat, here on the geometry; material textures sample with repeat wrapping).

physics.description: Register it as a physics mesh too.

dynamic.description: Whether og.render.updateGeometry may rewrite it later.

MergeGeometriesDesc.description: Geometries placed and merged into one, as three.js BufferGeometryUtils.mergeGeometries after applying each part's matrix: a prop of parts drawn in one draw, a mirrored half, an array (the same part at several placements). Normals follow each placement; a mirrored part turns its triangles so they still face out. Vertex colours are kept when any part has them.

parts.description: The parts, in order (at least one).

uvRepeat.description: How many times a texture repeats across it, along u and v: its UVs scaled by uvRepeat (three.js texture.repeat, here on the geometry; material textures sample with repeat wrapping).

physics.description: Register it as a physics mesh too.

dynamic.description: Whether og.render.updateGeometry may rewrite it later.

LineMode.description: How a line set's points join, as three.js's three line objects.

x-og-variants.strip: One polyline through every point, as three.js Line.
x-og-variants.segments: Pairs of points, each its own segment, as three.js LineSegments.
x-og-variants.loop: A polyline closed back to its first point, as three.js LineLoop.

LinesDesc.description:
Lines through points, drawn this frame only (immediate mode, as og.render.sprite): submit them every tick they should show. three.js Line, LineSegments and LineLoop with a LineBasicMaterial or LineDashedMaterial, but any width on every tier (each segment is a quad in screen space with a feathered edge, so WebGL2's one-pixel lines do not apply).
World lines are drawn in the scene after the transparent meshes and particles, exposed, bloomed and tone mapped with it; screen lines over the finished frame, after every post effect and under the UI.

points.description: The points, in order: world positions, or with screen CSS pixels from the top left of the play surface with y down (z ignored).

colors.description: Per point linear colours, blended along each segment (three.js vertexColors); empty is `color` for all.

width.description: The width: CSS pixels, or world units with worldUnits.

worldUnits.description: Measure width in world units (a line that thins with distance) instead of CSS pixels (as wide at any distance).

depthTest.description: Hidden behind nearer geometry, as three.js Material.depthTest; false draws it over the scene. Screen lines are never depth tested.

screen.description: Draw in screen space over the finished frame: points in CSS pixels, width in CSS pixels.

dashed.description: Dashes, as three.js LineDashedMaterial: dashSize on, gapSize off, along the line from its first point.

dashSize.description: A dash's length: world units (CSS pixels for screen lines).

PointsDesc.description: A point cloud drawn this frame only (immediate mode), as three.js Points with a PointsMaterial: a square per point facing the camera. Submit it every tick it should show (og.Points keeps a static set).

points.description: The positions: world, or with screen CSS pixels from the top left, y down.

colors.description: Per point linear colours; empty is `color` for all.

size.description: The side of each square: world units with sizeAttenuation, else CSS pixels.

sizeAttenuation.description: Size in world units, smaller with distance, as three.js PointsMaterial.sizeAttenuation; false keeps every point `size` CSS pixels.

depthTest.description: Hidden behind nearer geometry; false draws them over the scene.

screen.description: Draw in screen space over the finished frame, positions and size in CSS pixels.

Lines.description: Draws a geometry's vertices as lines at the entity's MatrixWorld, every frame (three.js Line, LineSegments or LineLoop over a BufferGeometry): a static set of lines kept as data, a level's outline, a track, a constellation. The vertices are taken in order (the geometry's indices are not read), with its vertex colours times color.

geometry.description: The vertices (og.render.bufferGeometry: an unindexed one of any count).

color.description: The linear colour, times the vertex colours.

width.description: CSS pixels, or world units with worldUnits.

dashSize.description: Dashes' length in world units along the line; 0 is solid (three.js LineDashedMaterial.dashSize).

layers.description: Three.js layers, as Mesh.layers: drawn by every camera whose mask shares a bit with it (og.Camera, og.CameraView, og.Mirror).

Points.description: Draws a geometry's vertices as a point cloud at the entity's MatrixWorld, every frame (three.js Points over a BufferGeometry): star fields, scanned surfaces, sparse markers kept as data. Vertex colours times color.

color.description: The linear colour, times the vertex colours.

size.description: World units with sizeAttenuation, else CSS pixels.

sizeAttenuation.description: Size in world units, smaller with distance.

layers.description: Three.js layers, as Mesh.layers: drawn by every camera whose mask shares a bit with it (og.Camera, og.CameraView, og.Mirror).

RaycastGeometryDesc.description: Which meshes og.render.raycast tests, as three.js Raycaster's near, far and layers.

maxDistance.description: How far the ray reaches (three.js Raycaster.far); 0 is unbounded.

first.description: Answer only the nearest hit (cheaper: the BVH stops early).

layers.description: A bit mask of the layers tested, as three.js Raycaster.layers: an og.Mesh or og.Model is tested when its own layers (Mesh.layers, Model.layers, 1 by default) share a bit with it, so the default tests every mesh on layer 0.

invisible.description: Test meshes whose visible is false too.

GeometryHit.description: Where a ray meets a drawn triangle, as three.js Raycaster's intersection.

distance.description: From the ray's origin along its normalised direction.

normal.description: The triangle's face normal in world space (its front side, counter-clockwise), unit length.

faceIndex.description: The triangle's index in the geometry, as three.js faceIndex.

RenderTargetFormat.description: How a render target's colour is stored.

x-og-variants.ldr: 8-bit sRGB: the view's finished image (exposed with its camera's exposure and tone mapped with RenderSettings' curve), as a loaded colour texture: a monitor, a minimap, a portrait (show it with an unlit material's map or a sprite).
x-og-variants.hdr: 16-bit float, linear: the view's radiance before exposure and tone mapping, exposed once with the frame that shows it: a mirror or a portal (show it as a material's emissiveMap with color black).

RenderTarget.description: A texture a camera draws into (og.render.renderTarget), as three.js WebGLRenderTarget.

RenderTargetDesc.description: A render target's size and storage, as three.js WebGLRenderTarget's width, height, type and depthTexture.

depth.description: Keep the view's depth too, as a second texture (RenderTargetInfo.depthTexture): its linear view depth from near (0) to far (1) in red, green and blue, of the opaque meshes and models, alpha-cut ones cut (transparent meshes, sprites and particles write none), drawn on every tier (RenderCapabilities.renderTargetDepth). It costs a second draw of the view's opaque meshes.

target.description: The target, for CameraView.target and Mirror.target.

texture.description: Its colour: any material map, og.Sprite, og.render.sprite or og.ui image shows it, as drawn by the last camera that drew into it (transparent black before).

CameraView.description:
A secondary camera, as a second three.js camera rendered with setRenderTarget or setViewport: it draws the scene from the entity's MatrixWorld (looking down its local -Z, as og.Camera) into a render target (target), or, without one, into a rect of the frame (viewport: split-screen, picture-in-picture) over the finished image and under the UI.
It draws what the main camera draws, from its own eye and on its own layers: the meshes and models (skinned and with any material: hooks and full shaders run their vertex and fragment entries), opaque then transparent back to front, the terrain and the sky, the particle systems, og.Lines and og.Points, world sprites (og.Sprite, og.render.sprite) and world text, lit by the frame's lights and shadowed by its shadow maps. Each view is a draw of everything its layers admit: keep a view cheap with its layers and `every`. Screen sprites, the UI and debug draw stay on the main frame. Of the post chain, an ldr target and a viewport carry the view's exposure (its camera's) and the frame's tone curve; an hdr target carries linear radiance before exposure, exposed by the frame that shows it. Neither runs the frame's bloom, AO, SSR, depth of field, colour grading or custom post passes, whose inputs are the main camera's. Sprites in a view are not 2D-lit and do not glow; trails and 2D fluids draw on the main frame only. Views draw lowest order first, all before the frame.

target.description: The target it draws into; 0 draws into the viewport rect of the frame.

viewportX.description: The viewport's left edge, as a fraction of the frame's width (without a target).

viewportY.description: The viewport's top edge, as a fraction of the frame's height.

viewportWidth.description: The viewport's width, as a fraction of the frame's.

viewportHeight.description: The viewport's height, as a fraction of the frame's.

fov.description: The vertical field of view, as og.Camera.fov.

orthographic.description: An orthographic projection of `height` world units.

height.description: The visible world height of the orthographic projection.

exposure.description: Its exposure before tone mapping (an ldr target and a viewport).

layers.description: Three.js layers, as og.Camera.layers: it draws the objects whose layers share a bit with it.

order.description: Views draw in ascending order (ties in entity order), all before the frame.

clear.description: Clear to clearColor instead of drawing the scene's background (sky or colour).

clearColor.description: The linear colour it clears to with clear.

every.description: Draw once every this many ticks (when the tick is a multiple of it); the target keeps its image between. 0 and 1 draw every frame: a security monitor at 4 costs a quarter.

Mirror.description: A planar mirror: the main camera reflected in the entity's xy plane (its local +Z the mirror's facing side), drawn into target fitted to a width by height rect centred on the entity, as a mirrored og.CameraView. Give the mirror's mesh (an og.render.planeGeometry of the same size) a material that reads the target: an hdr target as emissiveMap with color black, or an ldr target as an unlit map. Nothing behind the glass is drawn; seen from behind, it draws nothing.

width.description: The mirror's width along the entity's local +X.

layers.description: Three.js layers it reflects, as og.Camera.layers.

every.description: Draw once every this many ticks, as CameraView.every.

Post.description: A custom post pass from og.load.post (an `.ogt` of `type post`): a WGSL `post` function over the lit image and the parameters it reads.

PostError.description: A custom post pass the device failed to compile.

x-og-variants.froxel: A grid of view-aligned cells over the camera's frustum (160 by 90 by 64, slices deepening with the square of their index) lit in compute by the sun through its shadow cascades and by the clustered point, spot and rect lights through their shadows and cookies (each cell the mean of eight samples over its depth), then integrated front to back: the full tier.
x-og-variants.raymarch: Each pixel's view ray marched through the fog in 24 jittered steps, each lit by the sun through its cascades and by the first 8 point, spot and rect lights of its screen cluster through their shadows and cookies (RenderCapabilities.volumetricLights): WebGL2, which has no compute.

RectLight.description:
A rectangle of light, as three.js RectAreaLight: width by height metres centred on the entity in its local xy plane, facing along its local -Z (aim it with transform.lookAt, as a spot), emitting color * intensity from its front, or from both faces with twoSided. Shaded with linearly transformed cosines (Heitz et al. 2016, three.js's tables), so its highlight on a glossy floor is the rectangle's shape and its light on a matte wall falls off as a real panel's does. With castShadow it casts a soft shadow in the frame; og bake lightmaps traces its exact soft shadows into the bounce light either way.
Area lights are clustered with the point and spot lights and share their MAX_LIGHTS budget; each reaches as far as its brightness carries (where it would light a white surface facing it at one hundredth of one), and fades smoothly to zero there.

intensity.description: The emitted radiance (luminance), as three.js RectAreaLight.intensity.

width.description: Its size along the entity's local x, as RectAreaLight.width.

height.description: Its size along the entity's local y, as RectAreaLight.height.

twoSided.description: Emit from the back face as well (a hanging panel lit both ways).

castShadow.description: Cast a soft shadow: a shadow map from the rectangle's centre (two when twoSided, counted in the shadowed lights' budget) read with percentage-closer soft shadows, sharp where a caster touches its receiver and widening with the rectangle's size away from it. The view is from the centre, so a caster close to a large panel is shadowed as from its centre.

LightVolume.description:
A box of baked light probes (an irradiance volume): og bake lightmaps traces the light arriving from the scene (bounced off its static models, from the sky, from emissive surfaces) at a grid of points spacing metres apart inside it, as first-order spherical harmonics. Every mesh, model, skinned character and particle-lit surface drawn inside it that has no lightmap of its own takes its ambient light from the probes instead of the sky's, blended at the box's edge over one spacing: a ball rolling past a red wall turns red on that side.
The box is size metres centred on the entity, axis-aligned in world space (its rotation and scale are ignored). Its probes are the scene's: unbaked (no bake since the volume was added, moved or resized) it lights nothing and og doctor --project names the scene.

size.description: The box's extent along world x, y and z.

spacing.description: The most distance between neighbouring probes (the box is divided evenly, with probes on its faces; at most 64 a side).

BakedScene.description: One instantiated scene's baked lighting, as og.render.bakedLighting reports it.

scene.description: The scene's asset id, such as `scenes/cornell.ogt`.

baked.description: Its lightmap and probes are loaded and drawn.

reason.description: Why not, when not: the scene has no bake (`og bake lightmaps` writes `<scene>.lightmap.ogt`), its bake is stale (a static model or the scene changed since; the reason names which), or RenderSettings.bakedLighting is off. Empty when baked.

models.description: Static model instances drawn with the lightmap.

volumes.description: LightVolume grids its dynamic objects sample.

Asset.description: A loaded bundle, scene or glTF asset.

Font.description: A cooked MSDF font: its glyph table and one or more atlas pages.

Sound.description: A cooked sound: QOA-encoded PCM the audio module plays.

Style.description: A cooked UI style: its values, atlas, fonts, icons and sounds loaded with it, for og.ui.configure.

TextureArray.description: A cooked texture array: same-sized layers uploaded as one 2D-array texture (og.load.textureArray).

GltfDesc.description: How to load a glTF, as three.js GLTFLoader options where they apply.

castShadow.description: Whether the models instantiated from it cast shadows: world.instantiate of the handle and a scene's `model` line give their og.Model this castShadow. On when omitted, so a model loaded without a desc casts as it always has; false turns it off for the model (og.Model.castShadow turns it off for one instance). The flags belong to the asset: another og.load.gltf of the same path answers the same handle and sets them again, for the models instantiated after it.

receiveShadow.description: Whether the models instantiated from it receive shadows (og.Model.receiveShadow, as castShadow): on when omitted; false lights them as if unshadowed by every light.

geometries.description: Its geometries, in glTF mesh-primitive order.

materials.description: Its materials, in glTF order, then the default material.

animations.description: Its clip names, in glTF order, from the model's `#anim` blob (empty for a model without clips): a skinned glTF's animations, an animated `.vox`'s `frames` or `voxClip` names. og.load.animation answers the same clips with their ClipAsset handles and durations, and og.anim.clip finds one by name.

path.description: The cooked directory it was opened from.

FontInfo.description: A loaded font's metrics, in em units unless stated.

pages.description: Atlas pages; the renderer draws one page per pass with one shared layout.

pxRange.description: The distance range in atlas pixels.

lineHeight.description: Ascender minus descender plus the line gap.

icons.description: The icons of an icon set (an `.ogt` of `type icons`, SVGs cooked like a font for UiDesc.icons.font); 0 for a text font.

chunks.description: The chunks it was cooked in (`sound { stream true }` in its import settings, or a QOA file above 1 MiB), the first included; 0 when it was cooked whole. A chunked sound is never resident whole: the engine reads its chunks from about half a second behind each playhead to four seconds ahead (on the web, fetched like a streaming group's pack) and drops the rest.

layers.description: Its layers, in the order the file lists them.

format.description: The encoding on the GPU: `rgba8`, or the block format the device takes for its kind (`bc7`, `bc5`, `astc4x4`, `etc2`, `eacrg11`).

bytes.description: Bytes it takes on the GPU, every level of every layer (counted in the frame's texture bytes).

Model.description:
Draws a loaded glTF's default scene at the entity's world transform: every mesh node with its glTF material. Scene entities with a `model` line get one; world.instantiate of a glTF asset spawns one.
The glTF's materials are shared by every instance of it; `tint` and `flash` are this instance's own, carried with its transform to the lit shaders (one draw for every instance, whatever each shows), so one of a crowd can flash when struck.

tint.description: A linear colour, 0 to 1 a channel, multiplied with every material's base colour on this instance only (white: as the glTF).

flash.description: A hit flash on this instance only: the lit colour mixed towards flashColor by this much (og.tween.flash fades it out).

castShadow.description: Every mesh of the model casts shadows, as Mesh.castShadow: drawn into the sun's cascades and the shadowed lights' maps. On by default, unlike Mesh's (a loaded model casts, as it always has); false takes this instance out of every shadow pass. world.instantiate of a glTF and a scene's `model` line set it from the load's GltfDesc.castShadow, unless the scene gives the entity a `Model` table (whose castShadow is on unless it says false).

receiveShadow.description: Every mesh of the model receives shadows, as Mesh.receiveShadow; false lights this instance as if unshadowed by every light. On by default. Set as castShadow is, from GltfDesc.receiveShadow or the scene's `Model` table.

visible.description: Whether it is drawn, as Mesh.visible: false skips every draw of this instance (its meshes, its shadows) while it keeps its transform, its animation and its physics, so a ghost car or a pickup waiting to respawn is hidden without moving it away.

lodBias.description: This instance's level of detail bias, multiplied with RenderSettings.lodBias: the cook simplifies every mesh into levels (a model's import settings, `model { lods 1 0.5 0.25 }` by default, the triangle fraction of each level; a glTF with MSFT_lod keeps its own levels) and measures each level's error against the full mesh, and the renderer draws the coarsest level whose error covers less than a pixel at the model's distance, with hysteresis so it does not flicker at the boundary. Above 1 keeps detail farther (a hero), below 1 drops it sooner (a crowd); 0 always draws the full mesh. dump_entity shows the level drawn.

layers.description: Three.js layers of every mesh of the model, as Mesh.layers.

static.description: Part of its scene's baked lighting: og bake lightmaps gives a static model lightmap UVs (xatlas, over its world-space triangles) and traces the light arriving at its surfaces from the scene into the scene's lightmap (`<scene>.lightmap.ogt` and `.ktx2` beside the scene). Once baked, the model draws with it (its ambient light from the lightmap instead of the sky; its lights' direct light, shadows and highlights still drawn every frame) for as long as the bake matches the scene. A scene entity says `static true` beside its `model` line; an unbaked static model draws as any model, and og doctor --project names the scene.

path.description: The path it was loaded from.
The path it was loaded from.

RigidBody.description:
A body the physics step simulates. It needs an og.Transform and usually has an og.Collider; a dynamic body without an og.Velocity gets one.
Changing a RigidBody, a Collider or Transform.scale rebuilds the body (it loses its contacts' warm starts); a Transform or Velocity that game code changed moves it (a teleport).

kind.description: BODY_DYNAMIC (0, simulated and written back), BODY_STATIC (1, never moves) or BODY_KINEMATIC (2, moved by its Velocity each tick, or by game code through its Transform).

mass.description: Mass; 0 derives it from the collider's density and volume.

linearDamping.description: How fast linear velocity decays (0: none).

angularDamping.description: How fast angular velocity decays (0: none).

gravityScale.description: Multiplies Physics.gravity for this body: 0 floats, 1 is normal.

lock.description: Locked axes, a sum of the LOCK_* bits: 1, 2, 4 no translation along x, y, z; 8, 16, 32 no rotation about x, y, z (2D uses 1, 2 and 32).

ccd.description: 1 enables continuous collision detection, for fast small bodies that must not tunnel; 0 off.

centerOfMass.description: Moves the centre of mass from where the collider puts it (its shape's centre), in the entity's own frame and scaled by og.Transform.scale like Collider.offset; the inertia stays the shape's. A car's lowered below its wheel mounts keeps it on its wheels at full lock; a weight at a toy's base rights it. Needs an og.Collider.

Collider.description: The shape an entity collides with, attached to its RigidBody (or, without one, a static collider at its Transform). Sizes are scaled by og.Transform.scale.

shape.description: One of the SHAPE_* codes: 0 box, 1 sphere (a circle in 2D), 2 capsule, 3 cylinder (3D), 4 convex hull of `mesh` (a polygon in 2D), 5 triangle mesh of `mesh` (3D), 6 the height field `mesh` (3D: a terrain).

size.description: Full extents of a box, as three.js BoxGeometry(width, height, depth).

radius.description: Radius of a sphere, circle, capsule or cylinder.

height.description: A capsule's distance between its cap centres (three.js CapsuleGeometry length); a cylinder's height.

mesh.description: The geometry whose vertices a convex or triangle-mesh shape uses: a loaded glTF's geometry (registered automatically) or one given to og.physics.setMesh; for SHAPE_HEIGHTFIELD, a terrain's height field (og.terrain.load's TerrainInfo.geometry).

offset.description: Position of the shape relative to the entity.

rotation.description: Rotation of the shape relative to the entity.

friction.description: Coulomb friction (0 is ice, 1 rubber); a pair uses the mean of both colliders.

restitution.description: Bounciness (0 no bounce, 1 elastic); a pair uses the mean of both colliders.

sensor.description: 1 makes this a sensor: it reports SensorEntered and SensorExited and pushes nothing; 0 a solid.

layers.description: The collision layers this collider is on, as bits.

mask.description: The layers it collides with, as bits. Two colliders interact when each one's layers meet the other's mask.

Velocity.description: Linear and angular velocity. Written for dynamic bodies every tick (added to them by the step when missing); a kinematic body moves by it each tick (never added, never written). Set it to launch or stop a body; push one with og.physics.applyForce, applyImpulse, applyTorque or applyTorqueImpulse.

linear.description: The linear velocity (2D uses x and y).

angular.description: The angular velocity about each axis (2D uses z).

Physics.description: The physics settings of the world. The profile is the project's; the same components serve both profiles.

profile.description: PROFILE_2D (2: rapier2d, the xy plane, rotation about z) or PROFILE_3D (3: rapier3d), from project.ogt. Set the other one at run time to change profile: the next step builds that profile's simulation from the components (contacts, joints' warm starts, ropes, cloth, fluids and ragdoll bodies start again), so a 3D game can play a 2D scene and back.

gravity.description: The acceleration of every dynamic body, times its gravityScale; 2D uses x and y.

substeps.description: Physics steps per tick, each of dt / substeps: more is stiffer stacks and less tunnelling, at more cost.

restSpeed.description: A dynamic body touching something, supported with at most 2 mm of overlap and slower than this before and after a step, keeps its pose and loses its residual velocity (the same number in m/s and rad/s); 0 disables it.

CollisionStarted.description: Two solid colliders started touching during the tick. Read in the tick after, when og.Velocity already holds the solver's answer (the bodies parting): how hard they met is `impulse` and `relativeVelocity`, taken in the step itself.

a.description: The entity with the lower id.

b.description: The entity with the higher id.

point.description: The deepest contact point in world space (z is 0 in 2D).

normal.description: The contact normal, from a towards b.

impulse.description: The normal impulse the solver gave the pair in the step that made the contact (every substep, every contact point), in newton-seconds: b took `impulse` along `normal`, a the same against it. Its momentum answer to the hit, at least 0; heavier and faster hits give more.

relativeVelocity.description: a's velocity relative to b at `point` as that step began, before the solver answered: each body's linear velocity plus its angular velocity crossed with the point's offset from its centre of mass (a static collider is still; z is 0 in 2D). Along `normal` it is the closing speed, positive while they approach: max(0, relativeVelocity · normal) is how hard they hit, in m/s.

CollisionEnded.description: Two solid colliders stopped touching, or one of them went away.

a.description: The entity with the lower id.

b.description: The entity with the higher id.

SensorEntered.description: A collider started overlapping a sensor.

sensor.description: The entity whose collider is the sensor.

SensorExited.description: A collider stopped overlapping a sensor, or one of them went away.

sensor.description: The entity whose collider is the sensor.

Contact.description: One pair in contact at the end of a step, sent every tick for every touching pair: how a game asks what is touching what right now.

a.description: The entity with the lower id.

b.description: The entity with the higher id.

sensor.description: 0 for two solids; an overlap with a sensor otherwise: 1 a is the sensor, 2 b is, 3 both are.

Joint.description: A joint between two bodies (or a body and a point of the world). The component may sit on one of the bodies (`body` 0) or on an entity of its own, so one body can have several joints. Anchors are in each body's frame (rotated and moved with it, not scaled); without `other` the second anchor is a world point. A joint whose bodies are not both `og.RigidBody` entities does nothing until they are.

kind.description: JOINT_FIXED 0, JOINT_REVOLUTE 1 (hinge), JOINT_PRISMATIC 2 (slider), JOINT_SPRING 3, JOINT_ROPE 4, JOINT_BALL 5.

body.description: The first body; 0 is this entity.

other.description: The second body; 0 joins the first one to the world at `otherAnchor`.

anchor.description: Where the joint sits on the first body, in its frame.

otherAnchor.description: Where it sits on the second body, in its frame (a world point without `other`).

axis.description: The hinge or slide axis in the first body's frame (a hinge in 2D turns about z).

limits.description: Whether `min`..`max` bound the hinge angle (rad) or the slide (m).

min.description: The lower limit: radians for a hinge, metres for a slider.

motor.description: MOTOR_NONE 0, MOTOR_VELOCITY 1 (drive at motorTarget speed), MOTOR_POSITION 2 (spring to motorTarget).

motorTarget.description: The motor's target speed (rad/s, m/s) or angle or position (rad, m).

motorStiffness.description: A position motor's stiffness; a velocity motor's strength.

motorMaxForce.description: The most force (or torque) the motor applies; 0 is unbounded.

length.description: A rope's longest distance between the anchors.

collide.description: Whether the two bodies still collide with each other.

value.description: Written: the hinge angle (rad) or the slide (m) after the step; the anchors' distance for springs and ropes.

CharacterController.description: A kinematic character (3D, or top-down 2D): the entity's capsule (or any og.Collider) moved by `move` each tick, sliding along walls, climbing slopes up to `maxSlope` and steps up to `stepHeight`, snapped to the ground, carried by the moving platform it stands on and falling by gravity. It keeps `skin` off every surface, standing that far over the ground; a step is climbed when the ground beyond it is at most `stepHeight` over the ground it stands on. What blocks it is every solid collider its og.Collider's `layers` and `mask` interact with (each one's layers meeting the other's mask), as for bodies. The entity needs an og.Transform and an og.Collider; the step makes it a kinematic body and pushes the dynamic bodies it walks into (`pushBodies`) with at most `pushStrength`, so a light one is shoved and a heavy one holds.

move.description: The wanted velocity across the ground (m/s, world space; y is ignored unless gravityScale is 0). Set it every tick.

jump.description: Held to jump: a jump starts on the tick it becomes true while grounded (or in coyote time).

jumpSpeed.description: The upward speed of a jump.

gravityScale.description: Multiplies og.Physics.gravity; 0 for top-down movement in any direction.

maxSlope.description: The steepest slope it walks up.

stepHeight.description: The highest step it climbs without jumping (0: none).

snapDistance.description: How far below it the ground still holds it (stairs down, slopes): 0 lets it leave every edge.

skin.description: The gap kept between it and every surface.

coyoteTime.description: After leaving an edge, a jump still starts within this time.

pushBodies.description: Push dynamic bodies it walks into, with at most `pushStrength`.

pushStrength.description: The most force it pushes with: each tick the bodies it walks into share an impulse of at most this times the tick's length (mass times the speed it asks of them, capped), so a body of a few kilograms is shoved at its speed while one whose friction holds more (a tonne on the ground) does not move. 0 leaves every body where it is, as `pushBodies` false does.

grounded.description: Written: standing on walkable ground after the step.

sliding.description: Written: sliding down a slope steeper than maxSlope.

velocity.description: Written: the velocity it moved at this tick (the platform's carry included).

groundNormal.description: Written: the ground's normal (zero in the air).

coyote.description: Written: seconds left in which a jump may still start (coyote time).

jumpWasHeld.description: Written: `jump` as the last step saw it (a jump starts on its rising edge).

ground.description: Written: the entity it stands on (0 in the air); a moving one carries it.

PlatformerController.description: A 2D platformer character (the 2D profile): run, jump and fall with designer units (jump height and time to apex, not gravity), coyote time, jump buffering, variable jump height (releasing jump while rising cuts the jump), apex hang, air jumps, wall slide and wall jump, one-way platforms (colliders on `oneWayLayers` are solid from above only; hold `down` to drop through), moving platforms (it rides what it stands on) and corner correction (a jump that clips a ceiling corner by less than `cornerCorrection` slides past it). It keeps `skin` off every surface; what blocks it is every solid collider its og.Collider's `layers` and `mask` interact with (each one's layers meeting the other's mask), as for bodies. The entity needs an og.Transform and an og.Collider (a box or capsule); it becomes a kinematic body and pushes the dynamic bodies it runs into (`pushBodies`) with at most `pushStrength`, so a crate's mass tells: a light one is shoved at the run speed, a heavy one holds (set its og.RigidBody `mass`).

moveX.description: The run input, -1 (left) to 1 (right). Set it every tick.

jump.description: Held to jump: a press is buffered for jumpBuffer; releasing while rising cuts the jump.

down.description: Held to drop through a one-way platform.

impulse.description: A velocity change to take on the next step (a knock-back, a spring, a recoil): added to `velocity`, then set back to zero. One with an upward y leaves the ground; the run's acceleration and gravity act on the result from then on, so a knock-back is `{ x: away * 6, y: 7 }` with `moveX` 0 for its few ticks.

acceleration.description: How fast it reaches maxSpeed on the ground.

deceleration.description: How fast it stops on the ground without input.

airDeceleration.description: Deceleration in the air without input.

jumpHeight.description: How high a full jump goes.

timeToApex.description: How long a full jump takes to reach its height (sets gravity and the jump speed).

fallGravity.description: Gravity multiplier while falling (snappier landings above 1).

jumpCut.description: Gravity multiplier while rising with jump released (variable jump height; 1 disables it).

apexGravity.description: Gravity multiplier near the apex while jump is held (hang time; 1 disables it).

apexThreshold.description: The vertical speed below which the apex multiplier applies.

coyoteTime.description: After running off an edge, a jump still starts within this time.

jumpBuffer.description: A jump pressed this long before landing starts on landing.

airJumps.description: Extra jumps in the air (1: a double jump).

wallJumps.description: Slide down walls it pushes against (and jump off them).

wallSlideSpeed.description: The fastest slide down a wall.

wallJump.description: A wall jump's velocity: x away from the wall, y up.

wallJumpLock.description: After a wall jump, the run input is ignored for this long (so it leaves the wall).

oneWayLayers.description: The collision layers that are one-way platforms (solid from above), as bits.

cornerCorrection.description: How far a rising jump is nudged sideways past a ceiling corner (0: never).

maxSlope.description: The steepest slope it runs up.

snapDistance.description: How far below it the ground still holds it (slopes, small drops).

skin.description: The gap kept between it and every surface.

pushBodies.description: Push dynamic bodies it runs into, with at most `pushStrength`.

pushStrength.description: The most force it pushes with: each tick the bodies it runs into share an impulse of at most this times the tick's length (mass times the speed it asks of them, capped), so a body of a few kilograms is shoved at its speed while one whose friction holds more (a tonne on the ground) does not move. 0 leaves every body where it is, as `pushBodies` false does.

grounded.description: Written: standing on ground after the step.

onWall.description: Written: -1 sliding on a wall to its left, 1 to its right, 0 none.

facing.description: Written: -1 facing left, 1 right (the last run direction).

velocity.description: Written: the velocity after the step (the platform's carry excluded).

jumping.description: Written: rising from a jump (until the apex or a release cut).

airJumpsLeft.description: Written: air jumps left before landing.

coyote.description: Written: seconds of coyote time left.

buffer.description: Written: seconds a buffered jump press stays valid.

wallLock.description: Written: seconds the run input stays locked after a wall jump.

dropTime.description: Written: seconds one-way platforms stay passable after dropping through.

jumpWasHeld.description: Written: `jump` as the last step saw it.

ground.description: Written: the entity it stands on (0 in the air); a moving one carries it.

CharacterEvent.description: Something a CharacterController or PlatformerController did this step: the hooks for dust, squash, sounds and camera kicks. Read the next tick: the controllers move in the physics step, after the game's systems, so a jump pressed in tick T moves the character in T and its CHARACTER_JUMPED is read in T + 1 (og-feel §12 has the same-tick alternative).

kind.description: CHARACTER_JUMPED 1, LANDED 2, WALL_JUMPED 3, AIR_JUMPED 4, LEFT_GROUND 5, BUMPED 6.

speed.description: The vertical speed at the moment (a landing's impact speed is negative).

Vehicle.description:
A car on a dynamic chassis (the entity's og.RigidBody and og.Collider). 3D: a raycast car with four wheels (suspension, grip, steering on the front axle); its forward is the chassis's local +z (three.js Object3D.lookAt aims +z). 2D: two wheel bodies on sprung wheel joints (front at +x), driven by a motor. The wheels are not entities: og.physics.vehicleWheels gives their poses (and each tyre's slip) for drawing, smoke and skid marks.
The defaults drive a road car of about 1,000 kg: give the chassis that mass (og.RigidBody.mass 1000), since a car-sized box at the collider's density 1 weighs a few kilograms and the engine's and brakes' newtons would throw it. The suspension and the grip scale with the chassis's mass (Bullet's units), the engine and the brakes do not: a heavier car wants proportionally more engineForce and brakeForce. og-feel §12 has the numbers a game starts from.
The wheel rays meet what the chassis's collider would (its og.Collider layers against the other's mask, and the other's layers against its mask), so two cars on layers that do not meet (a ghost beside the player) pass through each other.

throttle.description: The accelerator, -1 (reverse) to 1. Set it every tick.

wheelBase.description: The distance between the front and rear axles.

track.description: The distance between the left and right wheels (3D).

mountHeight.description: The height of the wheel mounts below the chassis centre.

suspensionTravel.description: How far the suspension compresses or extends from rest.

grip.description: The tyres' grip (3D: the friction slip, how much of its load a tyre holds before it slides: 2 grips a road car through a bend, below 1 it slides like a drift car; 2D: the wheels' friction).

engineForce.description: The engine's force at full throttle (3D: per driven wheel, in newtons: 2,500 on the two rear wheels push 1,000 kg at 5 m/s²; 2D: the motor's torque, N·m).

maxSpeed.description: The top speed: the engine's force fades out towards it (throttle against the motion brakes first).

brakeForce.description: The brakes' force at full brake (3D: per wheel, in newtons, every wheel braking: 2,000 stop 1,000 kg at 8 m/s²; 2D: the wheels' braking torque).

maxSteer.description: The front wheels' largest steering angle (3D).

wheelMass.description: The wheels' mass (2D: the wheel bodies; 3D ignores it).

rollInfluence.description: How much the tyres' sideways grip rolls the chassis in a bend (3D): 0 pushes at the centre of mass's height, so the car corners flat and never tips over from steering (an arcade car); towards 1 at the road, the roll that tips a tall car over (rapier's own car uses 0.1, which rolls a 1,000 kg car at full lock above about 20 m/s). Raise it a little for body roll, with og.RigidBody.centerOfMass lowered to keep the car on its wheels.

speed.description: Written: the forward speed (m/s; negative reversing).

contacts.description: Written: how many wheels touch the ground.

slip.description: Written: the largest slip of its wheels (og.physics.vehicleWheels' `slip`): 0 every tyre grips, towards 1 one slides; for a squeal's volume or smoke without reading the wheels (3D; 0 in 2D).

Rope.description: A Verlet rope: `segments` links from the entity's world position (its og.Transform after its parents'; plus `offset`) to `end` (an entity, plus `endOffset`) or hanging free, swung by gravity and wind, colliding with every solid collider at `radius`. It moves nothing (one-way: a rope joint ties bodies together, og.Joint JOINT_ROPE). Its points are world state (the og.physics state block); og.physics.ropePoints reads them and the renderer draws the rope as a strip of `width` and `color`.

segments.description: The number of links (points minus one).

offset.description: The start's offset from the entity's position (world axes).

end.description: The entity the far end is tied to; 0 leaves it free.

endOffset.description: The far end's offset from `end`'s position.

iterations.description: Constraint passes per step: more is stiffer, at more cost.

damping.description: How much of its velocity each point keeps per tick (1: none lost).

radius.description: The thickness it collides at (0: no collision).

Cloth.description: A Verlet cloth: a `columns` × `rows` grid of points, `spacing` apart, hanging from the entity's world position (its og.Transform after its parents': its top-left corner, the grid laid out along the entity's local x and down -y), pinned by `pins` (pinned points follow the entity), with stretch and shear constraints, gravity, wind, collision against every solid collider and, with `thickness`, against itself. One-way like og.Rope; its points are world state. Drawn as a double-sided mesh with `material` (og.render.standardMaterial; 0: a plain cloth colour).

spacing.description: The rest distance between neighbouring points.

pins.description: Which points are pinned, a sum of PIN_* bits (1 top row, 2 top corners, 4 left column, 8 top rings).

damping.description: How much of its velocity each point keeps per tick.

wind.description: A steady acceleration (wind); the cloth flutters with it.

gust.description: How much the wind varies over the cloth and the tick (0: steady).

radius.description: The thickness it collides at (0: no collision).
