x-og-variants.inkInverse: Ink on a ground of ink (a selected chip).
x-og-variants.control: Neutral control fills: secondary buttons, tracks, fields.
x-og-variants.controlStrong: A neutral control hovered or pressed; selection.
x-og-variants.primary: The one directed action: primary buttons, a slider's fill, a switch that is on, the caret.
x-og-variants.highlight: Emphasised ink: a speaker's name, a price, a link, the player's map dot.
x-og-variants.focus: The focus ring of key and pad navigation.
x-og-variants.hud: HUD capsules over the game (scores, timers, toasts).
x-og-variants.gold: Currency: coins, gold, prices that can be paid.

TypeStepName.description: A step of the style's type ramp.

SizeRange.description: The bounds of a fit or grow size.

max.description: The largest size; absent is unbounded.

PercentSize.description: A size relative to the parent.

fraction.description: The fraction of the parent's inner size.

Size.description: A size along one axis. Absent (null) is fit: the content's size.

oneOf.description: The content's size, within the range.

max.description: The largest size; absent is unbounded.

oneOf.description: The content's size, then a share of the parent's free space, within the range.

max.description: The largest size; absent is unbounded.

oneOf.description: A fraction of the parent's inner size.

fraction.description: The fraction of the parent's inner size.

Insets.description: Padding or margins on four sides.

Paint.description: A colour: a theme token, or an sRGB colour as authored (components 0 to 1), with an alpha. Neither is white.

token.description: A semantic colour of the theme.

color.description: An sRGB colour as authored, when no token is given.

ElementDesc.description: A container: its layout and its look.

direction.description: Which way it lays out its children.

width.description: Its width; null fits the content.

height.description: Its height; null fits the content.

align.description: Where children sit along the main axis.

wrap.description: Break a row into lines at its inner width.

scroll.description: Scroll its content vertically and clip it.

scrollX.description: Scroll its content horizontally and clip it (with scroll: both ways).

interactive.description: Report a Response from close(), as a button does.

radius.description: Corner radius.

frame.description: The style frame its background takes (a HUD element, a card); null is a plain fill. Without a style the fill is drawn either way.

aspect.description: Width over height (0: none): with the height left to fit, it is as tall as its laid-out width over this; with a fixed height and the width left to fit, as wide as the height times it.

LabelDesc.description: How a label draws its text.

step.description: The type step; null is body.

nowrap.description: Keep to one line (breaking only at `\n`).

width.description: Its width; null fits the text.

heading.description: A heading: a style with a flourish frames it.

ellipsis.description: Cut with an ellipsis where the text does not fit its width: on its one line (with nowrap; the label can then shrink in a row) or on its last line (maxLines). The probe still reads the whole text.

maxLines.description: The most lines a wrapping label shows; 0 is no limit. With ellipsis the last ends in an ellipsis when text is left out.

size.description: The control height.

width.description: Its width; null fits the label.

autofocus.description: Take the focus when it appears (it was not on screen the tick before) and no dialog is open: what opens takes the focus (og-ui §4), so a menu's first item answers Enter and the pad's A from its first tick. og.ui.mainMenu's first item has it.

PanelDesc.description: A card: panel, the panel radius, padded and spaced by the style.

row.description: Lay children left to right (the default is top to bottom).

width.description: Its width; null fits the content.

height.description: Its height; null fits the content.

padding.description: Space inside; null is space.lg on every side.

gap.description: Space between children; null is space.md.

align.description: Where children sit along the main axis.

ScrollAxes.description: Which ways a scroll container scrolls.

ScrollDesc.description: A scroll container: the wheel (both axes, deltaX and deltaY) or a drag scrolls it, and a released drag keeps its momentum, slowing over motion.spring.momentum's response (none under reduced motion); it clips its content; a scrollbar on each scrolling axis shows the position, and a press on one grabs and drags it. Nested containers hand off: what the innermost under the pointer cannot take (it reached its end, or does not scroll that way) goes to the one around it.

width.description: Its width; null fits the content.

height.description: Its height; null fits the content.

ImageDesc.description: A texture region, or a solid rectangle without a texture.

texture.description: The texture; null draws a solid rectangle of the tint.

uv.description: The region drawn, [u0, v0, u1, v1] with v down; null is the whole texture.

tint.description: Multiplies the texture; null is white.

aspect.description: Width over height (0: none): with the height left to fit, the image is as tall as its laid-out width over this (a growing column keeps a picture's proportions); with a fixed height and the width left to fit, as wide as the height times it.

label.description: What a screen reader calls it (and the probe's text): a picture that means something (a portrait, a star earned) names it in the game's words; empty is decoration.

ZoomViewDesc.description: A zoomable picture (a map, an artwork): what it shows and its zoom limits.

texture.description: The picture; null draws a solid rectangle of the tint.

uv.description: The picture's region, [u0, v0, u1, v1] with v down; null is the whole texture.

tint.description: Multiplies the texture; null is white.

aspect.description: Width over height (0: none), as ImageDesc.aspect.

minZoom.description: The least zoom; 0 is 1 (the whole picture).

zoom.description: Its zoom: 1 shows the whole picture, 2 half of it each way.

centerX.description: The middle of what it shows, as a fraction of the picture's width (0.5 at rest).

centerY.description: The middle of what it shows, as a fraction of the picture's height (0.5 at rest).

width.description: Its width; null grows into the free space.

min.description: The smallest value; min equal to max (the zero value) means 0 to 1.

step.description: Snap to multiples of step from min; 0 is continuous.

placeholder.description: Shown, dimmed, while the field is empty.

maxChars.description: The most characters it takes; 0 is no limit.

placeholder.description: Shown, dimmed, while the area is empty.

rows.description: Lines shown at once; 0 is 4. More scroll.

maxChars.description: The most characters it takes, line breaks included; 0 is no limit.

Response.description: What happened to an element this tick. Edges (clicked, changed, submitted) are true for exactly one tick.

hovered.description: The pointer is over it and no other element holds the press.

pressed.description: The press that started on it is still held.

changed.description: Its value changed (slider, toggle, text field).

focused.description: It has focus: a text field being edited, or the control keyboard and gamepad navigation landed on.

submitted.description: Enter was pressed in it (text field).

dropped.description: A list row or grid cell a press started on was released over this one: that row's or cell's index (drag and drop).

pad.description: The gamepad (0 to 3) whose A pressed it this tick; null when the pointer or the keyboard did. Pads 1 to 3 press only while og.ui.setPlayers allows them (local multiplayer).

focusedBy.description: Bit k: pad k's focus is on it (bit 0 is the shared focus of the pointer, the keyboard and pad 0; bits 1 to 3 the other players' pads).

SliderResult.description: A slider's response and its value after this tick's input.

value.description: The value, to keep in game state and pass back next tick.

ToggleResult.description: A toggle's response and its state after this tick's input.

on.description: The state, to keep in game state and pass back next tick.

FieldResult.description: A text field's response and its text after this tick's input.

value.description: The text, to keep in game state and pass back next tick.

Viewport.description: The play surface the UI lays out in.

dpr.description: Device pixels per CSS pixel; rectangles snap to device pixels.

safeArea.description: The device's unsafe margins (notch, home indicator); the root pads by them.

coarsePointer.description: A touch screen or another coarse pointer.

reducedMotion.description: The page prefers reduced motion (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce, from the web shell): the UI's theme only fades, whatever UiDesc.reducedMotion says. Omitted is false.

highContrast.description: The page prefers more contrast (prefers-contrast: more, from the web shell): the UI's theme is the high-contrast one, whatever UiDesc.contrast says. Omitted is false.

reducedTransparency.description: The page prefers less transparency (prefers-reduced-transparency: reduce, from the web shell): glass parts are opaque surfaces and the scrim and translucent fills flat, whatever UiDesc.reducedTransparency says (UiTheme.reducedTransparency). Omitted is false.

macKeys.description: Text controls take macOS's editing keys: Command with A, C, X and Z, Command+←/→ to the line's ends (↑/↓ the text's), Option+←/→ and Option+Backspace by words, Control+A and E to the line's ends. Off: Control takes the shortcuts and moves by words (Alt too), Home and End go to the line's ends. The web shell sets it from the browser's platform (Apple's); a native host sets it on macOS, so a script that holds Ctrl or Meta edits as a person on that OS would (og.ui.previewViewport pins either). Omitted is false.

covered.description: Where the host's own control covers the surface: on a published page the web shell's round Back to the Portal, top left (about 12, 12 to 52, 52 CSS px; its name shows beside it for the first seconds of play). Anchored groups keep out of it, moved along the edge they sit on (a top-left group to its right), so the HUD templates never draw under it; a game drawing its own corner reads it from og.ui.frameViewport. Empty (omitted) is none: native hosts and pages without Back.

breakpoint.description: Its size class: phone portrait or landscape, tablet, desktop.

UiDesc.description: How the UI looks: the scheme, the density, its fonts, the contrast, the game's primary colour, motion, transparency, the icon atlas, the style and the sounds. og.ui.configure takes it in part: a field left out keeps the value the last call (or a look's style) gave it, null clears it.

font.description: The body font, from og.load.font; null measures text at half an em per character and draws none.

displayFont.description: The display font; null uses the body font.

monoFont.description: The monospaced font; null uses the body font.

roundedFont.description: The rounded font (levels and scores); null uses the display font, then the body font.

fallbackFonts.description: Fonts for other scripts (Hebrew, Devanagari, a CJK face with `font { runtime true }`), tried in order after the locale's (og.i18n) for a text the role's font cannot draw whole. A text mixing scripts takes each run from the first font that has it (the role's for its Latin, a fallback for its CJK or Arabic), one label in several fonts.

contrast.description: Standard or high contrast. The page's prefers-contrast: more takes high contrast too (Viewport.highContrast).

primaryColor.description: An sRGB colour as the game's primary (its hover, pressed and soft tones derived from it, the ink on it whichever of ink and inkInverse reads better); null keeps the style's.

reducedMotion.description: Transitions only fade; sheens stop. The page's prefers-reduced-motion turns it on too (Viewport.reducedMotion).

reducedTransparency.description: Nothing is see-through: glass parts (a style's glass line) are opaque surfaces (no blur of the frame under them, their frame whole), the scrim is the opaque colour it makes over backdrop and the translucent fills (control, controlStrong, primarySoft, hud) the opaque colours they make over panel. The page's prefers-reduced-transparency turns it on too (Viewport.reducedTransparency); UiTheme.reducedTransparency says it is on.

icons.description: The icon atlas og.ui.icon draws from; null takes the style's.

toastAnchor.description: Where toasts stack; null is the bottom centre.

style.description: A UI style from og.load.style: its palette, radii, type ramp, fonts, icons, frames, ornaments, motion and sounds replace the prototype style (fonts, icons and a primary colour given here still win); null is the prototype style, the engine's placeholder.

sounds.description: Sounds for UI events (they win over the style's).

UiSounds.description: Sounds the UI plays through og-audio (the ui bus) on its events; null is silent.

hover.description: The pointer reaches a control, or keyboard or gamepad focus moves to one.

press.description: A control is pressed: by the pointer, Enter, Space or the gamepad's A.

error.description: A refused press or a danger toast.

StylePart.description: An element class a style dresses with a nine-slice frame.

x-og-variants.button: Buttons (with hover, pressed and disabled states).
x-og-variants.hud: HUD elements over the game (counters, timers) and toasts.

TypeStep.description: One step of the type ramp.

size.description: The font size.

cjkLineHeight.description: The leading text with Chinese, Japanese or Korean characters takes.

ControlSizes.description: The control, row and header heights and the gutter of the density in effect.

UiTheme.description: The style values the UI draws with, read-only.

palette.description: Each ThemeColor as `#rrggbb` or `#rrggbbaa` (sRGB as authored).

space.description: The spacing scale by name (xxs, xs, sm, md, lg, xl, xxl, xl3), in CSS pixels.

radius.description: The corner radii by name (small, control, bar, panel), in CSS pixels.

sizes.description: The control sizes of the density in effect.

durationsMs.description: The motion durations by name (instant, fast, base, slow, spring, bounce), in milliseconds.

style.description: The configured style's name; empty for the prototype style.

contrast.description: The variant in effect: high when the game asked for it or the page prefers more contrast.

reducedMotion.description: Transitions only fade and sheens stop: the game asked for it or the page prefers reduced motion. A game's own animations read it to keep their state changes and drop their movement.

reducedTransparency.description: Nothing is see-through: the scrim and the translucent fills of `palette` are already the opaque colours they make over panel (the scrim over backdrop) and glass is an opaque surface; the game asked for it or the page prefers reduced transparency. A game's own translucent overlays read it to draw opaque too.

RichTextDesc.description: How a rich text paragraph draws: its defaults, which its markup's spans override.

step.description: The type step; null is body.

nowrap.description: Keep to one line (breaking only at `\n`).

width.description: Its width; null fits the text.

RichTextResult.description: What a rich text's links did this tick.

response.description: Its links together: hovered while one is, clicked when one was.

link.description: The link clicked this tick: its `[link=…]` id.

Anchor.description: A point of the safe area an anchored group sits at.

x-og-variants.top: The middle of the top edge.
x-og-variants.left: The middle of the left edge.
x-og-variants.right: The middle of the right edge.
x-og-variants.bottom: The middle of the bottom edge.

TransitionKind.description: How a transition moves its content in and out. Under reduced motion every kind only fades.

x-og-variants.scale: Grows from slightly smaller around its centre.
x-og-variants.pop: Springs up from smaller around its centre, overshoots and settles.

Tone.description: A status tone of badges, toasts and map markers.

x-og-variants.neutral: Neutral: control fill and muted ink.
x-og-variants.primary: The game's identity: the primary's soft wash and highlight ink.
x-og-variants.inverse: Neutral emphasis: ink fill, inverse ink.

MeterKind.description: What a meter measures, which sets its colour.

x-og-variants.desktop: 1024 CSS px wide or more, the shorter side 600 or more.
x-og-variants.tablet: The shorter side 600 or more, under 1024 wide.
x-og-variants.phoneLandscape: The shorter side under 600, wider than tall.
x-og-variants.phonePortrait: The shorter side under 600, taller than wide.

Contrast.description: The theme variant: high contrast remaps muted inks, fills and lines to the style's stronger ones and outlines every control (no new colour).

x-og-variants.standard: The style's palette as it is.

NavIntent.description: A focus-navigation intent, as the arrow keys, Tab, Enter, Space, Escape and a gamepad's d-pad, stick, A and B give.

x-og-variants.next: The next control in reading order (Tab).
x-og-variants.activate: Press the focused control (Enter, Space, A).
x-og-variants.back: Leave: the topmost dialog or menu closes, else og.ui.back() answers true (Escape, B).

UiRect.description: A rectangle of the play surface.

IconAtlasDesc.description: The icon atlas: a texture of equal cells in a grid, named in reading order, or an icon set cooked like a font (font).

font.description: An icon set from og.load.font (an `.ogt` of `type icons` naming SVGs, such as the UI kit's iconoir set): its icons are distance-field glyphs, crisp at any size and tinted by their ink, named by the set; texture, columns, rows and names are then not used.

names.description: Each cell's name, in reading order: og.ui.icon draws a cell by its name.

AnchorDesc.description: An anchored group: a layer at a point of the safe area, over the tree (HUD corners, a centred title, a bar of touch controls).

margin.description: The inset from the safe area's edges; null is the density's gutter.

direction.description: Which way it lays out its children.

align.description: Where children sit along the main axis.

radius.description: Corner radius.

width.description: Its width; null fits the content.

height.description: Its height; null fits the content.

over.description: Draw over dialogs and spotlights (a tutorial callout, a dragged item); the default draws under them.

frame.description: The style frame its background takes; null is the panel's.

instant.description: Shown settled the first time it is built: no style entrance or stagger, its controls answering at once. For the screen a game opens on while it is that: the web draws it behind the play gate, where an entrance would stay part-way until the tap.

TransitionDesc.description: How a transition moves, timed in ticks from the style's motion.

durationMs.description: How long entering and leaving take; 0 is motion.duration.base (240 ms).

distance.description: How far slides travel; 0 is space.xl.

instant.description: Shown at once the first time it is built (no entrance).

Presence.description: Where a transition or dialog is this tick.

visible.description: Build its content: shown, entering or leaving.

ModalDesc.description: A dialog: a scrim over everything and a centred panel. Focus moves in and stays while it is the topmost; Back and the backdrop dismiss it unless locked.

title.description: A title over the content; empty is none.

width.description: The panel's width; null is 420 CSS px, at most the surface less its gutters.

locked.description: Back and the backdrop do not dismiss it (a choice must be made).

ignoreBackdrop.description: A press on the backdrop does not dismiss it.

transition.description: How it enters and leaves; null is scale.

backdrop.description: The backdrop's fill; null is scrim.

bare.description: No panel: the content sits centred on the backdrop (full-screen menus, loading).

dismissed.description: Back or a press on the backdrop asked to close it: set your open flag false.

SpotlightDesc.description: A spotlight: the surface dimmed except a hole around a target.

padding.description: Room around the target; 0 is space.sm.

ListDesc.description: A virtualised list: only the rows in view (and one more each side) are built, fillers keep the scroll range of every row.

rowHeight.description: Every row's height; 0 is the density's row height.

height.description: Its height (it scrolls inside); null grows.

ListRange.description: The rows (or cells) to build this tick: first up to, not including, last.

ListResult.description: What happened in a list or grid this tick.

clicked.description: The row or cell pressed (or activated) this tick.

dropFrom.description: A drag and drop ended: the index it started on.

dropTo.description: And the index it was released over.

GridDesc.description: A virtualised grid of equal cells (inventories, level select), scrolling vertically.

cellWidth.description: A cell's width; 0 is 64 (never under the 44 px touch target). With columns set and a width other than fit, the cells share the grid's width instead, as wide as it allows (never under the touch target), and keep their height.

cellHeight.description: A cell's height; 0 is its width.

columns.description: Cells across, exactly, whatever the width: a fit grid is that many cells of cellWidth, any other the cells share; 0 is as many cells of cellWidth as fit.

width.description: Its width; null fits (exactly the columns when columns is set).
Its width; null fits (grows with fill).

label.description: What a screen reader calls the row of tabs (its accessible name), never drawn; empty is its id. A localised game passes its string table's.

ChoiceResult.description: A choice control's response and the chosen index after this tick's input.

response.description: What happened to it; changed when the choice moved.

selected.description: The chosen index, to keep in game state and pass back next tick.

SelectDesc.description: A select: a trigger that opens a menu of options.

label.description: What a screen reader calls it (its accessible name; the chosen option is its value), never drawn; empty is its id. A localised game passes its string table's.

StepperDesc.description: A number stepper's range, step and digits.

min.description: The smallest value; min equal to max (the zero value) is unbounded.

step.description: How much a press changes it; 0 is 1.

StepperResult.description: A stepper's response and value after this tick's input.

value.description: The value, to keep in game state and pass back next tick.

RadioDesc.description: How a radio group lays out, and its name.

horizontal.description: Options in a row (the default is a column).

label.description: What a screen reader calls the group (its accessible name), never drawn; empty is its id. A localised game passes its string table's.

CheckListResult.description: A checkbox list's response and values after this tick's input.

response.description: What happened to it; changed when any box flipped.

values.description: The values, to keep in game state and pass back next tick.

tone.description: Its tone: a dot of the tone's colour before the text.

durationMs.description: How long it stays; 0 is 3200 ms (6000 for danger).

MeterDesc.description: A meter: a track with a fill that animates its changes by the tick.

kind.description: What it measures, which sets its colour.

color.description: A colour of your own instead of the kind's.

label.description: Text inside the bar (such as `75 / 100`); empty is none.

height.description: Its height; 0 is space.md, or the caption's line with a label.

segments.description: Notches dividing it into this many parts; 0 or 1 is none.

CooldownDesc.description: A cooldown ring's size and centre.

size.description: Its diameter; 0 is 56 (never under 44).

label.description: Text in the middle (a key, seconds left); empty is none.

icon.description: An icon of the atlas in the middle, by name; empty is none.

IconDesc.description: An icon's size, ink and name.

size.description: Its size; 0 is 24.

label.description: What a screen reader calls it (and the probe's text): null is the icon's name in the atlas (an English word: `star`); empty is decoration, named by nothing, so a card or button it sits on is named by its other text. A localised game names a meaningful icon from its string table.

tone.description: Its colour; neutral is the stage ink.

player.description: The player: the primary, larger, ringed.

texture.description: The map; null is the stage colour.

uv.description: The region of the map shown, [u0, v0, u1, v1]; null is the whole texture.

size.description: Its side; 0 is 160.

label.description: A zone name under it; empty is none.

DialogueDesc.description: A dialogue box: a portrait slot, the speaker and the line typed out by the tick.

text.description: The line. A new text starts typing again.

portrait.description: A portrait texture; null is the speaker's initial.

portraitUv.description: The portrait's region of the texture; null is the whole texture.

portraitIcon.description: A portrait from the icon atlas by name, when no texture is given; empty is the speaker's initial.

DialogueResult.description: A dialogue box's answer this tick.

advanced.description: Pressed (or activated) while done: show the next line.

size.description: The base's diameter; 0 is 128 (never under three touch targets).

x.description: -1 left to 1 right; 0 inside the dead zone.

y.description: -1 up to 1 down; 0 inside the dead zone.

active.description: A press that started on it is held.

size.description: The pad's size; 0 is 132 (each arm at least 44).

DpadResult.description: Which arms of a d-pad are held this tick.

ActionButtonDesc.description: A square touch action button (jump, fire), cornered by the style's control radius.

size.description: Its side; 0 is 64 (never under 44).

icon.description: An icon of the atlas by name, instead of the label; empty is the label.

SkeletonDesc.description: A skeleton: the neutral fill standing in for content that is loading.

height.description: A line's height; 0 is the body size.

lines.description: Stacked lines; 0 or 1 is one, the last of several is shorter.

A11yNode.description: One node of the accessibility tree: an element with a role (layout containers and spacers have none and are left out).

path.description: Its path, as touch_move_to and og.ui.focus name it.

parent.description: The path of the nearest node above it in the tree; empty at the top.

role.description: Its role (probe.UiElement.role): button, link, text, heading, image, checkbox, radio, switch, slider, spinbutton, textbox, combobox, listbox, option, tab, tablist, radiogroup, progressbar, meter, timer, status, dialog, tooltip, separator, group.

name.description: Its accessible name: what a screen reader says it is. A text field or area is named by the label before it in its row, else by its placeholder, else by its id; never by the text in it (that is its value).

description.description: Read after the name (aria-description): a text field's placeholder when a label names it; empty for none.

value.description: Its value as text (a slider's number, a progress's percent, a field's text); empty for none.

states.description: Its states: disabled, focused, focusable, checked, selected, expanded, pressed, busy, offscreen (a scroll container cuts it out of view).

valueMin.description: A range's smallest value (aria-valuemin): a slider's min, a bounded stepper's, 0 for a progress (in percent) and a meter; null for a stepper without bounds and a control that is no range.

valueMax.description: A range's largest value (aria-valuemax): a slider's max, a bounded stepper's, 100 for a progress, a meter's max; null as valueMin is.

valueNow.description: A range's value as a number (aria-valuenow; value says it as people read it): a slider's, a stepper's, a meter's, a progress's percent; null for a control that is no range.

x.description: Left edge of the whole element.

y.description: Top edge of the whole element.

A11yTree.description: The last frame's accessibility tree, built from the same nodes the UI draws and takes input on.

nodes.description: The nodes, in tree order: the page, then each layer over it (a dialog after the page).

focusOrder.description: The paths keyboard Tab and the pads visit, in order: the nodes marked focusable, within the topmost dialog while one is open.

focused.description: The path keyboard and pad 0's focus is on; empty for none.

CounterDesc.description: A number that counts to its value.

step.description: The type step; null is body.

font.description: Which font: mono (the numeric role) for counts in a row, display for a big score.

align.description: How it aligns in its width.

width.description: Its width; null fits the text.

durationMs.description: How long a change takes to count; 0 is 900 ms.

from.description: Where the first count starts; null starts at the value (no count).

BurstDesc.description: Rays and sparks thrown from an element.

color.description: Their ink; null is the primary.

radius.description: How far they fly from the element's centre; 0 is 1.4 times its size.

durationMs.description: How long they fly; 0 is motion.duration.slow plus base.

delayMs.description: Wait this long after the element first appears.

ShakeDesc.description: A shake of an element: three sideways swings decaying to rest.

amount.description: The first swing; 0 is the style's motion.shake, else 6.

durationMs.description: How long it takes to come to rest; 0 is motion.duration.slow.

sound.description: Also play the style's error sound, as a refused press does.

ScreenWipe.description: How a screen transition covers the old screen and reveals the new one.

x-og-variants.fade: The cover fades in and out.
x-og-variants.iris: A circle closes on the centre and opens again.
x-og-variants.dissolve: Cells appear in a fixed scattered order.
x-og-variants.slide: A sheet slides over and away.

WipeSide.description: Where a wipe or a slide comes from.

durationMs.description: Cover and reveal together; 0 is twice motion.duration.slow.

color.description: The cover's colour (the texture's tint); null is backdrop.

texture.description: A texture stretched over the surface as the cover; null is the flat colour.

from.description: Where a wipe or a slide comes from.

ScreenTransitionResult.description: Where a screen transition is this tick.

shown.description: The screen to build this tick: the old one until the cover closes, then the new one.

covering.description: The cover is closing over the old screen.

revealing.description: The cover is opening on the new screen.

cover.description: How much of the surface is covered, 0 to 1.

MenuItem.description: An item of a menu: an id the game acts on and the label a player reads.

id.description: The id answered when it is chosen; also its probe id.

MenuResult.description: What a menu-like template answered this tick.

selected.description: The id of the item chosen this tick.

MainMenuDesc.description: A title screen: the title, a subtitle, a column of items (the first primary unless one says so) and a footer. Centred on desktop and tablet, bottom-weighted on a phone.

title.description: The game's title, in display type.

subtitle.description: A line under it; empty is none.

items.description: The items, such as Play, Continue, Settings, Quit.

footer.description: A line at the bottom (a version, credits); empty is none.

onSelect.description: Called with the chosen item's id.

instant.description: Shown settled the first time it is built (AnchorDesc.instant): pass it while the title is the screen the game opens on, so the frame behind the web's play gate is the whole title; a title the player comes back to enters with the style.

PauseMenuDesc.description: A pause screen: a dialog over the frozen game with Resume first. Back resumes.

items.description: The items; empty is Resume, Settings, Quit to menu (`resume`, `settings`, `quit`).

onSelect.description: Called with the chosen item's id; Back answers `resume`.

KeyBinding.description: A control the settings screen lists: an action and the key bound to it.

LanguageOption.description: A language the settings screen offers, in its own name.

label.description: Its name in itself (`English`, `简体中文`).

GameSettings.description: The settings most games share. The game keeps them (a resource, a save) and passes them in every tick.

reducedMotion.description: Keep state changes, drop movement (the UI's transitions only fade).

vibration.description: Vibrate on hits (where the device can).

bindings.description: The controls, as shown on the Controls tab.

SettingsDesc.description: A settings screen: Audio, Graphics, Controls and Language tabs (a select on a phone) over the game's settings, with persistence hooks.

languages.description: The languages offered; empty hides the Language tab.

onChange.description: Called on every change (apply it at once: volume, contrast).

onSave.description: Called when the screen closes after changes (persist here).

world.description: The world the graphics preset is drawn in: when the player picks another preset the screen calls og.render.applyQuality(world, preset) before onChange. Null leaves applying it to the game. Inside a system, the system declares RenderSettings among its writes.

title.description: The dialog's title. Every word of the screen is a field with its English default: a localised game passes its string table's (og.i18n.t).

qualityLabel.description: The graphics preset's heading, also the presets' group's accessible name.

doneLabel.description: The button that closes the screen.

sectionLabel.description: What a screen reader calls the row of tabs (the select on a phone): the group's accessible name, never drawn.

languagesLabel.description: What a screen reader calls the list of languages: the group's accessible name, never drawn.

SettingsResult.description: The settings screen's answer this tick.

settings.description: The settings after this tick's input: keep them.

closed.description: The player closed the screen (Back, Done): set open false.

Ability.description: An ability on a HUD: a cooldown ring with its key.

key.description: The key or button shown in the middle.

icon.description: An icon of the atlas instead of the key; empty is the key.

remaining.description: How much of its cooldown is left: 1 just used, 0 ready.

PlatformerHudDesc.description: A platformer HUD: lives as hearts and a level name top left, coins and score top right, a timer, a pause button. What a game leaves out it does not draw: no hearts with maxLives 0 (and no health), no coins or score capsule without coins or score.

maxLives.description: Lives at most (hearts drawn); 0 draws no hearts and no capsule for them (a game without lives).

coins.description: Coins collected; null or left out draws no coins capsule.

score.description: The score; null or left out draws no score capsule.

level.description: The level's name; empty is none.

timeLeft.description: Seconds left; null hides the timer.

health.description: A health bar instead of hearts, 0 to 1; null shows hearts.

touch.description: Show touch controls (a d-pad and Jump) on phones and tablets.

jumpLabel.description: The touch Jump button. Every word of the HUD is a field with its English default: a localised game passes its string table's (og.i18n.t).

pauseLabel.description: The pause button's name (what a screen reader says; the button shows its icon).

HudResult.description: What a HUD answered this tick.

paused.description: The pause button was pressed (or Back).

action.description: A HUD action pressed this tick (an ability's id, `jump`, a generator's `buy:<id>`, `tap`).

moveX.description: The touch controls' horizontal input, -1 to 1.

moveY.description: The touch controls' vertical input, -1 (up) to 1.

held.description: The touch action buttons held this tick.

ShooterHudDesc.description: A shooter HUD: health and armor bottom left, ammo bottom right, abilities as cooldown rings, kills top right, a crosshair, an optional mini-map.

crosshair.description: Draw a crosshair at the centre.

map.description: A mini-map top left; null is none.

touch.description: Show touch controls (a stick and Fire) on phones and tablets.

killsLabel.description: The word after the kill count. Every word of the HUD is a field with its English default: a localised game passes its string table's (og.i18n.t).

pauseLabel.description: The pause button's name (what a screen reader says; the button shows its icon).

PuzzleHudDesc.description: A puzzle HUD: level and moves, the score towards a target with three star marks, an optional timer.

stars.description: The scores for one, two and three stars; empty is a third, two thirds and all of the target.

movesLabel.description: The caption under the moves left. Every word of the HUD is a field with its English default: a localised game passes its string table's (og.i18n.t).

targetLabel.description: The line beside the stars; `{target}` is replaced by the target, formatted (1,000). A localised game passes its string table's, with `{target}` in it.

pauseLabel.description: The pause button's name (what a screen reader says; the button shows its icon).

Currency.description: A currency an idle game counts.

perSecond.description: How much it earns per second.

icon.description: An icon of the atlas; empty is none.

Generator.description: A generator an idle game lists: level, cost, progress.

affordable.description: The player can pay for it.

icon.description: An icon of the atlas; empty is none.

IdleHudDesc.description: An idle or incremental HUD: currencies with their rates on top, a big tap target, the generators in a list.

currencies.description: The currencies, the first the main one.

tapLabel.description: The tap target's label; empty hides it.

levelLabel.description: A generator's level badge; `{level}` is replaced by its level. Every word of the HUD is a field with its English default: a localised game passes its string table's (og.i18n.t), with `{level}` in it.

rateLabel.description: A currency's rate; `{rate}` is replaced by its per-second amount, formatted (+12/s is `+{rate}/s`). A localised game passes its string table's, with `{rate}` in it.

pauseLabel.description: The pause button's name (what a screen reader says; the button shows its icon).

RaceSplit.description: One split of a racing HUD: a sector's time and its delta against the reference (the record's split).

label.description: Its name (`S1`, a sector's), the game's own word.

time.description: Its time in seconds, shown as m:ss.mmm; null is not yet run (a dash).

delta.description: Against the reference in seconds, shown signed (`-0.412`, `+1.050`, with the ASCII minus every pack draws): negative is ahead, in success ink; positive behind, in danger ink; null shows none.

RacingHudDesc.description: A racing HUD: position and lap top left, the times top right (the race time, a live delta, the best, the splits), the speedometer and gear bottom right, the boost meter, an optional mini-map. A time trial sets racers 0 (no place) and boostMeter false (no meter), and shows its sectors as splits.

racers.description: Cars in the race; 0 hides the place (a time trial).

delta.description: A live delta in seconds against the reference lap, under the time, signed like a split's: negative (ahead) in success ink, positive in danger ink; null hides it.

best.description: The best lap in seconds; null hides it.

splits.description: Splits under the times (a time trial's sectors), one row each: label, time, delta; empty is none.

boostMeter.description: Draw the boost meter and the touch Boost pedal; a race without boost (a time trial) sets false.

touch.description: Show touch controls (steering arrows, Brake, Boost) on phones and tablets.

lapLabel.description: The caption under the lap. Every word of the HUD is a field with its English default (unit too): a localised game passes its string table's (og.i18n.t).

bestLabel.description: The best lap's line; `{best}` is replaced by the best lap as m:ss.mmm. A localised game passes its string table's, with `{best}` in it.

pauseLabel.description: The pause button's name (what a screen reader says; the button shows its icon).

boostLabel.description: The boost meter's label and the touch Boost pedal.

portrait.description: An icon of the atlas as the portrait; empty is the speaker's initial.

CutsceneDesc.description: A dialogue scene: letterbox bars, the dialogue box at the bottom, Skip at the top right.

index.description: The line shown, from game state.

skipLabel.description: The Skip button. Every word of the cutscene is a field with its English default: a localised game passes its string table's (og.i18n.t).

index.description: The line to show next tick: keep it.

finished.description: The last line was advanced past.

price.description: Its price in the shop's currency.

icon.description: An icon of the atlas; empty is none.

category.description: Its category tab; empty is the first.

owned.description: Already owned (one-off items): shown, not for sale.

ShopDesc.description: A shop: the balance, category tabs, a grid of items with prices, a detail panel with Buy (disabled when the balance is short).

currencyIcon.description: The currency's icon; empty is none.

categories.description: Category tabs; empty is one list.

onBuy.description: Called with the bought item's id.

priceLabel.description: The detail panel's price line. Every word of the shop is a field with its English default (title and currency too): a localised game passes its string table's (og.i18n.t).

shortLabel.description: The Buy button while the balance is short of the price.

ownedLabel.description: An owned item's badge and button.

emptyLabel.description: The detail panel when the category has no items.

bought.description: The item bought this tick: take the price and grant it.

refused.description: The item whose Buy was pressed this tick while the balance was short: the button shook with the error sound (og.ui.shake) and nothing was bought.

count.description: How many (stacks); 0 or 1 hides the count.

icon.description: An icon of the atlas; empty is its initial.

InventoryDesc.description: An inventory: a grid of slots, items dragged between them, a detail panel with Use.

useLabel.description: The detail panel's action; empty hides it. Every word of the inventory is a field with its English default (title too): a localised game passes its string table's (og.i18n.t).

hintLabel.description: The detail panel while no slot is selected.
hintLabel.default: Select an item. Drag it to another slot to move it.

countLabel.description: The detail panel's count line, beside a stacked item's count.

SlotMove.description: An item dragged from one slot to another.

to.description: The slot it was dropped on (swap when that slot holds an item).

moved.description: A drag and drop this tick: move (or swap) the items.

used.description: The id of the item Use was pressed for.

LevelInfo.description: A level in a level select.

locked.description: Not yet reachable: a lock, inert.

best.description: The best result as shown; empty is none.

LevelSelectDesc.description: A level select: a grid of level cards with stars and locks, the total stars, and a Back button. Back closes it from every input: the button, a press on the scrim around it, Escape and the pad's B.

title.description: Its title. Every word of the screen is a field with its English default: a localised game passes its string table's (og.i18n.t).

starsLabel.description: What a screen reader says for a card's stars (and the total's): `{stars}` is replaced by the stars earned, `{max}` by the most there are. The stars themselves are drawn, never this text.

lockedLabel.description: What a screen reader calls a locked card (it shows only a lock): `{name}` is replaced by the level's name or number.

LevelSelectResult.description: A level select's answer this tick.

closed.description: The player asked to close it: its Back button, a press on the scrim, Escape or the pad's B.

StatRow.description: A labelled value on a results screen.

ScoreFormat.description: How a results screen shows its score and best.

x-og-variants.points: A whole number grouped with commas (12,840), counted up from 0; the best is the higher.
x-og-variants.time: Seconds as m:ss.mmm (1:36.233), counted up from 0:00.000: a time trial's result. Lower is better: the best is the lower, and a best of 0 is none (no best line).

ResultsDesc.description: A results screen: the title, stars that land one by one, the score counting up (points, or a time with `format` time) under its label, the best (a badge for a new best), stats, actions and a share hook.

score.description: The score: points, or seconds with `format` time.

best.description: The best score: points, or seconds with `format` time (0 is none).

format.description: How the score and best are shown: points (the default) or a time.

scoreLabel.description: A caption over the score (`Total time`, `Score`); empty is none. A localised game passes its string table's.

actions.description: The actions; empty is Retry, Next and Menu (`retry`, `next`, `menu`).

shareText.description: Text a share would post; empty hides Share.

onShare.description: Called with the share text when Share is pressed (the shell posts it).

bestLabel.description: The best score's line; `{best}` is replaced by the best score, formatted as the score is (m:ss.mmm with `format` time). A localised game passes its string table's (og.i18n.t), with `{best}` in it.

newBestLabel.description: The badge a new best shows.

LeaderboardDesc.description: A leaderboard: scope tabs, a virtualised list of ranks (medal colours for 1 to 3, the player highlighted), and honest loading, error and empty states.

scopes.description: Scope tabs (Today, This week, All time); empty is none.

error.description: Loading failed: this message and Retry.

empty.description: Shown when there are no rows.

retryLabel.description: The button under an error. Every word of the leaderboard is a field with its English default (title and empty too; error and scopes are the game's): a localised game passes its string table's (og.i18n.t).

scope.description: The scope tab chosen: keep it and load its rows.

TutorialStep.description: A step of a tutorial: the element to point at, a title and a line.

target.description: The element's id or path (as touch_move_to takes); empty points at nothing.

TutorialDesc.description: An onboarding overlay: a spotlight on each step's target, a callout beside it with Next and Skip, and the step count.

index.description: The step shown, from game state.

skipLabel.description: The Skip button. Every word of the overlay is a field with its English default: a localised game passes its string table's (og.i18n.t).

nextLabel.description: The button that shows the next step.

doneLabel.description: That button on the last step.

stepLabel.description: The step count; `{step}` is replaced by the step's number from 1 and `{count}` by the number of steps. A localised game passes its string table's, with both in it.

index.description: The step to show next tick: keep it.

finished.description: The last step's Done was pressed.

LoadingDesc.description: A loading screen: the title, a real progress bar (or a spinner while unknown) and tips that change by the tick.

progress.description: How far, 0 to 1; null is unknown (a spinner, never a fake bar).

ConfirmDesc.description: A confirm dialog: a title, a consequence sentence, Cancel and the action.

message.description: What will happen, as rich text markup (og.ui.richText: [b], [color=…], [icon=…]…), so a translation carries its own emphasis.

danger.description: The action destroys something: the danger button.

ConfirmResult.description: A confirm dialog's answer this tick.

AlertDesc.description: An alert: a title, a message and one button.

message.description: The message, as rich text markup (og.ui.richText).

CoreAction.description: The actions the engine ships. Arguments follow the action, separated by `:`.

x-og-variants.screenshot: `screenshot[:path][:full|:N]`: capture the next frame. Without a renderer it writes nothing and logs, not as a warning, that the frame is unchecked.
x-og-variants.listen: `listen[:path][:seconds]`: write the last seconds of rendered audio as a WAV.
x-og-variants.touch_move_to: `touch_move_to:<ui id>`: move the pointer to a UI element.
x-og-variants.touch_move: `touch_move:x,y`: move the pointer to CSS pixel coordinates.
x-og-variants.touch_start: `touch_start`: press the pointer where it is.
x-og-variants.touch: `touch:<id>:<down|move|up>:<x,y | ui id>`: a further touch (pointer 1 to 4) held while the pointer is busy elsewhere.
x-og-variants.gamepad: `gamepad:<a+b+...|->[@pad][:lx,ly[,rx,ry]][:lt,rt]`: set a pad's whole state (pad 0 unless `@1` to `@3` follows the buttons); `gamepad:off` disconnects it.
x-og-variants.key_down: `key_down:[Mod+]<Key>`: hold a key by its code, with the modifiers named before it (`Shift+ArrowLeft`, `Meta+ArrowLeft` for Command, apart from Ctrl).
x-og-variants.key_up: `key_up:[Mod+]<Key>`: release a key, then the modifiers named before it.
x-og-variants.type: `type:<text>`: type text, two ticks per character: its key press and the character as typed text (input.TextInput); a character no key types is typed text alone. The text runs to the `;` exactly, a trailing space included; after it a text field takes typed text only, so a bare key_down types nothing.
x-og-variants.compose: `compose:<text>`: an input method's composition so far (input.TextInput composing); a focused text field shows it underlined at the caret, `compose:` with nothing ends it.
x-og-variants.commit: `commit:<text>`: an input method commits text; a focused text field inserts it and the composition ends.
x-og-variants.move_to_text: `move_to_text:[=]text[@N]`: move the pointer to the UI element showing the text (exactly with `=`, the Nth with `@N`).
x-og-variants.frame_entity: `frame_entity:<entity>`: point the camera at an entity.
x-og-variants.dump_world: `dump_world[:path]`: tables, systems and their matched counts.
x-og-variants.dump_ui: `dump_ui[:path]`: the UI tree with bounds, and `style`, the configured UI style's name (empty for the placeholder prototype).
x-og-variants.set: `set:<entity>.<component>.<field>=<value>` or `set:<Resource>.<field>=<value>`: a Tune write through the schema: a number, `true` or `false` for a bool, `x,y,z` for a vector, an enum's variant name or its index; refused outside the field's FieldOptions min/max, never clamped.
x-og-variants.get: `get:<Resource>[.<field>]` or `get:<entity>[.<component>[.<field>]][:path]`: read through the schema as game code sees it (an enum as its variant's name, `"music"`; og.Time whole, with rate and the time scale; the DirectionalLight og.DayNight drives with the colour, intensity and direction it is drawn with), logged and written as JSON to `get-<tick>.json` (more unnamed ones on one tick: `get-<tick>-2.json`, ...).
x-og-variants.pause: `pause`: hold the clock; advance still steps.
x-og-variants.describe: `describe[:path]`: write the frame as data (probe.Description): the visible entities with screen boxes, depth order and occlusion from the entity-id pass, what each secondary camera (og.CameraView, og.Mirror) shows from its own pass, the UI elements with rects and text, the camera.
x-og-variants.expect: `expect:<what>`: assert at this tick (probe.ExpectResult): `entity:<id>:within:x,y,w,h` (its visible box, CSS pixels) or `:within:x0,y0,z0,x1,y1,z1` (its position, world units), `event:<Name>[:count]`, `ui:text:[=]<text>`, `region:x,y,w,h:color:#rrggbb[:tolerance]`, `frame:<ref.png>:rmse:<=v`, `state:<path>==<value>` (also != < <= > >=), `entity:<id>:<path>==<value>` (a field of its dump_entity: `render.lod==2`, `og.Transform.position.y>0`), `timings:<path>==<value>` (state().timings: `triangles<=1500000`). A failure is a warning with the tick and the observed value; `og run --json` lists every result and exits 1 on a failure. Frame expectations without a renderer are unchecked, as are an entity's `render.*` fields and the renderer's timings (`triangles`, `render`, `passes`).
x-og-variants.save_scene: `save_scene[:path][:spawned]`: write every scene the world was assembled from back from the world (the boot scene's, then each og.world.instantiate made, each to its own `.ogt`): only the lines whose values changed (comments and order kept), the fields set or patch tuned, and resources as `resource <Name> { }` blocks; with `spawned`, the entities the game spawned at run time under the boot scene's marked section. To each scene's source, or with a path the boot scene's to that file under the output directory and the others beside it.
x-og-variants.help: `help`: list every action the channel knows, core and registered.

doc.description: One sentence on what it does.

CommandStep.description: One parsed step of a command script.

at.description: When it runs, in simulation seconds from the start of the script.

CommandInfo.description: One action as help lists it.

doc.description: One sentence on what it does.

core.description: Shipped with the engine (true) or registered by a module or a game.

untilTick.description: The tick of the last step.

warnings.description: Unknown actions and other skipped steps, each naming the fix.

PickResult.description: What a screen point resolved to.

entity.description: The probe id of the entity under the point.

world.description: Where the pick landed in world space: two components in the 2D profile, three in 3D; nothing pads a plane with an unmeasured zero.

source.description: Where a person would change it, as `player.ts::jump`.

ProbeTunable.description: One published tunable parameter and the range it means something over.

ProbeEntityRef.description: One entity the probe publishes in state().

ProbeTimings.description: The fixed timings head of state().

render.description: Time the last frame's render took; 0 without a renderer.

systems.description: The last tick's systems in run order, each with its milliseconds.

passes.description: The last rendered frame's render passes in the render graph's order, each with its milliseconds of CPU encoding (empty without a renderer).

gpuPasses.description: The render passes of the newest frame the GPU's timestamps were read back for (a frame or two behind `passes`), each with the GPU's milliseconds from the end of the pass before it to its own end; empty where the device has no timestamp queries (RenderCapabilities.gpuTimestamps) or without a renderer.

triangles.description: Triangles the last frame's main pass drew (after culling and level of detail); 0 without a renderer.

ProbeTiming.description: One named span of the last tick or frame.

name.description: A system's name, or a render pass's (`Main`, `Cascade0`, `Bloom`).

ProbeState.description: The probe's state(): a fixed head, then the game's own facts.

tick.description: Fixed steps since load.

seed.description: The seed the world was assembled from.

what.description: The expectation, as after `expect:` in a script, such as `state:started==true`.

ProbeOperation.description: One operation of a probe program, which runs in one evaluation so a scripted segment costs one round trip.

oneOf.description: Take fixed steps; answers the tick.
Read the state; answers `{ tick, state }`.
Pick a point; answers its result or null.
Read an entity's parameters; null is a refusal.
Evaluate an expectation; answers its ExpectResult, failed or not (a malformed one is a refusal).

what.description: The expectation, as after `expect:` in a script, such as `state:started==true`.

oneOf.description: Describe the frame; answers its Description.

ProbeProgramResult.description: What a program observed: one answer per operation that ran. A false, or entity's null, stops the program and `refused` names its index.

refused.description: The index of the refusing operation, or null.

tick.description: The tick after the last operation that ran.

Hello.description: The wire's hello: who is speaking.

members.description: The probe members this build serves.

modules.description: The engine modules this build carries beyond the core (`physics`, `audio`, `ui`, `cook`), so a client knows which members do something.

BuildProfile.description: The build configuration; publish builds keep only the player-facing probe members.

x-og-variants.dev: A development build: every member, the command channel, dumps.
x-og-variants.release: An optimised build with every member.
x-og-variants.publish: A published game: hello, tick, state, pick, entity, input and capture only.

tick.description: The tick the frame shows.

Heard.description: What the host's mixer rendered last: the audio up to the current tick.

tick.description: The tick it ends at.

rms.description: The root mean square of both channels.

ProbeHeap.description: The engine's allocator, counted (both hosts install a counting global allocator).

peak.description: The most bytes live at once since load.

ProbeStreamMemory.description: The streaming memory budget (og.stream.budget): what the admitted groups' assets take.

used.description: What the admitted groups take now.

peak.description: The most they took at once.

ProbeMemory.description: What the engine holds, in one shape on both hosts; a figure a host cannot read is null. A publish page, whose probe has no `memory`, answers the same from the engine Worker (`__runtime_probe__.memory()`, docs/web-export.md).

linear.description: The wasm linear memory's size, which the browser reserved for the engine and never takes back; null natively.

resident.description: The process's resident memory (Linux /proc/self/status, macOS task_info); null on the web, where a page cannot read its process's.

heap.description: The engine's allocator; null where the host counts nothing.

audio.description: The sound bank's samples in memory (decoded sounds and the resident chunks of streamed ones); null without audio.

id.description: The probe id of the entity.

values.description: The values to try, in order.

steps.description: Fixed steps to advance after each patch.

width.description: Capture width; 0 is the render target's.

height.description: Capture height; 0 is the render target's.

tick.description: The tick captured.

SweepResult.description: A sweep's frames, one per value.

tick.description: The tick the world was restored at.

ms.description: From bundle swap to restored world.

migrated.description: Fields carried across a layout change, as `Health.hp`.

dropped.description: Components or fields that no longer exist, dropped with their data.

warnings.description: Anything else worth reading, each naming the fix.

tick.description: The tick it was taken at.

hash.description: The world hash at that tick, hex: equal hashes mean equal worlds.

x-og-variants.world: Archetype tables, systems and their matched counts.
x-og-variants.desync: The first desync of a lockstep session (og.net): its tick, both hashes and the component-level diff of the two peers' snapshots.

id.description: The probe id, for an entity dump.

matched.description: Entities its queries match now; null for a system the host did not declare to the probe.

reads.description: What it declared it reads; null when undeclared.

writes.description: What it declared it writes; null when undeclared.

ms.description: Time it took on the last tick; null when not measured.

tick.description: The tick.

components.description: Each component's field values, by component name.

UiElement.description: One UI element with its bounds.

id.description: Its stable id, as the command channel targets it.

parent.description: Its parent's id; empty at the root.

disabled.description: A disabled control (its text is exempt from contrast rules, as WCAG exempts inactive controls).

clipped.description: Only part of it shows: a scroll container or the surface cuts it, and the bounds are the part that shows.

text.description: The text it shows, if any.

tick.description: The tick.

components.description: Each component's field values, by component name.

surface.description: The surface the bounds are on; null without a UI module.

desync.description: Whether a desync happened; false lists the ticks compared with each peer so far.

ScreenPoint.description: A point on the play surface.

order.description: Its depth order: 0 is the nearest.

camera.description: The camera; null without a scene.

entities.description: The entities the main camera shows, nearest first (each names the views that also show it).

castShadows.description: Cast the directional and local lights' shadows (it always receives them).

lodSpacing.description: The finest clipmap level's spacing (0: the terrain file's, or the samples' spacing).

lodRing.description: Quads per side of every clipmap level (0: the terrain file's, else 64; 16 to 256, rounded to a multiple of 4).

TerrainScatter.description: Scatters copies of a mesh (grass, flowers, stones) over a loaded terrain near the camera, where one of its layers shows: on a jittered grid fixed to the terrain, so each copy keeps its place, size and turn as the camera moves, every cell growing one with the probability of the layer's weight there (its control-map channel times its slope and altitude rules, over all the layers' weights). Copies keep their size and thin out (dithered) over the outer `fade` of `distance`. The renderer places them itself, a chunk of the grid at a time, once, and draws the chunks in range: copies cost about nothing per frame while the camera stays. They grow over the og.Terrain drawing the same data, placed as it is. Drawn only: no colliders, and the copies are not entities.

geometry.description: The mesh, its origin at its root.

layer.description: The terrain layer that places it, 0 to 3.

density.description: Copies per square metre where the layer's weight is 1.

distance.description: How far from the camera, along x and z, copies are placed.

fade.description: The outer part of `distance` over which copies thin out to nothing.

align.description: How far copies lean with the ground: 0 upright, 1 along its normal.

seed.description: Another seed places the copies elsewhere.

data.description: Its handle, for og.Terrain.data and this module's functions.

geometry.description: The height field registered with physics under this handle: the mesh of an og.Collider of shape SHAPE_HEIGHTFIELD.

size.description: Its extent along x and z, centred on its entity.

minHeight.description: The lowest point above its entity.

collision.description: Whether its terrain file asks for a collider (`collision`, default true).

seaLevel.description: A generated terrain's sea level (`generate { sea <m> }`) above its entity: place an og.Water there, the terrain's size; null without a sea.

origin.description: Where it stands: its og.Terrain entity's world position.

quaternion.description: How it is turned: its og.Terrain entity's world rotation (the zero value: along world x and z).

scale.description: How it is scaled: its og.Terrain entity's world scale.

height.description: The world y of the surface (the triangles drawn at the finest level and collided with) on the terrain's up axis through (x, z): straight down for a terrain turned only about y.

normal.description: The surface normal, smoothed between samples as the renderer shades it.

slope.description: The normal's angle from straight up.

inside.description: Whether the point is over the terrain (outside, the nearest edge answers).

TerrainBounds.description: A terrain's box in world space.

TerrainBrush.description: One runtime edit of a terrain (og.terrain.edit).

origin.description: Where the terrain stands: its og.Terrain entity's world position.

quaternion.description: How it is turned: its og.Terrain entity's world rotation.

scale.description: How it is scaled: its og.Terrain entity's world scale.

center.description: The brush's centre in world space; its y is flatten's target height.

radius.description: The brush's radius in world metres (across the terrain's surface).

strength.description: World metres at the centre (raise, lower), or how far to go, 0 to 1 (flatten, smooth, paint).

falloff.description: The outer part of the radius over which it fades to nothing (0: a hard edge, 1: fading from the centre).

samples.description: Height or control-map samples it touched.

TerrainLayerDesc.description: One material layer of a terrain: its look and the rules that place it. A layer shows where its control-map channel (1 without a map) times its slope band times its altitude band is high; the layers' weights are normalised.

tile.description: Metres per repeat of its textures.

triplanar.description: Sample by three projections blended by the normal (for cliffs).

normalStrength.description: How strongly its normal map bends the surface.

slopeMin.description: The flattest slope it shows on.

slopeFade.description: How far past its slopes it fades out.

altitudeMin.description: The lowest height above the terrain's origin it shows at.

altitudeFade.description: How far past its heights it fades out.

x-og-variants.unloaded: Not wanted; its assets draw and play their stand-ins.
x-og-variants.queued: Wanted, waiting for room in the memory budget.
x-og-variants.loading: Admitted: its pack is being read (its memory already counts).
x-og-variants.resident: Its assets are in place of their stand-ins.
x-og-variants.failed: Its pack could not be read, or it alone needs more than the budget (StreamStatus.reason says which).

StreamEvent.description: A group changed state: sent by og.stream at the start of the tick after the change.

state.description: Its new state: STREAM_UNLOADED, STREAM_QUEUED, STREAM_LOADING, STREAM_RESIDENT or STREAM_FAILED (StreamState's order).

wanted.description: Whether its trigger or a request wants it now.

requested.description: Whether og.stream.request asked for it (until og.stream.release).

priority.description: Higher loads first and is evicted last.

memory.description: What its assets take once loaded, in bytes.

reason.description: Why it is queued or failed; empty otherwise.

since.description: The tick of its last change.

loads.description: How many times it became resident.

kept.description: The bytes of its assets kept for the frame after it unloaded (counted in StreamBudget.used until let go); 0 otherwise.

StreamBudget.description: The streaming memory budget and every group.

budget.description: The bytes resident and loading groups may take.

used.description: The bytes they take now, with what unloaded groups keep for the frame.

kept.description: Of `used`, the bytes of assets kept for the frame after their group unloaded (an array a sprite still draws, the map the frame is lit by, ...).

peak.description: The most they ever took (never above the budget at the time).

Video.description: Cooked footage: its frames as a texture array, its sound (og.load.video).

texture.description: The texture that shows the frame its og.VideoPlayer is at (frame 0 until one plays it).

sound.description: Its sound track (og.load.sound's kind of handle, for an og.AudioSource); 0 when it has none or was cooked with `audio false`.

format.description: The frames' encoding on the GPU (`rgba8`, `bc7`, `astc4x4`, `etc2`).

bytes.description: Bytes its frames take on the GPU.

VideoPlayer.description: Plays a loaded video: VideoInfo.texture shows its current frame (frame n is the source at n / fps seconds), and when the entity has an og.AudioSource the og.video system sets its sound, playing, pitch and loop each tick so the sound plays in step: a seek or a restart starts the sound again at the new time on the next tick (AudioSource.startOffset). Each player has a texture of its own (written to `texture`): the first player of a video takes VideoInfo.texture, each further one a texture the og.video system makes for it over the same decoded frames (one frame of GPU memory each), so two players at different times show different frames. Show a player's `texture`, not VideoInfo.texture, once a video has more than one player.

time.description: Seconds into the video; written every tick, set it to seek.

speed.description: The playback rate: 1 as cooked, 0.5 half speed (the sound's pitch follows).

loop.description: Start again at 0 past the end; otherwise hold the last frame and set finished.

frame.description: Written: the frame shown, floor(time * fps).

finished.description: Written: a player without loop reached the end.

texture.description: Written: this player's texture (VideoInfo.texture for the video's first player, a texture of its own for each further one), for a material, sprite or UI image set up from the player. It keeps it while it lives.

DebugDrawDesc.description: How a debug shape looks and how long it lasts.

duration.description: How many ticks after this one it stays; 0 is this frame only (draw it every tick it should show).

rotation.description: The shape's rotation: a box's or a sphere's circles', the axes' frame.

Path.description: A path: its points, kind and arc-length table.

PathKind.description: How the points make the curve.

x-og-variants.catmullRom: Through every point, as three.js CatmullRomCurve3: tension scales the tangents (0.5 is Catmull-Rom).
x-og-variants.bezier: Cubic Bezier segments: anchor, two controls, anchor, ... (3n + 1 points open, 3n closed).

CurveDesc.description: What makes a path (three.js's Curve; PathDesc is og.nav's path query).

points.description: The points, in order: at least 2 (catmullRom, linear), 3n + 1 open or 3n closed (bezier).

closed.description: Join the last point to the first; t wraps.

kind.description: How the points make the curve.

tension.description: catmullRom's tangent scale, as three.js's tension.

up.description: A unit up perpendicular to the tangent: world +Y made perpendicular (world +Z where the path runs straight up or down).

PathNearest.description: The point of a path nearest another point.

distance.description: How far it is from the point asked about.

PathFollower.description: Moves the entity along a path at `speed`, by the engine's og.path system after the game's systems and before physics: og.Transform.position is the path's point at `distance` plus `offset` (in the path's frame with align, else in world axes). Advanced by scaled time (slow motion, hit stop). The distance is the component's own field, so a snapshot, a restore and the world hash carry it, and writing it moves the entity there.

path.description: The path (og.path.create or og.path.find); 0 does nothing.

speed.description: Metres per second along the path; negative goes backwards.

distance.description: How far along the path it is, from its start; written every tick, set it to place the entity.

loop.description: Wrap at the end (and the start, going backwards); otherwise stop there and set `finished`.

align.description: Turn og.Transform.quaternion to face along the tangent (local -Z forward, +Y the path's up).

offset.description: Added to the path's point: along the path's right, up and backward axes with align, else world x, y and z.

finished.description: Written: a path without loop reached its end.

TimelineAsset.description: A loaded timeline: its tracks, paths, sounds and clips.

Timeline.description: Plays a loaded timeline. Set `playing` (or call og.timeline.play) to run it from `time`; write `time` (or call og.timeline.seek) to jump; og.timeline.stop goes back to 0 and lets go of what it owns.

time.description: Where it is, in seconds; written every tick it plays, set it to seek.

speed.description: Playback rate: 1 as authored, 0.5 half speed (0 holds the time while playing).

loop.description: Start over at the end; otherwise stop playing there, hand the camera back and send og.TimelineEnded.

TimelineStarted.description: A timeline started playing from stopped or ended (not on a resume from pause, nor on a loop).

TimelineMarker.description: Playback passed a marker key (a seek over one does not send it).

TimelineEnded.description: A timeline without loop reached its duration and stopped playing.

TimelineTrackInfo.description: One track of a loaded timeline.

kind.description: camera, transform, animation, audio, music, caption, event, transition or marker.

target.description: The entity a transform or animation track drives, the path a rail rides, the entity a camera follows; empty otherwise.

markers.description: Its markers' names, in time order.

Lockstep.description: Lockstep's settings and this peer's place. The game sets enabled, players, inputDelay and hashEvery (the authority's are the room's once it starts: changes while running wait for the next start); the engine sets localPlayer and running. It is this peer's own: never hashed, never compared.

enabled.description: Whether the world takes its ticks in lockstep when in a room.

players.description: The seats: the peers lockstep waits for before it starts, and whose inputs each tick waits for.

localPlayer.description: This peer's seat, the og.PlayerInput.player its input drives; `players` while it watches (a peer beyond the seats). 0 before the start.

inputDelay.description: Ticks between a player's input and the tick it acts on: the time the input has to cross the room. 2 (33 ms at 60 Hz) on a LAN, 4 to 6 over the internet.

hashEvery.description: How often the peers exchange their world hashes, in ticks (every tick is hashed, so the first divergent tick is exact); 0 compares nothing.

running.description: Whether lockstep runs: the room filled the seats and the authority started (until this peer leaves the room or turns it off).

PlayerInput.description: One player's input for this tick, the same on every peer: the engine writes every field but `player` at the start of each tick from the seat's input (zero for a seat nobody holds, and before its holder's first input). Its packed bytes are what crosses the room, read through this layout.

player.description: The seat whose input this entity carries (0 to og.Lockstep.players - 1); the game sets it when it spawns the player.

buttons.description: The buttons held, one bit each, as the game numbers them (bit 0 fire, bit 1 dash, ...).

x.description: The move axis, left -1 to right 1.

y.description: The move axis, back -1 to forward 1.

aimX.description: A second axis (aim, a cursor's world x), as the game uses it.

aimY.description: A second axis (aim, a cursor's world y), as the game uses it.

tick.description: The tick these values are for: the tick now, once the engine wrote them.

Desync.description: This peer's world and another's differ: sent once, at the start of the tick after the hashes showed it. The probe's `desync` dump (`dump_desync`) names the component and field that differ, once the other peer's snapshot of that tick arrived.

tick.description: The first divergent tick: the world after it differs (og.Time.tick of the snapshots compared).

peer.description: The first peer whose world differs from this one.

peers.description: How many peers' worlds differ from this one.

InputDesc.description: This peer's player's input: og.PlayerInput's fields but `player` and `tick`.

buttons.description: The buttons held, one bit each.

LockstepSeat.description: One peer's hold on a seat.

peer.description: The peer that holds (or held) it.

since.description: The first tick of its input.

until.description: The last tick of its input, once it left.

LockstepStatus.description: Lockstep on this peer, as the probe and a HUD read it.

peer.description: This peer's number; null in no room.

startTick.description: The tick lockstep started (or this peer joined it) at.

spectators.description: The running peers without a seat.

waitingFor.description: The seats whose input for the next tick has not arrived.

waits.description: Tick boundaries this peer waited at for an input.

desync.description: The first divergent tick, once og.Desync was sent.
